  • --parquet-tools: Path to parquet-tools (default: each command's own default, parquet-tools)
  • --aws: Path to the AWS CLI (default: aws)
  • --R, --gzip, --sort, --python: Binaries on PATH (default: Rscript, gzip, sort, python3)

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Outputs depend on the enabled action flags. Refer to each module page for full output details and file formats.

  • --load-xenium-ranger: A Xenium assets JSON summarizing detected inputs (path: --xenium-ranger-assets). See the example in Xenium Add-ons.
  • --sge-convert: Unified SGE files and an assets manifest (sge_assets.json) under sge/. See sge_convert reference.
  • --run-ficture2: FICTURE analysis artifacts under ficture2/. See run_ficture2 reference.
  • --import-cells: Cell and boundary PMTiles and a cell assets JSON under cartload2/. See import_cell reference.
  • --import-images: Background image PMTiles (and intermediates) under cartload2/. See import_image reference.
  • --run-cartload2: PMTiles and a catalog.yaml under cartload2/. See run_cartload2 reference.
  • --upload-aws: Uploads the catalog-listed assets and catalog.yaml to --s3-dir.
  • --upload-zenodo: Uploads catalog.yaml and catalog-listed assets to Zenodo.

See also the example output in the Xenium end-to-end tutorial.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
SGE datasets vary widely in format and resolution across platforms. Since FICTURE requires SGE in a specific format, CartLoader provides the sge_convert module to standardize raw, platform-specific SGE into a FICTURE-compatible format (coordinates in µm).

Usually run for you

run_together calls sge_convert as its ingest stage, with per-platform settings. Use this page to run it directly in step-by-step or custom workflows.

Question

  • How do I define scaling (--units-per-um) for sge_convert?

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
The input (raw, platform‑specific SGE) must provide at least:

  • Spatial coordinates (X, Y)
  • Feature names (such as gene symbols)
  • Expression counts (optional for CSV/TSV input; each row counts as 1 when no count column is given)

Platform Compatibility

Source --platform Input flags 10x Visium HD 10x_visium_hd --in-mex and --pos-parquet (required); --scale-json (recommended) Seq-Scope seqscope --in-mex, or --in-csv (raw per-molecule TSV) Illumina StrataMap illumina --in-mex (coordinates are embedded in the barcodes) 10x Xenium 10x_xenium --in-csv or --in-parquet (not both) Stereo-seq bgi_stereoseq --in-csv CosMx SMI cosmx_smi --in-csv Vizgen MERSCOPE vizgen_merscope --in-csv Pixel-seq pixel_seq --in-csv Nova-ST nova_st --in-csv Generic CSV/TSV input 1 generic --in-csv

For 10x_xenium and 10x_visium_hd, --in-json can replace these flags (see Parameters).

1: For SGE from platforms not explicitly supported, or from custom/preprocessed sources. The default columns are X, Y, gene in a tab-delimited file; override them with the --csv-* options.

Pre-installed tools

  • gzip (or pigz).
  • spatula: required for every MEX conversion (10x_visium_hd, illumina, and seqscope with --in-mex) and for --sge-visual. Defaults to the repository submodule (<cartloader_dir>/submodules/spatula/bin/spatula).
  • Parquet input (--in-parquet, --pos-parquet): converted with cartloader parquet_to_csv_rapid (Python polars + pigz), or with parquet-tools when --use-parquet-tools is set.
  • --filter-by-density: the ficture Python package (installed with CartLoader), which provides ficture filter_by_density.
  • --north-up: gdal_translate and gdalwarp.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Action Specifications

SGE conversion always runs. --filter-by-density and --sge-visual are optional add-ons.

docs.title: SGE Conversion (always runs)
docs.text: Converts the input into a FICTURE-compatible transcript TSV, rescaling coordinates to µm (--units-per-um). Feature filters (lists or regexes) and, for 10x Xenium, a Phred quality filter are applied during conversion.

docs.title: Density-based Filtering (--filter-by-density)
docs.text: Identifies tissue regions from transcript density and spatial structure (ficture filter_by_density) and writes a filtered SGE alongside the unfiltered one. The filtered SGE then becomes the SGE recorded in sge_assets.json.

docs.title: SGE Visualization (--sge-visual)
docs.text: Draws a monochrome image of the transcript positions with spatula draw-xy. Add --north-up to also write a georeferenced, north-up GeoTIFF (Y increases northward, X eastward). With --filter-by-density, both the unfiltered and the filtered SGE are drawn.

docs.title: 1.1) Seq-Scope
docs.text:
cartloader sge_convert \
    --platform seqscope \
    --in-mex /path/to/input/mex/dir \
    --units-per-um 1000 \
    --icols-mtx 1 \
    --colname-count count \
    --out-dir /path/to/output/dir \
    --filter-by-density \
    --sge-visual \
    --north-up

For the raw per-molecule Seq-Scope TSV, pass --in-csv /path/to/raw.tsv.gz instead of --in-mex (no --units-per-um needed: the TSV route defaults to 1000).

docs.title: 1.2) 10x Visium HD
docs.text:
cartloader sge_convert \
    --platform 10x_visium_hd \
    --in-mex /path/to/binned_outputs/square_002um/filtered_feature_bc_matrix \
    --pos-parquet /path/to/binned_outputs/square_002um/spatial/tissue_positions.parquet \
    --scale-json /path/to/binned_outputs/square_002um/spatial/scalefactors_json.json \
    --exclude-feature-regex '^(BLANK|NegCon|NegPrb)' \
    --out-dir /path/to/output/dir \
    --sge-visual

docs.title: 1.3) Illumina StrataMap
docs.text:
cartloader sge_convert \
    --platform illumina \
    --in-mex /path/to/input/mex/dir \
    --out-dir /path/to/output/dir

The barcode delimiter (:), the coordinate fields (x = field 3, y = field 2) and --units-per-um (nanometer vs. micron barcodes) are set automatically.

docs.title: 2) Input SGE in TSV/CSV Format
docs.text:
This applies to every CSV/TSV platform. Below converts a Stereo-seq GEM file (500 nm bins, i.e. 2 units per µm; --csv-comment skips the # metadata lines at the top of the file):

cartloader sge_convert \
    --platform bgi_stereoseq \
    --in-csv /path/to/input.gem.gz \
    --csv-comment \
    --units-per-um 2 \
    --out-dir /path/to/output/dir \
    --exclude-feature-regex '^(mt-|Gm[0-9])' \
    --filter-by-density \
    --sge-visual \
    --north-up

Verify Your Input Structure

Always check the column names and delimiter of your input. If they differ from the platform defaults below, override them with the --csv-* options (and --min-phred-score for quality filtering).

Platform-specific Default Settings (CSV/TSV input)

Platform --csv-comment1 --csv-delim --csv-colname-x --csv-colname-y --csv-colname-count --csv-colname-feature-name 10x Xenium2 False , x_location y_location - feature_name Stereo-seq False \t x y ExonCount geneName CosMx SMI3 False , x_global_px y_global_px - target MERSCOPE False , global_x global_y - gene Pixel-seq False \t xcoord ycoord - geneName Nova-ST True \t x y MIDCount geneID Seq-Scope (--in-csv)4 False \t X Y gn gene Generic False \t X Y - gene

-: no count column; each row counts as 1. With a count column, rows whose count is 0 are dropped.

1 --csv-comment: if True, lines starting with # are skipped. Without it, a #-prefixed header line (e.g. the Seq-Scope TSV's #lane ...) is read as the header with the # stripped.

2 10x Xenium also defaults to --csv-colname-phredscore qv, --min-phred-score 20, and --exclude-feature-regex '^(BLANK|Blank-|Deprecated|Intergenic|NegCon|Unassigned)'.

3 CosMx global coordinates are in pixels, so set --units-per-um to pixels per µm. run_together ingests CosMx with reformat_cosmx instead.

4 The Seq-Scope TSV route also defaults to --units-per-um 1000 and --csv-colnames-positive lane tile X Y.

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Below are the core parameters. See more details in the collapsible sections below.

docs.title: SGE Conversion Parameters
docs.text:
• --platform (str, required): Source platform. Options: 10x_visium_hd, seqscope, illumina, 10x_xenium, bgi_stereoseq, cosmx_smi, vizgen_merscope, pixel_seq, nova_st, generic.
  • --out-dir (str, required): Output directory.
  • --in-mex (str): Input MEX directory (platforms: 10x_visium_hd, seqscope, illumina; default: current working directory).
  • --in-csv (str): Input CSV/TSV (CSV/TSV platforms; for seqscope it selects the raw per-molecule TSV route instead of --in-mex).
  • --in-parquet (str): Input transcript parquet (platform: 10x_xenium).
  • --pos-parquet (str): Position parquet with spatial coordinates (platform: 10x_visium_hd, required; typical: tissue_positions.parquet).
  • --scale-json (str): Scale JSON; sets --units-per-um to 1 / microns_per_pixel (platform: 10x_visium_hd; typical: scalefactors_json.json).
  • --in-json (str): Input manifest JSON whose SGE block names the inputs (as written by load_xenium_ranger / load_space_ranger). Replaces --in-csv/--in-parquet for 10x_xenium, and --in-mex/--pos-parquet/--scale-json for 10x_visium_hd (where it also sets --scale-xy 2).
  • --units-per-um (float): Coordinate units per µm in the input (default: 1). Platform defaults: 1000 for the Seq-Scope TSV route; for illumina it is detected from the barcode file (1000 for nanometer barcodes such as SBC:433503:2393851, 1 for micron barcodes such as SBC:686.951:4668.15), and an explicit value overrides the detection (a contradicting value is reported as a warning). For 10x_visium_hd, --scale-json takes precedence over this flag.

docs.title: Feature Filtering Parameters
docs.text:
• --include-feature-regex (regex): Keep only features whose name matches.
  • --exclude-feature-regex (regex): Drop features whose name matches (default for 10x_xenium: '^(BLANK|Blank-|Deprecated|Intergenic|NegCon|Unassigned)'; none for other platforms). Pass '' to disable the default.
  • --include-feature-list (str): File listing the feature names to keep (one per line).
  • --exclude-feature-list (str): File listing the feature names to drop (one per line).

Regexes use substring (search) semantics, so anchor them with ^/$ as needed. On the MEX platforms (10x_visium_hd, illumina, and seqscope with --in-mex), filtering runs inside spatula convert-sge, which accepts at most one include-type and one exclude-type filter: combining a list and a regex of the same polarity is an error there. Merge them into one list with cartloader feature_select. On the CSV/TSV platforms all four filters combine.

Auxiliary SGE Conversion Parameters

Recommend to use the default values; override only if needed. See more details by running: 

cartloader sge_convert --help

Auxiliary Input MEX Parameters (10x_visium_hd, seqscope, illumina):

  • --mex-bcd, --mex-ftr, --mex-mtx (str): File names of barcodes, features and matrix inside --in-mex (defaults: barcodes.tsv.gz, features.tsv.gz, matrix.mtx.gz).
  • --icols-mtx (int): 1-based index of the count column to use in the matrix file (default: 1).
  • --icol-ftr-id, --icol-ftr-name (int): 1-based columns of feature ID and name in the feature file (defaults: 1, 2).
  • --icol-bcd-barcode (int): 1-based column of the barcode in the barcode file (platform: seqscope; default: 1).
  • --icol-bcd-x, --icol-bcd-y (int): 1-based column (Seq-Scope) or barcode field (Illumina) holding X and Y (defaults: 6 and 7 for seqscope; 3 and 2 for illumina).
  • --bcd-delim (str): Delimiter splitting an Illumina barcode into fields (platform: illumina; default: :).
  • --pos-colname-barcode, --pos-colname-x, --pos-colname-y (str): Columns of --pos-parquet (platform: 10x_visium_hd; defaults: barcode, pxl_col_in_fullres, pxl_row_in_fullres).
  • --pos-delim (str): Delimiter of the converted position file (platform: 10x_visium_hd; default: ,).
  • --allow-duplicate-gene-names (flag): Allow duplicate gene names (platform: 10x_visium_hd).
  • --keep-mismatches (flag): Keep barcodes that did not match a spatial position (X = Y = 0); by default they are dropped by cartloader sge_drop_mismatches (platform: seqscope with --in-mex; for debugging).

Auxiliary Input CSV/TSV Parameters (defaults per platform: see the table above):

  • --csv-comment (flag): Skip lines starting with #.
  • --csv-delim (str): Delimiter of the input file.
  • --csv-colname-x, --csv-colname-y (str): Columns of X and Y coordinates.
  • --csv-colname-count (str): Column of the expression count. Without it, each row counts as 1.
  • --csv-colname-feature-name (str): Column of the gene name.
  • --csv-colnames-others (list): Additional columns to keep in the output (e.g., cell_id overlaps_nucleus).
  • --csv-colnames-positive (list): Columns that must be strictly positive; rows with a zero, negative or non-numeric value are dropped as malformed (default: lane tile X Y for the Seq-Scope TSV route).
  • --csv-colname-phredscore (str): Column of the Phred-scaled quality score (default: qv for 10x_xenium).
  • --min-phred-score (float): Minimum quality score to keep a transcript (default: 20 for 10x_xenium; no filtering for others).

Auxiliary Output Parameters:

  • --out-transcript (str): File name of the output transcript TSV (default: transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz).
  • --out-minmax (str): File name of the coordinate min/max TSV (default: coordinate_minmax.tsv).
  • --out-feature (str): File name of the per-gene count TSV (default: feature.clean.tsv.gz).
  • --out-json (str): Output JSON manifest of SGE paths (default: <out-dir>/sge_assets.json).
  • --precision-um (int): Decimal places for output coordinates; 0 rounds to integers (default: 2).
  • --colname-x, --colname-y (str): Output X/Y column names (defaults: X, Y).
  • --colname-count (str): Output count column name (default: count).
  • --colname-feature-name (str): Output gene column name (default: gene).
  • --jitter-xy (float): Maximum random jitter (µm) added to each coordinate (default: 0, off).

Environment Parameters:

  • --gzip (str): Path to gzip (default: gzip; e.g., "pigz -p 4" for speed).
  • --spatula (str): Path to spatula (default: <cartloader_dir>/submodules/spatula/bin/spatula).
  • --pigz (str), --pigz-threads (int): pigz binary and threads used for parquet conversion (defaults: pigz, 4).
  • --use-parquet-tools (flag): Convert parquet with parquet-tools instead of polars/pigz (may be slower for large files).
  • --parquet-tools (str): Path to parquet-tools (used only with --use-parquet-tools; default: parquet-tools).

Run Parameters:

  • --dry-run (flag): Write the Makefile and print the commands without executing.
  • --restart (flag): Ignore existing outputs and rerun all steps.
  • --makefn (str): Makefile name under --out-dir (default: sge_convert.mk).
  • --n-jobs, -j (int): Number of parallel jobs (default: 1).

docs.title: Density‑based Filtering Parameters
docs.text:
• --filter-by-density (flag): Enable density-based filtering.
  • --out-filtered-prefix (str): Prefix of the filtered outputs under --out-dir (default: filtered).
Auxiliary Density‑based Filtering Parameters

We recommend using default values; override only if needed.

  • --radius (int): Radius for the polygon area calculation (default: 15).
  • --quartile (int): Quartile for the polygon area calculation (default: 2).
  • --hex-n-move (int): Sliding step (default: 1).
  • --polygon-min-size (int): Minimum polygon size (default: 500).

docs.title: SGE Visualization Parameters
docs.text:
• --sge-visual (flag): Draw the SGE image.
  • --north-up (flag): Also write a north-up GeoTIFF (with --sge-visual).
Auxiliary SGE Visualization Parameters

We recommend using default values; override only if needed.

  • --out-xy (str): File name of the SGE image (default: xy.png; the filtered image is prefixed by --out-filtered-prefix).
  • --out-northup-tif (str): File name of the north-up image (default: xy_northup.tif).
  • --scale-xy (float): µm per pixel of the image (default: 1.0).
  • --srs (str): Spatial reference system (with --north-up; default: EPSG:3857).
  • --resample (str): Resampling method (with --north-up; e.g., near, bilinear, cubic; default: cubic).
  • --gdal_translate, --gdalwarp (str): Paths to the GDAL binaries (with --north-up; defaults: gdal_translate, gdalwarp).

docs.title: Output
docs.text: All outputs are written under --out-dir.

docs.title: Unified SGE matrix
docs.text:
SGE conversion writes:

transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz: transcript-indexed SGE in TSV 
X        Y        gene     count
295.29   1422.35  Myo3a    0
1745.54  1110.72  Med14    1
1745.54  1110.72  Ntpcr    1
  • X: X coordinates in um
  • Y: Y coordinates in um
  • gene: gene symbols
  • count: expression count per pixel per gene
feature.clean.tsv.gz: UMI counts on a per-gene basis in TSV 

gene           gene_id             count
Gm29155        ENSMUSG00000100764  1
Pcmtd1         ENSMUSG00000051285  431
Gm26901        ENSMUSG00000097797  1
* gene: gene symbols * gene_id: gene IDs * count: expression count per gene

coordinate_minmax.tsv: X Y min/max coordinates 
xmin    0.14
xmax    2359.90
ymin    0.23
ymax    1439.95
  • xmin xmax: min and max X coordinates in um
  • ymin ymax: min and max Y coordinates in um

With --filter-by-density, the filtered SGE uses fixed names (independent of --out-transcript/--out-feature/--out-minmax):

  • <prefix>.transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz, <prefix>.feature.lenient.tsv.gz, <prefix>.coordinate_minmax.tsv (<prefix> = --out-filtered-prefix)
  • tissue boundaries from ficture filter_by_density (<prefix>.boundary.lenient.geojson, <prefix>.boundary.strict.geojson, and PNG previews)

docs.title: SGE manifest (sge_assets.json)
docs.text:
sge_convert records the SGE to use downstream in sge_assets.json (or --out-json), written when the Makefile is generated:

{
  "transcript": "/path/to/out/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz",
  "feature": "/path/to/out/feature.clean.tsv.gz",
  "minmax": "/path/to/out/coordinate_minmax.tsv",
  "density_filtering": false,
  "visual": { "png": "/path/to/out/xy.png", "northup": false }
}
  • transcript, feature, minmax: the SGE files. With --filter-by-density they point to the filtered files and density_filtering is true.
  • visual (only with --sge-visual): the image (png is the north-up TIFF when --north-up is set, and the filtered image when filtering is enabled).

run_ficture2 --in-json reads this file directly.

docs.title: SGE Images
docs.text:
• --sge-visual: monochrome PNG of the SGE (xy.png, plus <prefix>.xy.png when filtered).
  • --north-up: georeferenced north-up GeoTIFF (xy_northup.tif, plus <prefix>.xy_northup.tif when filtered).

docs.title: Other files
docs.text:
• sge_convert.done (and sge_density_filtering.done): done flags used to skip completed steps on rerun.
  • sge_convert.mk: the generated Makefile.
  • transcripts.parquet.csv.gz: CSV converted from --in-parquet (10x Xenium only).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
sge_orientate rotates and flips an SGE to match the desired image orientation.

Not part of run_together

run_together does not reorient the SGE; sge_stitch calls sge_orientate for tiles that need it. Use this page to reorient an SGE directly in step-by-step or custom workflows.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: • Input SGE in the unified format (from SGE format conversion). The coordinate columns must be named X and Y (fixed; not configurable), and the min/max file must be the two-column xmin/xmax/ymin/ymax TSV.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text: Rotations are clockwise; flips are applied after rotation. The SGE is transformed within its own bounding box, so the coordinate range is preserved (with X and Y ranges swapped for 90°/270°).

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
Below is an example with 90 degree rotation and a horizontal flip.

OUT_PREFIX=r90_hflip                # Replace r90_hflip with your prefix
cartloader sge_orientate  \
    --in-transcript /path/to/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz \
    --in-feature  /path/to/feature.clean.tsv.gz \
    --in-minmax /path/to/coordinate_minmax.tsv \
    --out-transcript /path/to/${OUT_PREFIX}.transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz \
    --out-feature /path/to/${OUT_PREFIX}.feature.clean.tsv.gz \
    --out-minmax  /path/to/${OUT_PREFIX}.coordinate_minmax.tsv \
    --rotate 90 \
    --flip-horizontal

docs.title: Input/Output Parameters
docs.text:
All six are required.

  • --in-transcript (str): Input transcript SGE TSV (gzipped).
  • --in-feature (str): Input feature TSV (gzipped).
  • --in-minmax (str): Input coordinate min/max TSV.
  • --out-transcript (str): Output oriented transcript SGE TSV (gzipped).
  • --out-feature (str): Output feature TSV (an unchanged copy of the input).
  • --out-minmax (str): Output oriented min/max TSV.

docs.title: Key Parameters
docs.text:
• --rotate (90|180|270): Rotate clockwise (applied before flips). Omit for no rotation.
  • --flip-vertical (flag): Flip vertically (along the Y-axis; applied after rotation).
  • --flip-horizontal (flag): Flip horizontally (along the X-axis; applied after rotation).
  • --chunk-size (int): Rows per chunk when processing the transcript TSV (default: 1,000,000).

Equivalent combinations are normalized first (e.g. --rotate 180 is the same as both flips).

docs.title: Output
docs.text: The oriented transcript TSV and min/max TSV, plus a copy of the feature TSV, at the three --out-* paths.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
sge_stitch stitches two or more SGE tiles into a single SGE, with optional per-tile orientation. It can also run density-based filtering on the stitched SGE.

Not part of run_together

run_together does not stitch tiles. Use sge_stitch in step-by-step or custom workflows; its stitched transcript TSV can then be given to run_together as an already-ingested transcript (--in-transcript; see Transcript sources).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Input SGE tiles in the unified format (from SGE format conversion), with X and Y coordinate columns.
  • cartloader on the PATH (the generated Makefile calls cartloader sub-commands).
  • gzip; the ficture Python package (installed with CartLoader) for --filter-by-density.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
Define each input tile as a comma-separated tuple of paths and layout/orientation fields:

cartloader sge_stitch \
    --in-tiles \
        "/path/to/tileA/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz,/path/to/tileA/feature.clean.tsv.gz,/path/to/tileA/coordinate_minmax.tsv,0,0,,false,false" \
        "/path/to/tileB/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz,/path/to/tileB/feature.clean.tsv.gz,/path/to/tileB/coordinate_minmax.tsv,0,1,90,false,true" \
    --out-dir /path/to/output/dir \
    --units-per-um 1.0 \
    --precision 2

Tile A is placed as is (empty rotate field); tile B is rotated 90° clockwise, then flipped horizontally.

docs.title: SGE Stitch
docs.text:
• --in-tiles (list of str): One tuple per input tile (see below).
  • --out-dir (str, required): Output directory for the stitched (and filtered) SGE and the Makefile.

Input Tile Tuple Format

Each tuple has exactly eight comma-separated fields; quote each tuple: 

"transcript_path,feature_path,minmax_path,row,col,rotate,vertical_flip,horizontal_flip"

  • transcript_path (str): The tile's transcript-indexed SGE TSV (.tsv.gz).
  • feature_path (str, optional): The tile's per-gene count TSV. Leave empty (or None) to generate it with cartloader sge_supp.
  • minmax_path (str, optional): The tile's coordinate min/max TSV. Leave empty (or None) to generate it with cartloader sge_supp.
  • row, col (int): Grid position of the tile. Each grid cell is as wide as the widest tile in its column and as tall as the tallest tile in its row, and each tile is centered in its cell; col increases along X and row along Y. A (row, col) pair may be used only once.
  • rotate: Clockwise rotation, 90, 180, or 270; leave the field empty for no rotation (0 is not accepted).
  • vertical_flip, horizontal_flip: true/false (case-insensitive); flips are applied after rotation.

Generated feature/min-max files are written next to the tile's transcript file: <id>.feature.tsv.gz and <id>.minmax.tsv, where <id> is the transcript file name without .tsv.gz and .transcripts; or feature.clean.tsv.gz and coordinate_minmax.tsv when the transcript is named transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz.

Known issues

  • A tile whose orientation reduces to flips only — a flip without rotation, or 180 with or without a single flip — currently fails at its sge_orientate step. Pre-orient such tiles with sge_orientate and pass the result with an empty rotate field and both flips false.
  • --sge-visual currently fails while the Makefile is being generated; omit it.
Auxiliary SGE Stitching Parameters

We recommend using default values; override only if needed.

Auxiliary Output Parameters:

  • --out-transcript (str): Output transcript-indexed SGE under --out-dir (default: transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz).
  • --out-feature (str): Output per-gene count TSV under --out-dir (default: feature.clean.tsv.gz).
  • --out-minmax (str): Output coordinate min/max TSV under --out-dir (default: coordinate_minmax.tsv).
  • --out-tile-minmax (str): Output per-tile min/max and offset TSV under --out-dir (default: coordinate_minmax_per_tile.tsv).
  • --out-json (str): Output JSON manifest of the SGE (default: <out-dir>/sge_assets.json).

Auxiliary Colname Parameters:

  • --colname-count (str): Count column (default: count).
  • --colname-feature-name (str): Feature name column (default: gene).
  • --colname-feature-id (str): Feature ID column, if present (default: none).
  • --colname-x, --colname-y (str): X/Y columns (defaults: X, Y).
  • --colnames-others (list): Additional columns to keep.

Auxiliary Scale and Precision Parameters:

  • --units-per-um (float): Coordinate units per µm of the input tiles (default: 1.0). Tiles from sge_convert are already in µm; keep the default.
  • --precision (int): Decimal places of the stitched coordinates (default: 2).

docs.title: Density-based Filtering
docs.text:
• --filter-by-density (flag): Enable density-based filtering of the stitched SGE.
  • --out-filtered-prefix (str): Prefix of the filtered outputs (default: filtered).
Auxiliary Density-based Filtering Parameters

We recommend using default values; override only if needed.

  • --radius (int): Radius for the polygon area calculation (default: 15).
  • --quartile (int): Quartile for the polygon area calculation (default: 2).
  • --hex-n-move (int): Sliding step (default: 1).
  • --polygon-min-size (int): Minimum polygon size (default: 500).

docs.title: Run Parameters
docs.text:
• --dry-run (flag): Write the Makefile and print the commands without executing.
  • --restart (flag): Ignore existing outputs and rerun all steps.
  • --n-jobs, -j (int): Number of parallel jobs (default: 1).
  • --makefn (str): Makefile name under --out-dir (default: sge_stitch.mk).

docs.title: Environment Parameters
docs.text: • --gzip (str): Path to gzip (default: gzip).

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Under --out-dir:

  • The stitched SGE: transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz, feature.clean.tsv.gz, coordinate_minmax.tsv (see the unified SGE format).
  • coordinate_minmax_per_tile.tsv: per tile, the local min/max, the X/Y offsets applied, and the resulting global bounds in µm.
  • feature.distribution.tsv.gz: per feature, the number of tiles containing it and its count in each tile.
  • sge_assets.json: paths of the SGE to use downstream, in the same format as sge_convert's; written after the Makefile runs.
  • Oriented tiles (for tiles with a rotation): r<row>c<col>.rot<deg>[.vfip][.hfip].transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz, with matching .feature.clean.tsv.gz and .coordinate_minmax.tsv.
  • With --filter-by-density: <prefix>.transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz, <prefix>.feature.lenient.tsv.gz, <prefix>.coordinate_minmax.tsv (and boundary GeoJSONs); sge_assets.json then points to these files.
  • sge_stitch.done, sge_density_filtering.done, and per-tile .done flags; the Makefile sge_stitch.mk.

docs.title: Supported Platforms & Inputs
docs.text:
run_together's one-command convenience comes from platform profiles that read each platform's standard output layout automatically. This page is the status hub; each built-in profile has its own page with the exact expected inputs and example commands.

For the profile mechanics (input modes, the canonical config, layer merging), see Specifying Inputs.

docs.title: Profile status
docs.text:
--platform Profile Ingest Details 10x_xenium ✅ built-in sge_convert (10x_xenium) Xenium page 10x_visium_hd ✅ built-in sge_convert (10x_visium_hd) Visium HD page cosmx_smi ✅ built-in reformat_cosmx CosMx SMI page merfish (Vizgen MERSCOPE) ✅ built-in sge_convert (vizgen_merscope) MERSCOPE page illumina (Illumina StrataMap) ✅ built-in sge_convert (illumina) Illumina StrataMap page stereoseq (BGI Stereo-seq) ✅ built-in SAW gef2gem + sge_convert (bgi_stereoseq) Stereo-seq page seqscope (Seq-Scope) ✅ built-in sge_convert (seqscope) Seq-Scope page generic (any source) ✅ built-in an already-ingested transcript TSV, or sge_convert (generic) Generic page Pixel-seq, Nova-ST via a custom profile sge_convert (pixel_seq, nova_st) below
  • built-in — run_together --platform <name> works with no extra configuration. The profiles are assets/run_together_profiles/<name>.json.
  • via a custom profile — sge_convert already has an ingest preset; there is no dedicated run_together profile yet.

docs.title: Built-in platforms
docs.text:
Each page documents the expected input files/columns, the FICTURE/packaging defaults, and example commands for the input modes (single-sample CLI, sample sheet, config JSON):

  • 10x Xenium — Xenium Ranger directory; morphology images auto-detected; xeniumranger clusters.
  • 10x Visium HD — Space Ranger outs/; square-bin and segmented-cell layers; a cartloader cell analysis on the segmented cells; per-sample H&E.
  • CosMx SMI — AtoMx flat-file export via reformat_cosmx; glob-based file matching with overrides.
  • MERSCOPE / MERFISH — individual files or a standard export dir; cell analysis from boundaries, a cell×gene matrix, or an existing cell_id (incl. mixed joint runs).
  • Illumina StrataMap — MEX input with spatial coordinates embedded in the barcode; optional cell boundaries enable cell-level analysis.
  • BGI Stereo-seq — prefix-addressed binary GEFs expanded by SAW (--saw); cell-bin segmentation clustered from its own pixel TSV; registered histology at 0.5 µm/pixel.
  • Seq-Scope — --in-dir is the MEX directory (or a raw per-molecule TSV via --raw-transcript); nanometer coordinates; pixel-level only (no segmentation); pre-georeferenced H&E.
  • Generic — a transcript TSV from any source (already in CartLoader's layout, or a CSV/TSV converted by sge_convert --platform generic); optional cell analysis from a cell-id column or a MEX.

docs.title: Custom profiles
docs.text:
--platform-json <file> deep-merges a JSON file over the built-in profile named by --platform: nested blocks merge key by key, while lists (e.g. ingest.extra_flags, ingest.autodetect, images) are replaced whole. --platform must still name a built-in profile, so a custom profile is always a modification of one — start from the closest match, or from generic for a plain transcript table. The file is not checked for unknown keys.

For example, a Pixel-seq transcript table through sge_convert's pixel_seq preset:

{ "ingest": { "sge_platform": "pixel_seq" } }

cartloader run_together --platform generic --platform-json pixelseq.json \
    --raw-transcript /data/pixelseq/transcripts.tsv.gz --out-dir OUT

ingest.sge_platform selects the sge_convert preset (column names, delimiter); add --units-per-um if the coordinates are not in microns. Any profile key can be set this way; a --config can carry the same blocks for a single run (see Specifying Inputs → Mode 3), with strict key validation.

Without run_together, the modules can also be run directly: sge_convert → run_ficture2 → run_cartload2 (see the platform tutorials and sge_convert for the per-platform ingest presets).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• run_together Overview · Specifying Inputs · Image Modalities
  • Guides: single sample · multiple samples
  • sge_convert reference — per-platform ingest details.

docs.title: Upload to AWS S3
docs.text:
Usually run for you

run_together uploads each packaged sample (and, for joint runs, multi-catalog.yaml with the shared files) with its own --s3-upload stage, to <s3-prefix>/batch=<YYYY_MM>/<collection>/<dir>. Use upload_aws to upload a packaged directory directly, to any S3 path.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Use upload_aws to publish CartLoader outputs (PMTiles, factor files, and the catalog) to Amazon S3 for sharing or deployment. It supports single‑dataset uploads and collection uploads (multiple dataset directories via --in-list). File lists are taken from catalog.yaml and split into three groups:

  • basics: every file the catalog references, except the two groups below (includes the SGE basemaps and AI alias files recorded as alias_ai);
  • optional: UMAP files (umap.tsv, umap.png, umap.ind_png, umap.pmtiles) and manual alias files;
  • basemaps: non-SGE basemaps, such as histology images.

Question

  • Why did my AWS upload fail, and how can I fix it?

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A packaged directory with a catalog.yaml, from run_cartload2 (or each sample directory of run_cartload2_multi). Every file the catalog references must exist locally.
  • AWS CLI installed and configured (e.g., aws configure).

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Writes a Makefile (--makefn, inside --in-dir) with one upload target per group and runs it:

  • basics: all basic files plus catalog.yaml in one target, flagged by <in-dir>/cartload.aws.done;
  • optional and basemap files: one target per file, each followed by a re-upload of catalog.yaml, flagged by <file>.aws.done.

catalog.yaml is always uploaded as <s3-dir>/catalog.yaml. Existing flags make reruns skip completed uploads; use --restart to upload again.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
Single Dataset UploadCollection Upload (Multiple Datasets) 
AWS_DIR="s3://example/aws/prefix"   # S3 prefix that will contain the dataset
DATA_ID="EXAMPLE_ID"                # dataset identifier

cartloader upload_aws \
  --in-dir /path/to/cartload2/output \
  --s3-dir "${AWS_DIR}/${DATA_ID}" \
  --n-jobs 10

AWS_DIR="s3://example/aws/prefix"        # S3 prefix that will contain the collection
COLLECTION_ID="EXAMPLE_COLLECTION_ID"    # collection identifier
IN_LIST=/path/to/dirs.tsv                # one sub-directory name per line; no header
cartloader upload_aws \
  --in-dir /path/to/parent_cartload_outputs \
  --s3-dir "${AWS_DIR}/${COLLECTION_ID}" \
  --in-list ${IN_LIST} \
  --n-jobs 10

Collection Structure

Input Collection

  • --in-dir is a parent directory containing one subdirectory per dataset; --in-list names those subdirectories (first column).
  • Each subdirectory must include its own catalog.yaml.
  • For a run_cartload2_multi output, the subdirectories are named <multi_id>-<sample_id>; list those names. Collection mode uploads only the subdirectories, not the root multi-catalog.yaml or the shared factor files next to it.
/path/to/parent_cartload_outputs/   # defined by `--in-dir`
├── SAMPLE_001      # listed in `--in-list`
│   ├── catalog.yaml
│   ├── ...         # SGE assets (e.g., genes_all.pmtiles)
│   ├── ...         # FICTURE assets (e.g., *-model.tsv, *-pseudobulk.tsv.gz, *-bulk-de.tsv, *-info.tsv, *.pmtiles, *-rgb.tsv)
│   ├── ...         # Background assets (e.g., from `cartloader import_image`)
│   └── ...         # Cell assets (e.g., from `import_*_cell`)
├── SAMPLE_002
│   └── ...
└── SAMPLE_003
   └── ...

Output S3 Collection

  • Each dataset uploads to <s3-dir>/<s3_id>/, where <s3_id> is the catalog's id, or, without one, the listed name lowercased with underscores replaced by hyphens.
s3://example/aws/prefix/EXAMPLE_COLLECTION_ID/   # defined by `--s3-dir`
├── sample-001      # catalog `id`, else lowercased name with underscores → hyphens
│   ├── catalog.yaml
│   └── ...
├── sample-002
│   └── ...
└── sample-003
   └── ...

docs.title: Input/Output
docs.text:
• --in-dir (str, required): Input directory (single) or parent directory with per-dataset subdirectories (collection).
  • --s3-dir (str, required): S3 destination (single) or parent prefix for per-dataset outputs (collection).
  • --catalog-yaml (str): Catalog to read (single mode only; default: <in-dir>/catalog.yaml).

docs.title: Upload Selection
docs.text:
• --upload-basics-only (flag): Upload only the basic files and the catalog.
  • --upload-optional-only (flag): Upload only the optional files (UMAP, alias).
  • --upload-basemap-only (flag): Upload only the additional basemaps.

Use at most one of these flags: combining two or more uploads nothing.

docs.title: Collection Parameters
docs.text: • --in-list (str): TSV of subdirectory names under --in-dir (first column; no header); enables collection mode. Cannot be combined with --catalog-yaml.

docs.title: AWS Configuration
docs.text:
• --aws (str): AWS CLI executable (default: aws).
  • --profile (str): AWS CLI profile passed to every aws s3 cp (default: the CLI's default profile).

docs.title: Run Parameters
docs.text:
• --dry-run (flag): Write the Makefile and print the commands (make -n) without uploading.
  • --restart (flag): Ignore existing .aws.done flags and upload everything again.
  • --n-jobs (int): Number of parallel jobs (default: 2).
  • --makefn (str): Makefile name, written inside --in-dir (default: upload_aws.mk).

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Files uploaded under --s3-dir (per-dataset subdirectories in collection mode).
  • <in-dir>/upload_aws.mk (always written, also in dry-run mode).
  • Flag files: cartload.aws.done in each dataset directory and <file>.aws.done next to each uploaded optional or basemap file.

docs.title: Upload to Zenodo
docs.text:
Not part of run_together

run_together has no Zenodo stage; its publishing step uploads to S3 only. Run upload_zenodo yourself on a packaged directory (e.g., cartl/<id>/).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Use upload_zenodo to publish CartLoader outputs (PMTiles, factor files, and the catalog) to a Zenodo deposition, either an existing one or a newly created draft. In catalog mode, files are taken from catalog.yaml and uploaded in three groups: cartload basics (with catalog.yaml), additional basemaps (non-SGE PMTiles), and optional files (UMAP, alias), using the same grouping as upload_aws.

--restart deletes every file in the target draft

With --zenodo-deposition-id, --restart removes all files currently in the target draft deposition before uploading, including files that are not part of this upload and files a new-version draft inherited from the published record. To replace only the files you are uploading, use --overwrite instead.

--dry-run still changes Zenodo

--dry-run skips file uploads, file deletions, and publishing, but it still:

  • creates a new deposition when --zenodo-deposition-id is omitted;
  • opens a new-version draft when the ID points to a published record;
  • writes the merged metadata to the deposition.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A packaged directory from run_cartload2 with a catalog.yaml (for --upload-method catalog).
  • A Zenodo access token saved in a file.
  • For a new deposition: --title and at least one --creators entry.
  • (Optional) A Zenodo deposition ID to upload to an existing deposition.

Question

  • What are the Zenodo token and deposition ID, and how do you get them?

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
1. Choose the deposition. Without --zenodo-deposition-id, a new draft is created with the given metadata. With an ID of a draft, that draft is used. With an ID of a published record, its latest unsubmitted draft is reused if one exists; otherwise a new version is created. New-version drafts start with the files of the published version.
  2. Update metadata (existing depositions). Provided --title, --description, and --creators replace the existing values; --upload-type (default dataset) always replaces the existing type.
  3. Select files by --upload-method. Files are uploaded under their basenames.
  4. Check capacity. If the deposition would hold more than 100 files (existing plus new distinct names), the command aborts before uploading.
  5. Upload. Files not yet in the deposition are uploaded; files whose names already exist are skipped unless --overwrite (or --restart) is set. In catalog mode the groups are uploaded in order: basics with catalog.yaml, then basemaps, then optional files.
  6. Publish with --publish (skipped in dry-run mode). Uploads rejected by Zenodo are listed at the end with a command to retry them; other upload errors (e.g., connection failures) are only printed in the log.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
Create a new deposition to uploadUpload to an existing depositionUpload explicit files 
cartloader upload_zenodo \
  --upload-method catalog \
  --in-dir /path/to/run_cartload2/output/directory \
  --zenodo-token /path/to/zenodo_token.txt \
  --title  "Title Info" \
  --creators "Lastname, Firstname" \
  --description "Description Info"
  • --upload-method catalog: Upload the files referenced by the catalog.
  • --title and --creators are required for a new deposition.
zenodo_deposition_id=DEPOSITION_ID                # replace with your deposition ID (published IDs get a new draft automatically)

cartloader upload_zenodo \
  --upload-method catalog \
  --in-dir /path/to/run_cartload2/output/directory \
  --zenodo-token /path/to/zenodo_token.txt \
  --zenodo-deposition-id ${zenodo_deposition_id}

Add --overwrite to replace files that already exist in the deposition.

cartloader upload_zenodo \
  --upload-method files \
  --in-dir /path/to/run_cartload2/output/directory \
  --files catalog.yaml genes_all.pmtiles some_factor.pmtiles \
  --zenodo-token /path/to/zenodo_token.txt \
  --zenodo-deposition-id ${zenodo_deposition_id}
  • --upload-method files: Upload only the files given by --files.

docs.title: Input Selection
docs.text:
• --in-dir (str, required): Directory containing the files to upload.

  • --upload-method (str): Which files to upload (default: all).

    --upload-method Options

    • all: every regular file directly in --in-dir (not recursive; includes Makefiles, logs, and flag files);
    • catalog: the files referenced by catalog.yaml, plus the catalog itself;
    • files: only the files given by --files.

  • --files (list of str): Files to upload, relative to --in-dir or absolute. Required with --upload-method files.

  • --catalog-yaml (str): Catalog for --upload-method catalog (default: <in-dir>/catalog.yaml).

docs.title: Zenodo Configuration
docs.text:
• --zenodo-token (str, required): Path to a file containing your Zenodo access token.
  • --zenodo-deposition-id (str): Existing deposition ID. A published record gets a draft (reused or newly created); omit to create a new deposition.
  • --publish (flag): Publish the deposition after upload. Recommended to leave off and publish manually after reviewing the draft on Zenodo.

docs.title: Zenodo Metadata
docs.text:
• --title (str): Deposition title. Required for a new deposition.
  • --creators (list of str): Creators, each quoted, e.g. "Lastname, Firstname". Required for a new deposition.
  • --description (str): Deposition description (new depositions default to No description provided.).
  • --upload-type (str): One of dataset, software, publication, poster, presentation, image, video, lesson, other (default: dataset; also applied to existing depositions).

docs.title: Behavior Flags
docs.text:
• --overwrite (flag): Re-upload files whose names already exist in the deposition, replacing them.
  • --restart (flag): Delete all files in the target draft first, then upload (see the warning above). Implies --overwrite.
  • --dry-run (flag): Print the files that would be uploaded or deleted; Zenodo is still contacted and modified as described above.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
• Files uploaded to the Zenodo deposition (existing draft, new version draft, or new deposition); the deposition ID is printed.
  • With --upload-method catalog (not in dry-run mode): <in-dir>/cartload.zenodo.done is touched after the basics group, even if some of its files failed to upload, and <file>.zenodo.done is written next to each successfully uploaded basemap or optional file. Check the log for failures before relying on these flags.

docs.title: Visium HD Pipeline Add-on Modules (Legacy)
docs.text:
Legacy

load_space_ranger supports the legacy run_visiumhd orchestrator, which is superseded by run_together; run_together detects Visium HD inputs from --in-dir through its Visium HD profile. This page is kept for reference and is not part of the recommended workflow; see Legacy Orchestrators.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: load_space_ranger scans a 10x Visium HD Space Ranger output directory and writes a JSON manifest of detected assets: SGE inputs (2 µm bins and spatial metadata), segmented cell analysis outputs, the 8 µm and 16 µm square-bin analyses, and an H&E image. The manifest can be passed as --in-json to sge_convert, import_visiumhd_cell, import_visiumhd_square, and import_image, and is read by run_visiumhd. It is also a way to unpack Space Ranger .tar.gz archives, which run_together does not extract.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A Space Ranger output directory.
  • Optional: a writable directory for archive extraction (--unzip-dir).

docs.title: Load Space Ranger (load_space_ranger)
docs.text:
For each key below, the first existing path under --in-dir is used. If none exists, any matching archive found anywhere under --in-dir (*_segmented_outputs.tar.gz for cells; *_square_<NNN>um_binned_outputs.tar.gz or *_binned_outputs.tar.gz for bins) is extracted into --unzip-dir and searched there.

  • SGE (required keys):

    • TRANSCRIPT_MEX: square_002um/filtered_feature_bc_matrix or binned_outputs/square_002um/filtered_feature_bc_matrix
    • SCALE: square_002um/spatial/scalefactors_json.json or binned_outputs/square_002um/spatial/scalefactors_json.json
    • POSITION: square_002um/spatial/tissue_positions.parquet or binned_outputs/square_002um/spatial/tissue_positions.parquet

  • CELLS (segmented outputs):

    • Required: CELL_FEATURE_MEX — segmented_outputs/filtered_feature_cell_matrix
    • Required: CELL_GEOJSON — segmented_outputs/cell_segmentations.geojson
    • Optional: NUCLEUS_GEOJSON — segmented_outputs/nucleus_segmentations.geojson
    • Required: CLUSTER — segmented_outputs/analysis/clustering/gene_expression_graphclust/clusters.csv
    • Required: DE — segmented_outputs/analysis/diffexp/gene_expression_graphclust/differential_expression.csv
    • Optional: PCA_PROJ — segmented_outputs/analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/projection.csv
    • Optional: PCA_VAR — segmented_outputs/analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/variance.csv
    • Optional: UMAP_PROJ — segmented_outputs/analysis/umap/gene_expression_2_components/projection.csv

  • GRID_8um and GRID_16um (square bins of 8 µm and 16 µm; all optional), each under square_008um/ or binned_outputs/square_008um/ (square_016um/ for 16 µm):

    • GRID_FEATURE_MEX: filtered_feature_bc_matrix
    • SCALE: spatial/scalefactors_json.json
    • POSITION: spatial/tissue_positions.parquet
    • CLUSTER: analysis/clustering/gene_expression_graphclust/clusters.csv
    • DE: analysis/diffexp/gene_expression_graphclust/differential_expression.csv
    • PCA_PROJ: analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/projection.csv
    • PCA_VAR: analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/variance.csv
    • UMAP_PROJ: analysis/umap/gene_expression_2_components/projection.csv

  • IMAGES (optional):

    • HnE: The first file under --in-dir (searched recursively) ending in _tissue_image.btf, _tissue_image.tif, or _tissue_image.tiff, in that order of preference. Archives are not searched for images.

Missing files

Paths are exact; availability varies by dataset. Missing optional entries are left out of the manifest (a section with nothing found is written empty), but a missing required entry stops the command with an error listing what was not found.

If --out-json already exists and --overwrite is not set, its entries are kept and only missing keys are resolved.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
cartloader load_space_ranger \
  --in-dir /path/to/SpaceRanger_*_outs \
  --out-json /path/to/out/visiumhd_space_ranger_assets.json

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• --in-dir (str, required): Space Ranger output directory to scan.
  • --out-json (str, required): Path to write the assets JSON.
  • --unzip-dir (str): Directory to extract archives into (default: --in-dir).
  • --overwrite (flag): Re-resolve all entries instead of keeping those in an existing --out-json.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Writes a JSON manifest at --out-json.

Example (includes/visiumhd_space_ranger_assets.visiumhd_3prime_mouse_brain.json):

{
    "SGE": {
        "TRANSCRIPT_MEX": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_002um/filtered_feature_bc_matrix",
        "SCALE": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_002um/spatial/scalefactors_json.json",
        "POSITION": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_002um/spatial/tissue_positions.parquet"
    },

        "DE": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/segmented_outputs/analysis/diffexp/gene_expression_graphclust/differential_expression.csv",
        "PCA_PROJ": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/segmented_outputs/analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/projection.csv",
        "PCA_VAR": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/segmented_outputs/analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/variance.csv",
        "UMAP_PROJ": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/segmented_outputs/analysis/umap/gene_expression_2_components/projection.csv"
    },
    "GRID_8um": {
        "GRID_FEATURE_MEX": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_008um/filtered_feature_bc_matrix",
        "SCALE": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_008um/spatial/scalefactors_json.json",
        "POSITION": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_008um/spatial/tissue_positions.parquet",
        "CLUSTER": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_008um/analysis/clustering/gene_expression_graphclust/clusters.csv",
        "DE": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_008um/analysis/diffexp/gene_expression_graphclust/differential_expression.csv",
        "PCA_PROJ": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_008um/analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/projection.csv",
        "PCA_VAR": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_008um/analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/variance.csv",
        "UMAP_PROJ": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_008um/analysis/umap/gene_expression_2_components/projection.csv"
    },
    "GRID_16um": {
        "GRID_FEATURE_MEX": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_016um/filtered_feature_bc_matrix",
        "SCALE": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_016um/spatial/scalefactors_json.json",
        "POSITION": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_016um/spatial/tissue_positions.parquet",
        "CLUSTER": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_016um/analysis/clustering/gene_expression_graphclust/clusters.csv",
        "DE": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_016um/analysis/diffexp/gene_expression_graphclust/differential_expression.csv",
        "PCA_PROJ": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_016um/analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/projection.csv",
        "PCA_VAR": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_016um/analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/variance.csv",
        "UMAP_PROJ": "/example_dir/Visium_HD_3prime_Mouse_Brain/binned_outputs/square_016um/analysis/umap/gene_expression_2_components/projection.csv"
    },
