docs.title: Xenium Pipeline Add-on Modules (Legacy)
docs.text:
Legacy

load_xenium_ranger supports the legacy run_xenium orchestrator, which is superseded by run_together; run_together detects Xenium inputs from --in-dir through its Xenium profile. This page is kept for reference and is not part of the recommended workflow; see Legacy Orchestrators.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: load_xenium_ranger scans a 10x Xenium Ranger output directory and writes a JSON manifest of detected assets (SGE, cell analysis outputs, and morphology images). The manifest can be passed as --in-json to sge_convert, import_xenium_cell, and import_image, and is read by run_xenium. It is also a way to unpack the Xenium analysis.tar.gz and cell_feature_matrix.tar.gz archives, which run_together does not extract.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• A Xenium Ranger output directory.
  • Optional: a writable directory for archive extraction (--unzip-dir).

docs.title: Load Xenium Ranger (load_xenium_ranger)
docs.text:
For each key below, the first existing path under --in-dir is used. If none exists and the key lists an archive, the archive (under --in-dir) is extracted into --unzip-dir and searched there.

  • SGE:
    • Required: TRANSCRIPT — transcripts.csv.gz or transcripts.parquet
  • CELLS:
    • Required: CELL — cells.csv.gz or cells.parquet
    • Required: BOUNDARY — cell_boundaries.csv.gz
    • Optional: CELL_FEATURE_MEX — cell_feature_matrix/ (archive: cell_feature_matrix.tar.gz)
    • Required: CLUSTER — analysis/clustering/gene_expression_graphclust/clusters.csv (archive: analysis.tar.gz)
    • Required: DE — analysis/diffexp/gene_expression_graphclust/differential_expression.csv (archive: analysis.tar.gz)
    • Optional: PCA_PROJ — analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/projection.csv (archive: analysis.tar.gz)
    • Optional: PCA_VAR — analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/variance.csv (archive: analysis.tar.gz)
    • Optional: UMAP_PROJ — analysis/umap/gene_expression_2_components/projection.csv (archive: analysis.tar.gz)
  • IMAGES (OME‑TIFF, all optional):
    • DAPI_OME — morphology_focus.ome.tif or morphology_focus/morphology_focus_0000.ome.tif
    • BOUNDARY_OME — morphology_focus/morphology_focus_0001.ome.tif
    • INTERIOR_RNA_OME — morphology_focus/morphology_focus_0002.ome.tif
    • INTERIOR_PROTEIN_OME — morphology_focus/morphology_focus_0003.ome.tif
    • DAPI_MIP_OME — morphology_mip.ome.tif (present in older Xenium outputs only)

The 3D DAPI stack (morphology.ome.tif) is not detected.

Missing files

Paths are exact; availability varies by dataset. Missing optional entries are left out of the manifest, but a missing required entry stops the command with an error listing what was not found. An optional entry whose archive is listed above also stops the command if neither the file nor the archive exists (e.g., cell_feature_matrix/ and cell_feature_matrix.tar.gz both absent, or a missing UMAP_PROJ without analysis.tar.gz).

If --out-json already exists and --overwrite is not set, its entries are kept and only missing keys are resolved.

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
cartloader load_xenium_ranger \
  --in-dir /path/to/xenium/ranger/output \
  --out-json /path/to/out/xenium_ranger_assets.json \
  --unzip-dir /path/to/out/unzip

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
• --in-dir (str, required): Xenium Ranger output directory to scan.
  • --out-json (str, required): Path to write the assets JSON.
  • --unzip-dir (str): Directory to extract archives into (default: --in-dir).
  • --overwrite (flag): Re-resolve all entries instead of keeping those in an existing --out-json.

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
Writes a JSON manifest at --out-json.

Example (includes/xenium_ranger_assets.human_lung_cancer.json):

{
    "SGE": {
        "TRANSCRIPT": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/transcripts.csv.gz"
    },
    "CELLS": {
        "CELL": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/cells.csv.gz",
        "BOUNDARY": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/cell_boundaries.csv.gz",
        "CELL_FEATURE_MEX": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/cell_feature_matrix",
        "CLUSTER": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/analysis/clustering/gene_expression_graphclust/clusters.csv",
        "DE": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/analysis/diffexp/gene_expression_graphclust/differential_expression.csv",
        "PCA_PROJ": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/projection.csv",
        "PCA_VAR": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/analysis/pca/gene_expression_10_components/variance.csv",
        "UMAP_PROJ": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/analysis/umap/gene_expression_2_components/projection.csv"
    },
    "IMAGES": {
        "DAPI_OME": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/morphology_focus/morphology_focus_0000.ome.tif",
        "BOUNDARY_OME": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/morphology_focus/morphology_focus_0001.ome.tif",
        "INTERIOR_RNA_OME": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/morphology_focus/morphology_focus_0002.ome.tif",
        "INTERIOR_PROTEIN_OME": "/example_dir/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs/morphology_focus/morphology_focus_0003.ome.tif"
    }
}

docs.title: Platform: CosMx SMI (--platform cosmx_smi)
docs.text: Built-in profile. Unlike the others, ingest does not run sge_convert: a dedicated reformat_cosmx step reads the three raw CSVs and, converting global-pixel coordinates to microns (0.12028 µm/px), writes the transcript TSV plus the cell-metadata (xy) and polygon (boundaries) files that FICTURE and cell decode consume. Point --in-dir at the AtoMx / CosMx SMI flat-file export directory; filenames are matched by glob (exactly one file must match each).

docs.title: Expected inputs (under --in-dir)
docs.text:
Purpose Default glob reformat flag Produces Transcripts *tx_file.csv.gz (cols fov, cell_ID, target, x_global_px, y_global_px, z) --tx *.transcripts.tsv.gz Cell centroids *metadata*.csv.gz (cols fov, cell_ID, CenterX_global_px, CenterY_global_px) --meta *.metadata.csv.gz (xy, cols X/Y) Cell boundaries *polygons.csv.gz (cols fov, cellID, x_global_px, y_global_px) --poly *.polygons.csv.gz

Cell ids are formed as <fov>_<cell_ID>; transcripts with cell_ID = 0 are kept but tagged UNASSIGNED, and System* control probes are dropped at ingest. The cartloader cell factor is decoded from the metadata + polygon files via run_ficture2_multi_cells.

Defaults: FICTURE width=12, n_factor=12,24,48, min_ct_per_unit_hexagon=100, single-molecule mode; packaging with --use-pmpoint --bin-count 500.

docs.title: 1. Single sample (direct CLI)
docs.text:
cartloader run_together --platform cosmx_smi \
    --in-dir /data/cosmx/export --out-dir OUT \
    --width 12 --n-factor 24 -j 8 --threads 8

docs.title: Overriding the input file patterns
docs.text:
CosMx exports don't always use the standard suffixes. Any glob can be overridden with a small JSON whose ingest.inputs block deep-merges over the profile — restate only the patterns that differ:

{ "platform": "cosmx_smi", "ingest": { "inputs": { "--tx": "*tx_unique.csv.gz" } } }

cartloader run_together --config cosmx.json --in-dir /data/cosmx/export --out-dir OUT

For an export with ..._tx.csv.gz, ..._tx_unique.csv.gz, ..._metadata.csv.gz, and ..._polygons.csv.gz, only the --tx override above is needed (the default --meta/--poly globs already match _metadata/_polygons).

docs.title: 2. Multi-sample (sample sheet)
docs.text:
For raw exports, one in_dir per row (each reformatted independently, then jointly modeled):

id      in_dir
s1      /data/cosmx/s1
s2      /data/cosmx/s2

For already-reformatted samples, point the role columns at the produced files to skip re-ingest:

id      transcript                    cell_xy                    cell_boundary
s1      /out/s1/s1.transcripts.tsv.gz /out/s1/s1.metadata.csv.gz /out/s1/s1.polygons.csv.gz

cartloader run_together --platform cosmx_smi --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT \
    --width 12 --n-factor 24 -j 8

docs.title: 3. Full config (JSON)
docs.text:
// run.json — per-sample glob override + joint samples
{
  "platform": "cosmx_smi", "out_dir": "OUT",
  "resources": { "n_jobs": 8, "threads": 16 },
  "ingest": { "inputs": { "--tx": "*tx_unique.csv.gz" } },
  "samples": [
    { "id": "s1", "in_dir": "/data/cosmx/s1" },
    { "id": "s2", "in_dir": "/data/cosmx/s2" }
  ]
}

cartloader run_together --config run.json

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Glob discipline: each pattern must match exactly one file — zero or multiple is an error that lists what's present. Narrow the pattern via ingest.inputs.
  • Transcripts already carry a per-molecule cell_ID, so no tsv-add-cell-id step is needed (contrast with MERSCOPE).
  • --jitter-xy and --units-per-um are rejected on this platform: reformat_cosmx, not sge_convert, writes the transcript TSV. The ingest feature filters do apply.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• reformat_cosmx · Specifying Inputs · Overview
  • Starter tutorial: CosMx SMI

docs.title: Platform: Generic (--platform generic)
docs.text:
Built-in profile (assets/run_together_profiles/generic.json) for spatial data from any source that can be expressed as a transcript table: one row per molecule (or per spatial bin and gene) with X, Y, gene, and optionally a count and a cell id. Use it for platforms without a dedicated profile, or for data you have already converted yourself.

A sample's transcript comes in one of two forms:

  • Already ingested — a TSV in CartLoader's transcript layout; ingest is skipped.
  • Raw — a CSV/TSV converted by sge_convert --platform generic at ingest.

docs.title: Expected inputs
docs.text:
Role Auto-detected under --in-dir CLI flag / column Format Transcript (already ingested) transcripts.tsv.gz --in-transcript / transcript (tsv) Tab-separated with a header row X Y gene count, optionally a fifth cell_id column; coordinates in µm. Ingest filters, --jitter-xy and --units-per-um do not apply to it. Transcript (raw) — --raw-transcript / raw_transcript Defaults: tab-separated, columns X, Y, gene, no count column (each row counts 1), coordinates in µm. Override with --colname-transcript-x/-y/-feature/-count, --units-per-um, and ingest.extra_flags (e.g. ["--csv-delim ,"] for a comma-separated file). A .parquet is converted to .csv.gz first. Cell centroids cells.csv.gz --in-cell-xy / xy (cell_xy) Columns X, Y, and a cell id (--colname-cell or --colname-xy-cell, else cell_id). Cell boundaries cell_boundaries.csv.gz --in-cell-boundary / boundaries Comma-separated; the first three columns are cell_id, vertex_x, vertex_y (µm), vertices grouped by cell. Used to render cell polygons. Cell-feature MEX — mex (mex_dir) or mex_bcd / mex_ftr / mex_mtx; or cellxgene (cell_by_gene, --in-cellxgene), converted to a MEX at ingest for a raw-transcript sample Barcodes are the cell ids.

Only a transcript is required. With --in-dir, a directory without transcripts.tsv.gz has no transcript source and the run stops; give the file with --in-transcript or --raw-transcript instead.

Defaults: FICTURE width=12, n_factor=12,24,48, single-molecule mode; packaging with --use-pmpoint --bin-count 500; no images (attach them with --image / --images).

docs.title: Cell-level analysis
docs.text:
The cartloader cell analysis is selected explicitly, for all samples of a run at once:

Cell-count source How to turn it on A cell_id column in the transcript (column 5) --colname-cell <name> (or top-level colname_cell in --config). The column is read by position; the name is also the default cell-id column of the xy file. For a raw transcript, also pass --colname-transcript-cell <raw column> so ingest carries that column to position 5. A MEX in every sample Provide mex (or cellxgene) for each sample; no flag needed.

Giving both is an error; with neither, cell analysis is skipped and the run is pixel-level (FICTURE → packaging). When present, xy and boundaries are added to the decode (cell centroids, polygons). --colname-boundary-* has no effect on this platform.

docs.title: 1. Single sample (direct CLI)
docs.text:
A directory holding the already-ingested files under their standard names:

/data/sample1/
├── transcripts.tsv.gz       # X, Y, gene, count, cell_id  (µm)
├── cells.csv.gz             # optional: cell_id, X, Y
└── cell_boundaries.csv.gz   # optional: cell_id, vertex_x, vertex_y

cartloader run_together --platform generic \
    --in-dir /data/sample1 --out-dir OUT --colname-cell cell_id \
    --width 12 --n-factor 24

A raw comma-separated file with its own column names:

cartloader run_together --platform generic \
    --raw-transcript /data/molecules.csv \
    --colname-transcript-x x_um --colname-transcript-y y_um \
    --colname-transcript-feature gene_name \
    --config generic.json --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 24

{ "ingest": { "extra_flags": ["--csv-delim ,"] } }

As on every platform, a lone --out-dir sample is rep1 unless --id is given, and its packaged directory is OUT/cartl/<OUT basename>-rep1/.

docs.title: 2. Multi-sample (sample sheet)
docs.text:
One joint FICTURE model across samples sharing --out-dir. Here every sample has a cell-feature MEX, so the cell analysis is MEX-based:

id    transcript                     mex                   xy
s1    /data/s1/transcripts.tsv.gz    /data/s1/cell_mex     /data/s1/cells.csv.gz
s2    /data/s2/transcripts.tsv.gz    /data/s2/cell_mex     /data/s2/cells.csv.gz

cartloader run_together --platform generic \
    --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 24 -j 8

docs.title: 3. Full config (JSON)
docs.text:
// run.json
{
  "platform": "generic", "out_dir": "OUT",
  "colname_cell": "cell_id",
  "samples": [
    { "id": "s1", "in_dir": "/data/s1" },
    { "id": "s2", "transcript": "/data/s2/tx.tsv.gz", "xy": "/data/s2/cells.csv.gz" }
  ],
  "ficture": [ { "id": "denovo", "mode": "train", "width": "12", "n_factor": "12,24,48" } ]
}

cartloader run_together --config run.json

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• A different sge_convert preset. To read a raw file with another platform's sge_convert preset (e.g. pixel_seq, nova_st), set ingest.sge_platform in a --config or a --platform-json file; see Supported Platforms → Custom profiles.
  • Coordinates must be in µm after ingest. Boundary and centroid files are never rescaled.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Specifying Inputs · Image Modalities · Overview
  • sge_convert — the generic CSV/TSV ingest options.
  • Unsupported platform?

docs.title: Platform: Illumina StrataMap (--platform illumina)
docs.text: Built-in profile for Illumina StrataMap. Ingest runs sge_convert (the illumina preset). Like SeqScope, StrataMap is a sequencing-based spatial platform whose input is a MEX matrix (barcodes.tsv.gz / features.tsv.gz / matrix.mtx.gz); the spatial coordinates are embedded in the barcode string, so no separate positions/scale-factor file is needed. Individual per-molecule transcripts are not available — the transcript TSV is derived from the MEX.

docs.title: Expected inputs
docs.text:
Role What it is Column / config Required MEX matrix The StrataMap MEX directory (barcodes.tsv.gz, features.tsv.gz, matrix.mtx.gz) mex (alias mex_dir) ✅ Cell boundaries Cell boundary polygons (CSV) → enables cell-level analysis boundaries (aliases cell_boundary, cell_boundaries) / --in-cell-boundary optional Cell centroids (xy) Per-cell centroids → adds the spatial cluster scatter xy (alias cell_xy) / --in-cell-xy optional

The mex role must be a single directory (StrataMap ships the three files together) — it is passed to sge_convert --in-mex. sge_convert reads the coordinates out of the barcode with these StrataMap defaults: barcode delimiter :, X = field 3, Y = field 2. The coordinate units are detected from the barcode file (see below); override any of these per run — the units with --units-per-um, the rest through ingest.extra_flags in a --config; see sge_convert.

docs.title: Barcode coordinate units (nanometers or microns)
docs.text:
StrataMap has shipped two barcode formats, and they differ by a factor of 1000:

Barcode Units --units-per-um SBC:433503:2393851 (older) nanometers 1000 SBC:686.951:4668.15 (current) microns 1

Ingest reads the barcode file and picks the right one — a fractional coordinate means microns, otherwise the coordinate magnitude decides — and prints the value it used, so both formats run correctly without a flag. State it yourself when you want it pinned, or when a file is unusual enough that detection should not be trusted:

cartloader run_together --platform illumina --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT --units-per-um 1

--units-per-um always wins over the detection; if it contradicts the file, the run warns and uses your value. The config equivalent is {"ingest": {"units_per_um": 1}}. Getting this wrong rescales the whole sample by 1000x, so it is worth checking the reported units in the ingest log against gzip -cd barcodes.tsv.gz | head.

Default boundary/centroid column names (overridable — see below): boundaries cell_id / vertex_x / vertex_y; xy cell_id / X / Y.

Defaults: FICTURE width=12, n_factor=24,48,96, single-molecule mode; packaging with --use-pmpoint --bin-count 500.

How the MEX is supplied

The StrataMap MEX is provided as the mex role (sample sheet / config), not via --in-dir auto-detection — StrataMap has no standard directory layout, so this profile does not assume where the MEX sits. There is no single-sample --in-mex shortcut; use a one-row sample sheet or a --config.

docs.title: Cell-level analysis (boundaries)
docs.text:
StrataMap has no per-transcript cell assignment, so — exactly like MERSCOPE — supplying cell boundaries turns on cell-level decode: after sge_convert builds the X, Y, gene, count transcript, ingest runs spatula tsv-add-cell-id to assign each transcript to the polygon that contains it (point-in-polygon; transcripts inside no cell → UNASSIGNED), appending a cell_id column. The cartloader cell factor is then decoded via run_ficture2_multi_cells, and the boundaries render cell polygons. xy (optional) adds the per-cell spatial cluster scatter.

Without boundaries the run stays pixel-level (FICTURE → packaging).

Coordinate units

The boundary polygon coordinates must be in microns, matching the barcode-derived transcript coordinates — tsv-add-cell-id does not rescale them.

docs.title: 1. Single sample
docs.text:
Give a one-row sample sheet (or a --config) pointing mex at the matrix directory; add boundaries for cell-level analysis:

id        mex                         boundaries
MYSAMPLE  /data/stratamap/MYSAMPLE    /data/stratamap/MYSAMPLE/bounds.csv

cartloader run_together --platform illumina \
    --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 48

Boundary/centroid column names can be overridden per run with --colname-boundary-cell/-x/-y and --colname-xy-cell/-x/-y. The boundary overrides apply to tsv-add-cell-id; the cell-polygon layer still expects cell_id, vertex_x, vertex_y as the first three columns of the boundary CSV.

docs.title: 2. Multi-sample (sample sheet)
docs.text:
One joint FICTURE model across samples sharing --out-dir; a mix of boundary and pixel-only samples is fine (cell analysis runs for the samples that supply boundaries):

id      mex                          boundaries                       xy
s1      /data/stratamap/s1           /data/stratamap/s1/bounds.csv    /data/stratamap/s1/cells.csv
s2      /data/stratamap/s2

cartloader run_together --platform illumina \
    --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 48 -j 8

docs.title: 3. Full config (JSON)
docs.text:
// run.json
{
  "platform": "illumina", "out_dir": "OUT",
  "resources": { "n_jobs": 8, "threads": 16 },
  "samples": [
    { "id": "s1", "mex": "/data/stratamap/s1", "boundaries": "/data/stratamap/s1/bounds.csv" },
    { "id": "s2", "mex": "/data/stratamap/s2" }
  ],
  "ficture": [ { "id": "denovo", "mode": "train", "width": "12", "n_factor": "24,48,96" } ],
  // units are detected from the barcode file; pin them (and any other barcode parsing
  // that differs from the StrataMap defaults) here:
  "ingest": { "units_per_um": 1,
              "extra_flags": ["--sge-visual", "--bcd-delim :", "--icol-bcd-x 3", "--icol-bcd-y 2"] }
}

cartloader run_together --config run.json

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Coordinates come from the barcode. No --pos-parquet / --scale-json is used. The nanometer/micron convention is detected per dataset (see Barcode coordinate units) and can be pinned with --units-per-um; if a run's barcode layout differs, override the parsing flags via ingest.extra_flags.
  • Images: StrataMap has no standard morphology image; attach any histology you have as a generic image (see Image Modalities).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Specifying Inputs · Image Modalities · Overview
  • sge_convert — barcode/MEX parsing details.
  • Related sequencing-based platform: SeqScope starter tutorial.

docs.title: Platform: MERSCOPE / MERFISH (--platform merfish)
docs.text: Built-in profile for Vizgen MERSCOPE / MERFISH. Ingest runs sge_convert (the vizgen_merscope preset). Inputs are individual files that may be arbitrarily named and need not share a directory, so you can point at each one explicitly — or point --in-dir at a standard export directory and let the profile auto-detect them.

docs.title: Expected inputs
docs.text:
Role Standard file (auto-detected in --in-dir) CLI flag / column Expected columns (defaults) Transcripts (raw) detected_transcripts.csv.gz, detected_transcripts.csv, transcripts.csv.gz, or transcripts.csv (first found) --raw-transcript / raw_transcript global_x, global_y, gene (global_z optional) Cell centroids (xy) cell_metadata.csv --in-cell-xy / xy center_x, center_y; the unnamed first column holds the cell id Cell boundaries cell_boundaries.csv --in-cell-boundary / boundaries cell_id, vertex_x, vertex_y Cell×gene matrix cell_by_gene.csv --in-cellxgene / cellxgene first column = cell id; remaining columns = genes (Blank* dropped)

Column names may be overridden when they differ (the flags apply to every sample): --colname-transcript-x/-y/-feature/-count, --colname-xy-cell/-x/-y (use --colname-xy-cell '' for the unnamed index column), and --colname-boundary-cell/-x/-y. The boundary overrides apply to tsv-add-cell-id; the cell-polygon layer still expects cell_id, vertex_x, vertex_y as the first three columns of the boundary CSV.

An already-ingested transcript TSV can be given instead with --in-transcript / transcript (skips ingest, including the cellxgene → MEX conversion).

Defaults: FICTURE width=12, n_factor=12,24,48, single-molecule mode; packaging with --use-pmpoint --bin-count 500. Coordinates are already in microns and are not shifted, so the files stay aligned.

docs.title: 1. Single sample (direct CLI)
docs.text:
Point at each file explicitly:

cartloader run_together --platform merfish \
    --raw-transcript   /data/detected_transcripts.csv \
    --in-cell-xy       /data/cell_metadata.csv \
    --in-cell-boundary /data/cell_boundaries.csv \
    --id MYSAMPLE --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 24

Or point at a standard export directory:

cartloader run_together --platform merfish --in-dir /data/MYSAMPLE --out-dir OUT

--in-dir auto-detects the transcript file (detected_transcripts.csv[.gz], else transcripts.csv[.gz]), cell_metadata.csv, cell_boundaries.csv, and cell_by_gene.csv. The sample id is rep1 (packaged as OUT/cartl/<OUT basename>-rep1/) unless --id is given.

Only a transcript source is required; with just it, the run is pixel-level (FICTURE → packaging). Adding a cell-count source (below) enables cell-level decode.

docs.title: 2. Multi-sample (sample sheet)
docs.text:
For standard directories, one in_dir per row; a per-row role column overrides an auto-detected file:

id      in_dir              raw_transcript           cell_boundary                cellxgene
s1      /data/s1
s2      /data/s2                                     /data/s2/bounds.csv
s3                          /data/s3/tx.csv.gz                                    /data/s3/cell_by_gene.csv

cartloader run_together --platform merfish --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT \
    --width 12 --n-factor 24 -j 8

Every sample needs a transcript source: a sample with no in_dir (like s3) gives raw_transcript (or an already-ingested transcript) plus its role columns explicitly; otherwise the run stops before planning.

docs.title: 3. Full config (JSON)
docs.text:
// run.json
{
  "platform": "merfish", "out_dir": "OUT",
  "resources": { "n_jobs": 8, "threads": 16 },
  "samples": [
    { "id": "s1", "in_dir": "/data/s1" },
    { "id": "s2", "raw_transcript": "/data/s2/tx.csv", "cellxgene": "/data/s2/cell_by_gene.csv", "xy": "/data/s2/meta.csv" }
  ],
  "ficture": [ { "id": "denovo", "mode": "train", "width": "12", "n_factor": "12,24,48" } ]
}

docs.title: Cell-level analysis: three sources
docs.text:
MERSCOPE transcripts carry no per-transcript cell assignment, so cell identity comes from one of three sources. Cell analysis runs when any is present:

Source How it works Column / flag Cell boundaries After sge_convert, ingest runs spatula tsv-add-cell-id to assign each transcript to the polygon that contains it (point-in-polygon; transcripts inside no cell → UNASSIGNED), appending a cell_id column. Cells are then clustered from those per-transcript counts. boundaries Cell×gene matrix cell_by_gene.csv is converted to a MEX directory (cartloader convert_cellxgene); cells are clustered directly from that matrix. Works without boundaries. cellxgene Existing cell_id column (rare) If the transcript CSV already carries a cell-id column, name it with --colname-transcript-cell <name>; it is carried to transcript column 5 and used directly (no tsv-add-cell-id). --colname-transcript-cell

--in-cell-xy / xy adds the per-cell spatial cluster scatter (and cell coordinates for MEX-based clustering).

docs.title: Source precedence
docs.text:
When more than one source is present, the clustering source order is:

cellxgene MEX → transcript cell_id → boundary-derived

  • A cellxgene MEX, when present, always drives clustering (even alongside boundaries).
  • Boundaries, when present, are still used to render cell polygons, regardless of which source drives clustering.
  • --colname-transcript-cell skips tsv-add-cell-id but does not override a cellxgene MEX.

docs.title: Mixed joint runs
docs.text:
A joint run may mix sources across samples — e.g. some samples with boundaries, some with only a cell_by_gene.csv. Each sample's cell-count source is resolved per sample, and all are decoded against the shared model and packaged from one call:

id      in_dir              cell_boundary          cellxgene
sA      /data/sA            /data/sA/bounds.csv
sB      /data/sB                                   /data/sB/cell_by_gene.csv
sC      /data/sC            /data/sC/bounds.csv    /data/sC/cell_by_gene.csv

Here sA clusters from boundaries, sB and sC from their MEX (with sC's boundaries still rendering polygons) — assuming the directories hold no other auto-detected files (a cell_by_gene.csv inside sA's in_dir would be picked up too).

Nearest-cell fallback

Assign an outside-all-cells transcript to the closest cell within a distance with { "ingest": { "assign_cell_id": { "expand_um": <µm> } } } (boundary-based decode only).

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
MERSCOPE morphology images (DAPI, protein, poly-T, …) have non-standard paths and need the mosaic transform, so declare them explicitly as TIFFs (e.g. images/mosaic_DAPI_z3.tif with images/micron_to_mosaic_pixel_transform.csv). The MERSCOPE transform column is merfish_csv → import_image --micron2pixel-csv; the profile applies --shrink-factor 5.0 --high-memory for the large mosaics.

Image sheet (--images images.tsv):

sample    type      source            merfish_csv           color
MYSAMPLE  dapi      /p/dapi.tif       /p/transform.csv      -
MYSAMPLE  protein   /p/protein.tif    /p/transform.csv      008A00

Or inline for a single sample:

cartloader run_together --platform merfish \
  --raw-transcript /p/molecules.csv --in-cell-boundary /p/polys.csv \
  --image type=dapi,source=/p/dapi.tif,merfish_csv=/p/transform.csv \
  --image type=protein,source=/p/protein.tif,color=008A00,transform=/p/transform.csv \
  --id MYSAMPLE --out-dir OUT

See Image Modalities for the full field set and type registry (dapi, protein, polyt, cellbound1..3, hne, …).

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• Specifying Inputs · Image Modalities · Overview
  • Starter tutorial: MERSCOPE

docs.title: Platform: Seq-Scope (--platform seqscope)
docs.text:
Built-in profile for Seq-Scope. The usual input is a MEX triple (barcodes.tsv.gz, features.tsv.gz, matrix.mtx.gz) in the Seq-Scope dialect: the barcode file carries the spatial coordinates, and the feature file and matrix carry five count columns per entry instead of one. sge_convert --platform seqscope (via spatula convert-sge) reads that dialect; this profile wires it into the end-to-end run. A raw per-molecule TSV can be ingested instead with --raw-transcript.

Seq-Scope has no cell segmentation, so the run is pixel-level throughout: ingest → FICTURE → packaging (+ histology). No cell analysis stage is planned or expected.

docs.title: Expected inputs
docs.text:
--in-dir is the MEX directory itself — there is no standard parent layout to search:

File in --in-dir Contents barcodes.tsv.gz barcode, index, …, X (col 6), Y (col 7), counts — coordinates in nanometers features.tsv.gz gene_id, gene_name, index, counts matrix.mtx.gz MatrixMarket with 5 count columns: gn, gt, spl, unspl, ambig

Alternatively, --raw-transcript / a raw_transcript column names a raw per-molecule TSV (header #lane tile X Y gene_id gene gn gt spl unspl ambig, coordinates in nanometers), which sge_convert ingests through its CSV route (--in-csv) instead of the MEX; --in-dir is then not needed. An already-ingested transcript can be given with --in-transcript.

Histology has no standard filename, so it is always given explicitly with --image (see Images).

Defaults: ingest with --units-per-um 1000 (nm → µm), --icols-mtx 2 (the gene-exon count), --sge-visual; FICTURE width=12, n_factor=24,48,96, single-molecule mode; packaging with --use-pmpoint --bin-count 500.

docs.title: 1. Single sample
docs.text:
cartloader run_together --platform seqscope \
    --in-dir /data/seqscope/sample1/mex \
    --out-dir OUT \
    --image type=hne,source=/data/seqscope/sample1/HE.tif \
    --width 12 --n-factor 24

The sample id defaults to rep1, so the packaged directory is OUT/cartl/<OUT basename>-rep1/; override with --id.

From the raw per-molecule TSV instead:

cartloader run_together --platform seqscope \
    --raw-transcript /data/seqscope/sample1/molecules.tsv.gz \
    --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 24

docs.title: 2. Multi-sample (sample sheet)
docs.text:
Each row's in_dir is that sample's MEX directory (or give raw_transcript). Images come from a separate --images TSV keyed by sample:

samples.tsv

id     in_dir
liver1 /data/seqscope/liver1/mex
liver2 /data/seqscope/liver2/mex

images.tsv

sample type source
liver1 hne  /data/seqscope/liver1/HE.tif
liver2 hne  /data/seqscope/liver2/HE.tif

cartloader run_together --platform seqscope \
    --samples samples.tsv --images images.tsv --out-dir OUT -j 8

docs.title: Hosting without FICTURE
docs.text:
Seq-Scope datasets are often published without factor analysis. Add --no-ficture to any of the commands above:

cartloader run_together --platform seqscope --in-dir /data/mex --out-dir OUT --no-ficture \
    --image type=hne,source=/data/HE.tif

Only FICTURE's tiling step runs; the packaged output carries the transcript points, the SGE raster basemap, and the histology, with no factor layers. Nothing about this is Seq-Scope specific — it works on every platform. See FICTURE mode.

docs.title: Hexagon-binned 10x MEX files
docs.text:
To also get the hexagon-binned counts as 10x MEX directories (for Seurat/Scanpy-style downstream analysis), add --segment-10x, optionally with the widths to export:

cartloader run_together --platform seqscope --in-dir /data/mex --out-dir OUT --no-ficture \
    --segment-10x --segment-width-10x 12,24

For a wide hexagon (roughly --width above 40), also raise the tiling size — punkst rejects a tile under 20× the hexagon side length and recommends 50–100× — e.g. --width 100 --tile-size 5000 (config: "tile_size": 5000). Each sample and width yields OUT/fic/samples/<id>/<id>.hex_<width>.mex/ with barcodes.tsv.gz (hexagon centers as x:y, µm), features.tsv.gz, and matrix.mtx.gz. These are converted from the same hexagon files FICTURE trains on (after --min-ct-per-unit-hexagon, default 50), so they match the factor analysis exactly; without --segment-width-10x every --width is exported. Works together with a full FICTURE run too. Config equivalent: "segment_10x": true or { "widths": "12,24" }.

docs.title: Coordinates and count columns
docs.text:
Barcode X/Y are in nanometers, so the profile's ingest.extra_flags pass --units-per-um 1000 to sge_convert. Columns 6 and 7 of barcodes.tsv.gz are read as X and Y (the sge_convert defaults --icol-bcd-x 6 --icol-bcd-y 7).

The matrix's five count columns are, in order, gn, gt, spl, unspl, ambig. The profile selects column 2 (--icols-mtx 2), the gene-exon count, and names it count in the output.

These settings live in ingest.extra_flags, which come last on the sge_convert command line, so --units-per-um on the CLI (or ingest.units_per_um) has no effect here — the profile's --units-per-um 1000 takes precedence. To change any of them, replace the list in a --config (a list is replaced whole, so restate every flag you want to keep):

{ "ingest": { "extra_flags": ["--units-per-um 1000", "--icols-mtx 2", "--icol-bcd-x 5", "--icol-bcd-y 6", "--sge-visual"] } }

To quantify on a different count column — e.g. total gene counts (gn) — set --icols-mtx 1 the same way.

On the raw-TSV route (--raw-transcript), --icols-mtx does not apply: the count column defaults to gn (sge_convert's Seq-Scope TSV preset), so pass --colname-transcript-count gt to count the gene-exon column, as the MEX route does.

Barcodes whose features do not match the feature file are dropped by sge_drop_mismatches after conversion (the sge_convert default for this platform).

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
Seq-Scope histology is typically an H&E TIF that has already been georeferenced — it carries its own geotransform, aligned to the transcript frame, but usually no CRS. The profile therefore sets image_defaults.georeferenced = true: the corner coordinates are kept as they are and only the CRS is assigned:

cartloader image_png2pmtiles --in-img HE.tif --out-prefix .../hne \
    --geotif2mbtiles --mbtiles2pmtiles --georeference --georef-detect gtiff

No bounds are synthesized, so --um-per-pixel / --georef-plain do not apply. If a particular image is not already georeferenced, opt it out per image and state its scale instead:

--image type=hne,source=/data/HE_plain.tif,georeferenced=false,georef_plain=true,um_per_pixel=0.5

Single-channel modalities (e.g. type=dapi) are colorized through import_image on the usual path and are not covered by georeferenced; give them a scale with um_per_pixel.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • Specifying Inputs · Image Modalities · Overview

docs.title: Platform: BGI Stereo-seq (--platform stereoseq)
docs.text:
Built-in profile for BGI Stereo-seq / SAW output. Unlike every other platform, the inputs are binary GEF files that only SAW can read, so this profile shells out to the SAW binary (--saw) to expand them into text GEMs before the ordinary ingest runs.

Because a SAW sample is a set of files sharing a name prefix rather than a directory layout, this platform is addressed with --in-prefix instead of --in-dir.

docs.title: Expected inputs
docs.text:
All resolved by suffixing --in-prefix; each is optional except the tissue GEF.

Role File (auto-detected from --in-prefix) Column Purpose Tissue GEF {prefix}.tissue.gef gef Required. Pixel-level transcripts Cell-bin GEF {prefix}.cellbin.gef cellbin_gef Cell segmentation; enables cell-level analysis H&E {prefix}_HE_regist.tif --image Registered RGB histology ssDNA {prefix}_ssDNA_regist.tif --image Registered single-channel histology DAPI {prefix}_DAPI_regist.tif --image Registered single-channel histology

Missing files are simply skipped. Naming is not always consistent across SAW versions — when a file does not match, give it explicitly (--image type=hne,source=/p/whatever.tif, or a gef / cellbin_gef sample-sheet column), which always wins over auto-detection.

Defaults: FICTURE width=12, n_factor=12,24,48, single-molecule mode; packaging with --use-pmpoint --bin-count 500; histology at 0.5 µm/pixel.

docs.title: 1. Single sample
docs.text:
cartloader run_together --platform stereoseq \
    --saw /path/to/saw \
    --in-prefix /data/C04687E314 \
    --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 24

With --out-dir, the lone sample's id defaults to rep1 (packaged as OUT/cartl/<OUT basename>-rep1/); override with --id. With --out-root, or for a joint run's samples without an id, it defaults to the prefix basename (C04687E314).

docs.title: 2. Multi-sample (sample sheet)
docs.text:
id            in_prefix                  cellbin_gef
C04687E314    /data/C04687E314
Y40320NA      /data/chipB/Y40320NA       /data/alt/Y40320NA.cellbin.gef

cartloader run_together --platform stereoseq --saw /path/to/saw \
    --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT -j 8

docs.title: Counts and gene names
docs.text:
Both ingests read ExonCount (the exonic subset of the MIDs), not MIDCount, and rows with a zero count are dropped — a large share of rows, since many MIDs have no exonic overlap.

The count column is resolved by name, not position

ExonCount is the last column of the bin1 GEM but not of the cell-bin GEM, where CellID follows it. A positional filter (grep -v -w 0$) is therefore wrong on cellbin in both directions: it keeps zero-count rows whose CellID is non-zero, and discards real counts whose CellID is 0. Both ingests read the header and select the named column, so layout differences between GEM variants are handled. A CellID of 0 is preserved and treated as unassigned later by pixel2sptsv --ignore-ids.

Features are read from geneName (the gene symbol), not geneID (Ensembl id). Symbols are what CartoScope displays, and they are what the exclude-feature regexes are written against — Gm[0-9], mt-, Rps, Rpl match nothing at all against Ensembl ids, so using geneID would silently disable that filtering.

Override both together if a GEM variant differs:

{ "ingest": { "csv_colnames": { "feature": "geneID", "count": "MIDCount" } } }

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text:
Stereo-seq GEM coordinates are on a 0.5 µm grid, so ingest passes --units-per-um 2 to convert them to microns. The registered histology is at the same 0.5 µm/pixel, so it is georeferenced with --px-per-um-x/y 2 (single-channel) or --um-per-pixel 0.5 (RGB) and lands in the same frame with no further transform.

The GEM #OffsetX / #OffsetY headers are not applied by either conversion. The cell-bin conversion (convert_stereoseq_cellbin) stops on a non-zero offset rather than producing cells shifted relative to the transcripts and histology; the bin1 conversion (sge_convert) skips the # header lines without checking them. convert_stereoseq_cellbin has an --allow-offset override, but run_together has no way to pass it. Instead, re-export without the offset, or run the conversion yourself and supply the result as cell_tsv (see Skipping SAW).

docs.title: Ingest: what SAW is run for
docs.text:
Two conversions, each deleted as soon as it has been read — the GEMs are tens of GB of text:

# pixel-level transcripts -> the FICTURE transcript
saw convert gef2gem --bin-size 1 --gef {prefix}.tissue.gef --gem bin1.gem

# cell segmentation -> the cell-level counts
saw convert gef2gem --cellbin-gef {prefix}.cellbin.gef \
                    --gef {prefix}.tissue.gef --cellbin-gem cellbin.gem

Re-running ingest re-runs SAW

The GEMs are removed after ingest, so --restart (or deleting mk/sge.*.done) pays the SAW conversion again. Use --skip ingest to resume from a completed ingest.

docs.title: Skipping SAW: supplying pre-processed inputs
docs.text:
To test alternative filtering, or when SAW output is already on hand, you can bypass the GEFs (and SAW) entirely and feed the pipeline the two files ingest would otherwise produce. Provide them as roles in a --samples sheet or a --config JSON, or for a single sample with --in-transcript plus a --list-cell-tsv file; --saw is then not required.

Role Replaces Format transcript (alias tsv) tissue.gef → bin1 gzipped TSV with header X<TAB>Y<TAB>gene<TAB>count, coordinates in µm (i.e. already divided by 2). Skips ingest, so no feature filtering / scaling is applied — do it yourself. cell_tsv cellbin.gef TSV with a header row X Y gene count cell_id (µm; columns read by name). This is exactly what convert_stereoseq_cellbin emits; it feeds run_ficture2_multi_cells --tsv-list. 
id    transcript                 cell_tsv
C1    /data/C1.tx.tsv.gz         /data/C1.cells.tsv

cartloader run_together --platform stereoseq --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 24

The single-sample equivalent, where cells.list holds one line C1<TAB>/data/C1.cells.tsv (its first column must be the run's sample id):

cartloader run_together --platform stereoseq \
    --in-transcript /data/C1.tx.tsv.gz --list-cell-tsv cells.list \
    --id C1 --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 24

Giving a transcript role skips all ingest for that sample, including the cell-bin conversion — so pair it with an explicit cell_tsv if you want cell analysis (a cellbin_gef is ignored once transcript is present). Omit cell_tsv for a pixel-only run. Mixing is fine: some samples from GEFs (with --saw), others from pre-processed roles, in one sheet.

docs.title: Cell-level analysis
docs.text:
Stereo-seq is the one platform where cell identity cannot be attached to the pixel-level transcript: the cell-bin GEM's rows cannot be mapped back onto the bin1 GEM. So instead of a cell_id column on the transcript, the cell-bin GEM becomes a standalone pixel TSV:

cartloader convert_stereoseq_cellbin   # cellbin.gem -> X, Y, gene, count, cell_id

which the cells stage passes to run_ficture2_multi_cells --tsv-list. Cells are clustered from that file (spatula pixel2sptsv), and the resulting clusters are projected back onto all bin1 pixels by the pixel decode. Cell centroids come from the same step, so no separate cell-metadata file is needed. There are no cell polygons, so no cell boundaries are rendered.

Cell analysis runs only when {prefix}.cellbin.gef is present; without it the run is pixel-level (FICTURE → packaging).

Feature naming must match between the two GEMs

The cell clusters are projected onto a model trained from the bin1 features. If the two GEMs name genes differently (geneID vs geneName, Ensembl id vs symbol), the projection yields near-empty cells rather than an error. The converter therefore checks its features against the pixel run's feature file and fails the run if fewer than 50% overlap. Both ingests read geneName by default; to switch, set both together:

{ "ingest": { "csv_colnames": { "feature": "geneID" } } }

docs.title: Images
docs.text:
The registered TIFs are plain (non-OME) TIFFs with no pixel-size metadata, so the scale is stated rather than detected. The profile handles the three standard suffixes automatically; declare anything else explicitly:

cartloader run_together --platform stereoseq --saw /path/to/saw \
  --in-prefix /data/C04687E314 --out-dir OUT \
  --image type=hne,source=/data/odd_name_HE.tif,um_per_pixel=0.5,georef_plain=true

Override the scale per image with um_per_pixel when a TIF is at a different resolution (e.g. um_per_pixel=1.0 for a 2× downsampled export).

The profile's image_defaults.um_per_pixel = 0.5 applies to single-channel images only (ssDNA, DAPI). An H&E (rgb) given with --image / --images must state georef_plain=true and um_per_pixel itself, as above, or the import stops for lack of bounds. A sample-sheet hne column cannot carry these fields, so a plain-TIFF H&E given that way stops the same way.

16-bit H&E TIFs need a rescale range

Some SAW versions export the registered H&E as 16-bit RGB (e.g. the V1.2 *_HE_regist.tif). geotiff2pmtiles rejects 16-bit input without an explicit value range, and the pipeline fails at the tiling step (the error may surface as a misleading possibly OOM-killed message). Supply a linear rescale — the range is given as rescale_min + rescale_max on a --image value (they survive the comma split; a --images TSV or config can use rescale_range directly):

--image "type=hne,source=/data/HE_regist.tif,um_per_pixel=0.5,georef_plain=true,rescale=linear,rescale_min=0,rescale_max=65535"

0,65535 maps the full 16-bit range; if the H&E then looks washed out, read the true per-band range with gdalinfo -stats and pass that instead. 8-bit H&E (e.g. the V1.3 eyeball demo) needs none of this.

docs.title: See also
docs.text: • Specifying Inputs · Image Modalities · Overview

docs.title: Platform: 10x Visium HD (--platform 10x_visium_hd)
docs.text: Built-in profile. Ingest runs sge_convert on the 2 µm bins. Point --in-dir at the Space Ranger outs/ directory. Bin positions are converted to µm with microns_per_pixel from the 2 µm scalefactors_json.json; the profile's scale settings only set the resolution of the rendered raster images (2 µm per pixel), not the coordinates.

docs.title: Expected inputs (under --in-dir)
docs.text:
Purpose Path under --in-dir Used by Scale factors binned_outputs/square_002um/spatial/scalefactors_json.json ingest (--scale-json); H&E scale; centroid scaling Count matrix binned_outputs/square_002um/filtered_feature_bc_matrix/ ingest (--in-mex) Bin positions binned_outputs/square_002um/spatial/tissue_positions.parquet ingest (--pos-parquet) Square layers binned_outputs/square_008um, binned_outputs/square_016um spaceranger-sq008, spaceranger-sq016 layers (imported if present) Segmented cells segmented_outputs/ spaceranger cell layer (imported if present) Segmented cell matrix segmented_outputs/filtered_feature_cell_matrix (mex role) cartloader cell analysis Segmented cell polygons segmented_outputs/cell_segmentations.geojson (boundaries role) cartloader cell analysis (optional) H&E image not auto-detected: the sample's hne column / config key hne layer

Defaults: FICTURE width=12, n_factor=24,48,96, single-molecule mode, decode_scale=2; packaging with --use-pmpoint --bin-count 500 --sge-scale 2; sge_convert with --sge-visual --scale-xy 2.0. These three scale settings render the ingest preview (xy.png), the FICTURE pixel-decode images, and the packaged SGE raster at 2 µm per pixel.

docs.title: Cell layers
docs.text:
Two cell-level layers can come out of a Space Ranger run that includes segmentation:

Layer What it is Runs when spaceranger Space Ranger's own segmented cells and clusters, imported by import_visiumhd_cell in the images stage segmented_outputs/ exists cartloader Cells clustered from the segmented cell matrix and decoded against the FICTURE model by run_ficture2_multi_cells the sample has the segmented cell matrix (mex role); on a joint run, every sample must have it (require_all)

For the cartloader analysis, cell centroids are derived from cell_segmentations.geojson when it is present: the polygon ids (property cell_id) are formatted as cellid_{:09d}-1 to match the matrix barcodes and rescaled to µm with microns_per_pixel from the scale factors JSON. Its polygons are not rendered by this analysis (the spaceranger layer renders them).

The square layers (spaceranger-sq008, spaceranger-sq016) are imported by import_visiumhd_square when those directories exist.

docs.title: 1. Single sample (direct CLI)
docs.text:
cartloader run_together --platform 10x_visium_hd \
    --in-dir /data/visiumhd/sample/outs --out-dir OUT \
    --width 12 --n-factor 48 -j 8 --threads 8

Square (8/16 µm) and cell layers are added automatically when present. The bins sit on a 2 µm lattice; --jitter-xy 0.8 spreads each bin's molecules across the bin (see Coordinate jitter).

H&E is not inside the standard bin layout, so name it in the sample's hne field — for a single sample, a one-row sample sheet:

in_dir                         hne
/data/visiumhd/sample/outs     /data/visiumhd/sample/he.tif

cartloader run_together --platform 10x_visium_hd \
    --samples sample.tsv --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 48

Without an id column the lone sample is rep1, exactly as with --in-dir. Give the hne path as absolute (it is not resolved against in_dir).

--image type=hne does not use the scale factors

An H&E given through --image or --images is an ordinary rgb image: it does not read scalefactors_json.json, so it needs its own bounds (georef_plain=true,um_per_pixel=<µm per pixel>), or the image import stops with an error. Only the sample's hne field gets the profile's H&E handling.

docs.title: 2. Multi-sample (sample sheet)
docs.text:
One joint model; add a per-sample hne column for the H&E layer:

cartloader run_together --platform 10x_visium_hd \
    --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT --width 12 --n-factor 48 -j 8

id      in_dir                       hne
s1      /data/visiumhd/s1/outs       /data/visiumhd/s1/he.tif
s2      /data/visiumhd/s2/outs       /data/visiumhd/s2/he.tif

docs.title: 3. Full config (JSON)
docs.text:
cartloader run_together --platform 10x_visium_hd --config run.json

// run.json
{
  "platform": "10x_visium_hd", "out_dir": "OUT",
  "resources": { "n_jobs": 8, "threads": 16 },
  "samples": [
    { "id": "s1", "in_dir": "/data/visiumhd/s1/outs", "hne": "/data/visiumhd/s1/he.tif" },
    { "id": "s2", "in_dir": "/data/visiumhd/s2/outs", "hne": "/data/visiumhd/s2/he.tif" }
  ],
  "ficture": [ { "id": "denovo", "mode": "train", "width": "12", "n_factor": "24,48,96" } ]
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• H&E is an rgb (passthrough) image imported as the hne layer with --georef-plain: its upper-left corner is placed at (0,0) and its scale is microns_per_pixel from the 2 µm scalefactors_json.json (read with jq at run time). See Image Modalities.
  • Square (8/16 µm) and spaceranger cell imports are wired by the profile's squares / cell_import blocks and appended to the catalog when the directories exist.

docs.title: Platform: 10x Xenium (--platform 10x_xenium)
docs.text: Built-in profile. Ingest runs sge_convert. Point --in-dir at a Xenium Ranger output directory and the profile auto-detects everything below.

docs.title: Expected inputs (under --in-dir)
docs.text:
First match wins where several paths are listed; optional files are skipped when absent.

Purpose Path under --in-dir Transcripts transcripts.csv.gz, or transcripts.parquet, or transcripts/transcripts.parquet Cell boundaries cell_boundaries.csv.gz Cell centroids cells.csv.gz (columns x_centroid, y_centroid) Cluster labels analysis/clustering/gene_expression_graphclust/clusters.csv → the xeniumranger factor Morphology images morphology_focus/morphology_focus_000{0,1,2,3}.ome.tif → dapi/boundary/rna/protein; or a single morphology_focus.ome.tif / morphology.ome.tif → dapi

Defaults: FICTURE width=12, n_factor=12,24,48, single-molecule mode; packaging with --use-pmpoint --bin-count 500. Two cell analyses are wired: cartloader (jointly-decoded factors from boundaries + xy) and xeniumranger (the Ranger clusters.csv).

docs.title: 1. Single sample (direct CLI)
docs.text:
cartloader run_together --platform 10x_xenium \
    --in-dir /data/xenium_lung --out-dir OUT \
    --width 18 --n-factor 24 -j 8 --threads 8

Morphology images are auto-detected — nothing to list. Everything (transcripts, boundaries, centroids, clusters, images) comes from the directory. The sample id is rep1, so the packaged directory is OUT/cartl/<OUT basename>-rep1/; set --id to name it.

docs.title: 2. Multi-sample (sample sheet)
docs.text:
One joint FICTURE model across sections sharing --out-dir. For standard Ranger directories you only need id + in_dir:

cartloader run_together --platform 10x_xenium \
    --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT --width 18 --n-factor 24 -j 10

id      in_dir
rep1    /data/xenium/rep1/outs
rep2    /data/xenium/rep2/outs

GEO-style layouts (non-standard filenames / scattered paths) — name each file per role with sheet columns. The raw transcript goes in raw_transcript (it still needs ingest; the transcript column is for an already-ingested TSV and skips ingest). Role paths are forwarded to the per-sample cell import as --csv-* overrides:

id      raw_transcript                xy                     boundaries               clusters                dapi
rep1    /geo/rep1_transcripts.csv.gz  /geo/rep1_cells.csv.gz /geo/rep1_bounds.csv.gz  /geo/rep1_clusters.csv  /geo/rep1_morphology.ome.tif
rep2    /geo/rep2_transcripts.parquet /geo/rep2_cells.parquet /geo/rep2_bounds.parquet -                       /geo/rep2_morphology_focus.ome.tif
  • Parquet is fine. transcripts.parquet, cells.parquet and cell_boundaries.parquet are converted to .csv.gz (OUT/tsv/<id>/parquet2csv/) as the first ingest step, with a NOTE: at planning time; the run aborts if a conversion fails.
  • No clusters? The xeniumranger import (Ranger's own clusters) needs clusters; a sample without it — as a column, or as analysis/clustering/gene_expression_graphclust/clusters.csv under in_dir — simply skips that import (a NOTE: says so). The cartloader analysis (clustering recomputed on the shared SGE) needs only xy + boundaries and still runs.
  • DAPI. A per-sample dapi column takes the image (an OME-TIFF) directly. A file ending in morphology.ome.tif (any prefix) is the multi-page z-stack and is imported with --use-middle-page --high-memory automatically; morphology_focus.ome.tif is the 2D projection and needs nothing special. See Image Modalities.

docs.title: 3. Full config (JSON)
docs.text:
Use --config when samples differ or to add analyses/images. Example: de-novo base on the CLI, plus a projection model and an extra protein image.

cartloader run_together --platform 10x_xenium --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT \
    --width 18 --n-factor 24 --config extra.json -j 10

// extra.json
{
  "ficture": [ { "id": "ref", "mode": "project", "model": "/models/ref.tsv", "width": 12 } ],
  "images":  [ { "id": "cd3", "source": "cd3.ome.tif", "kind": "single", "color": "FF0000" } ]
}

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Xenium Ranger clusters on joint runs. The xeniumranger analysis relies on sample-specific cluster labels, so it cannot be jointly decoded: a single-sample run decodes it via run_ficture2_multi_cells, but a joint run imports each sample's clusters per-sample via import_xenium_cell (appended to that sample's catalog). The cartloader factor, whose clustering is recomputed on the shared SGE, is decoded jointly in both cases.
  • Images: the morphology_focus_000{0..3} channels map to dapi/boundary/rna/protein. To recolor or add channels, see Image Modalities.
