docs.title: Human Cortex Multi‑Sample Spatial Factor Analysis Tutorial
docs.text:
This tutorial demonstrates how to run multi‑sample FICTURE analysis and package results with individual commands, starting from the raw data.

Question

  • Why use Multi‑Sample FICTURE Analysis?

Prefer one command?

run_together runs this whole analysis (SGE conversion, one joint FICTURE model, and packaging) from a sample sheet. After downloading the data, from ${work_dir}:

sample_ids=(FB080_O1a FB080_O1b FB080_O1c FB080_O1d FB121_O1)
printf "id\traw_transcript\n" > samples.tsv
for s in "${sample_ids[@]}"; do
  printf "%s\traw/%s/detected_transcripts.csv\n" "${s}" "${s}" >> samples.tsv
done

cartloader run_together \
  --platform merfish \
  --samples samples.tsv \
  --out-dir ./out/walsh2025-human-cortex-fb080-O1 \
  --width 24 \
  --n-factor 96,192 \
  --threads 10 -j 10

With Docker, run the same command as docker run --rm -v ${work_dir}:/data -w /data hyunminkang/cartloader:latest run_together ...; -w /data makes the sheet's relative paths resolve inside the container.

Each sample is packaged as out/walsh2025-human-cortex-fb080-O1/cartl/walsh2025-human-cortex-fb080-O1-<sample_id>/, next to a multi-catalog.yaml that links them; --s3-upload publishes the whole collection. Its default feature filters differ slightly from the commands below: Blank-* probes are dropped at ingest, and MT- genes are left out of the factor models.

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text: This tutorial uses a series of five human cortex ST datasets from Walsh et al. Nature 2025, generated by MERFISH.

docs.title: Data Access
docs.text:
Follow the commands below to download the source data (about 8 GB to download and 29 GB unzipped).

# Define the work directory
work_dir=/path/to/work/directory
mkdir -p ${work_dir}/raw
cd ${work_dir}/raw

sample_ids=(FB080_O1a FB080_O1b FB080_O1c FB080_O1d FB121_O1)
for s in "${sample_ids[@]}"; do
  wget -O ${s}.zip "https://zenodo.org/records/15127709/files/${s}.zip?download=1"
done

# The FB080_O1* archives hold their files at the top level; FB121_O1 has its own folder
for s in FB080_O1a FB080_O1b FB080_O1c FB080_O1d; do
  unzip ${s}.zip -d ${s}
done
unzip FB121_O1.zip -x '__MACOSX/*'

Each sample then has its own folder, raw/<sample_id>/, holding detected_transcripts.csv, cell_metadata.csv, and cell_by_gene.csv.

docs.title: File Format
docs.text:
detected_transcripts.csv

,barcode_id,global_x,global_y,global_z,x,y,fov,gene,transcript_id,cell_id
36,0,154.75854,8197.335,0.0,1790.1895,303.81055,0,HS3ST1,ENST00000002596,224295401131100634
53,0,157.40007,8211.97,0.0,1814.648,439.31885,0,HS3ST1,ENST00000002596,-1
76,0,154.28473,8230.835,0.0,1785.8022,614.0,0,HS3ST1,ENST00000002596,224295401131100700
  • Column 1: Unique numeric index for each transcript within a field of view (non-consecutive, ascending).
  • barcode_id: Zero-based index of the transcript barcode in the codebook; forms a composite key with fov.
  • global_x: Transcript x coordinates (µm) in the experimental region; may be negative due to alignment.
  • global_y: Transcript y coordinates (µm) in the experimental region; may be negative due to alignment.
  • global_z: Zero‑based z‑position index.
  • x: The x-coordinate of the transcript (µm), within the coordinate space of the field of view.
  • y: The y-coordinate of the transcript (µm), within the coordinate space of the field of view.
  • fov: Zero-based field of view index; forms a composite key with barcode_id.
  • gene: Gene name.
  • transcript_id: Unique identifier for the transcript.
  • cell_id: Unique identifier for cell.

docs.title: Define ID and Parameters
docs.text:
cd $work_dir
# Unique identifier for your collection
COLLECTION_ID="walsh2025-human-cortex-fb080-O1" # change this to reflect your dataset name
sample_ids=(FB080_O1a FB080_O1b FB080_O1c FB080_O1d FB121_O1)

# LDA parameters
train_width=24                           # define LDA training hexagon width (comma-separated if multiple widths are applied)
n_factor=96,192                          # define number of factors in LDA training (comma-separated if multiple n-factor values are provided)

The raw coordinates are already in µm, so no scaling is needed.

docs.title: Choose Local or Docker Setup
docs.text:
Choose One Mode

This tutorial supports two execution modes:

  • local runs (cartloader installed on your machine)
  • Docker runs (docker run hyunminkang/cartloader:latest ...)

Choose one setup mode and complete that setup only.

After setup, both modes use the same pipeline commands via the cartloader_cmd and aws_cmd wrappers.

Set Up Local RunsSet Up Docker Run

Set Up Environment

# ====
# Replace the placeholders with values for your system.
# ====
work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # directory holding the input data; outputs are written here too
cd $work_dir

n_jobs=10                               # number of parallel jobs (also used as threads per job below)

# Activate the Python environment in which CartLoader is installed
conda activate ENV_NAME                 # replace ENV_NAME (or: source /path/to/venv/bin/activate)

No tool paths needed

Once submodules/build.sh has run (see Installation), every CartLoader command finds spatula, punkst, tippecanoe, pmtiles, and pmpoint in the submodules/ directory of the repository, and the default color map at assets/default_color_map.tsv. Pass --spatula, --ficture2 (the punkst repository directory, which contains bin/punkst), --tippecanoe, --pmtiles, or --cmap-file only to use a different build or file. upload_aws runs the aws CLI from your PATH (--aws to override).

Define command wrappers

# The work directory as the tools see it
data_root="${work_dir}"

# Use the same command shape as Docker mode
cartloader_cmd() { cartloader "$@"; }
aws_cmd() { aws "$@"; }

Set Up Environment

# ====
# Replace the placeholder with the actual path on your system.
# ====
work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # directory holding the input data; mounted at /data in the container
cd $work_dir

n_jobs=10                               # number of parallel jobs (also used as threads per job below)

docker pull hyunminkang/cartloader:latest

Using the Docker image

  • The image's entry point is cartloader: whatever follows the image name is a cartloader subcommand and its options (docker run --rm -v ${work_dir}:/data hyunminkang/cartloader:latest <command> [options]).
  • Paths passed to the command are container paths: with -v ${work_dir}:/data, a host file ${work_dir}/raw/x.csv is /data/raw/x.csv.
  • Every tool is built into the image, so no tool-path options are needed.
  • Uploads need credentials inside the container: mount them read-only, e.g. -v ${HOME}/.aws:/root/.aws:ro for AWS.
  • latest is the most recent release; for reproducible runs use a dated tag (e.g. hyunminkang/cartloader:20261007-1432).

Define command wrappers

# The work directory as the tools see it: mounted at /data inside the container
data_root="/data"

# Use the same command shape as local mode.
# ~/.aws is mounted (read-only) for the upload step.
cartloader_cmd() {
  docker run --rm \
    -v "${work_dir}:/data" \
    -v "${HOME}/.aws:/root/.aws:ro" \
    hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
    "$@"
}
aws_cmd() {
  docker run --rm \
    -v "${work_dir}:/data" \
    -v "${HOME}/.aws:/root/.aws:ro" \
    --entrypoint aws \
    hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
    "$@"
}

Warning

All remaining commands are identical for local and Docker runs. Paths given to cartloader_cmd and aws_cmd start with ${data_root} (the work directory as the tools see it); plain shell commands, which run on your machine, use ${work_dir}.

docs.title: SGE Format Conversion
docs.text:
Warning

Convert each sample transcript file to CartLoader SGE format. Commands below process all five samples in a loop.

Recommended: sge_convertFast path: direct transform (no visualization/filtering) 
cd "${work_dir}"

for sample_id in "${sample_ids[@]}"; do
  cartloader_cmd sge_convert \
    --in-csv "${data_root}/raw/${sample_id}/detected_transcripts.csv" \
    --platform generic \
    --out-dir "${data_root}/sge/${sample_id}" \
    --csv-delim "," \
    --csv-colname-x global_x \
    --csv-colname-y global_y \
    --csv-colname-feature-name gene \
    --csv-colnames-others cell_id global_z \
    --sge-visual \
    --n-jobs "${n_jobs}"
done

Tip

Raw coordinates are already in micrometers. Use this only if you do not need SGE visualization or density/feature-based filtering. It runs directly in your shell, in either mode.

cd "${work_dir}"

for sample_id in "${sample_ids[@]}"; do
  mkdir -p "${work_dir}/sge/${sample_id}"
  (
    echo -e "X\tY\tgene\tcount\tcell_id\tZ"
    tail -n +2 "${work_dir}/raw/${sample_id}/detected_transcripts.csv" \
      | tr ',' '\t' \
      | perl -lane 'print join("\t",$F[2],$F[3],$F[8],1,$F[10],$F[4]);'
  ) | gzip > "${work_dir}/sge/${sample_id}/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz"
done

docs.title: Prepare Input List
docs.text:
Create input.tsv (tab-separated, one sample per line). The paths in it are read by run_ficture2_multi, so they start with ${data_root}.

cd "${work_dir}"

: > input.tsv
for sample_id in "${sample_ids[@]}"; do
  printf "%s\t%s/sge/%s/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz\n" \
    "${sample_id}" "${data_root}" "${sample_id}" >> input.tsv
done

cat input.tsv

Example Input List: input.tsv

The TSV has one sample per line, no header, and two columns (in Docker mode the paths begin with /data).

FB080_O1a    /path/to/work_dir/sge/FB080_O1a/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz
FB080_O1b    /path/to/work_dir/sge/FB080_O1b/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz
FB080_O1c    /path/to/work_dir/sge/FB080_O1c/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz
FB080_O1d    /path/to/work_dir/sge/FB080_O1d/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz
FB121_O1     /path/to/work_dir/sge/FB121_O1/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz
  • 1st Column (required, str): Unique sample identifier (avoid whitespace).
  • 2nd Column (required, str): Path to the transcript-indexed SGE file in CartLoader format, generated from the SGE format conversion step above.

docs.title: Multi-Sample FICTURE Analysis
docs.text:
Train cohort-level LDA models (per width and factor setting), decode each sample, and write the JSON manifests.

The shared models are written to ficture2/, each sample's results to ficture2/samples/<sample_id>/, and the manifest that links them to ficture2/ficture.multi.params.json. See details in run_ficture2_multi.

cartloader_cmd run_ficture2_multi \
  --in-list "${data_root}/input.tsv" \
  --out-dir "${data_root}/ficture2" \
  --width "${train_width}" \
  --n-factor "${n_factor}" \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(Blank-.*$)' \
  --threads "${n_jobs}" \
  --n-jobs "${n_jobs}"

docs.title: Multi-Sample Asset Packaging
docs.text:
Package every sample into web-ready PMTiles and catalogs. run_cartload2_multi finds the samples and the shared models in ficture2/ficture.multi.params.json, so it needs no input list.

Each sample is written to its own self-contained directory, cartload2/${COLLECTION_ID}-<sample_id>/ (with its catalog.yaml), and the shared factor files (model, colors, DE, UMAP) and multi-catalog.yaml, which links the samples, to cartload2/. See details in run_cartload2_multi.

cartloader_cmd run_cartload2_multi \
  --fic-dir "${data_root}/ficture2" \
  --out-dir "${data_root}/cartload2" \
  --id "${COLLECTION_ID}" \
  --threads "${n_jobs}" \
  --n-jobs "${n_jobs}"

docs.title: Upload to AWS
docs.text:
Upload each sample's directory, then multi-catalog.yaml and the shared files it lists, into one S3 directory for the collection. See upload_aws for options.

AWS_DIR=s3://your-bucket/${COLLECTION_ID}   # recommended: end with COLLECTION_ID

# 1. Each sample's packaged directory
for sample_id in "${sample_ids[@]}"; do
  cartloader_cmd upload_aws \
    --in-dir "${data_root}/cartload2/${COLLECTION_ID}-${sample_id}" \
    --s3-dir "${AWS_DIR}/${COLLECTION_ID}-${sample_id}" \
    --n-jobs "${n_jobs}"
done

# 2. multi-catalog.yaml and the shared files it lists (the names without a '/')
cd "${work_dir}/cartload2"
for f in multi-catalog.yaml $(grep -E '\.' multi-catalog.yaml | awk '{print $NF}' | grep -v / | sort -u); do
  aws_cmd s3 cp "${data_root}/cartload2/${f}" "${AWS_DIR}/${f}"
done

Each sample directory is self-contained, so to share a single sample, run only its upload_aws command.

docs.title: Output Summary
docs.text: See output details in the reference pages for run_ficture2_multi and run_cartload2_multi.

docs.title: View/Explore
docs.text:
The outputs are available in CartoScope.

Explore in CartoScope

docs.title: Step-by-step
docs.text:
run_together chains the CartLoader commands for you. This section is for running those commands yourself, one stage at a time.

When to run the individual commands

  • To learn what each stage does and what it produces.
  • To customize a stage beyond what run_together exposes (for example a parameter of run_ficture2 that has no run_together option).
  • To rerun or replace a single stage, or to combine CartLoader with your own tools.

For a standard run, use run_together: it applies platform defaults, runs the stages in the right order as one resumable Makefile, and packages the result for CartoScope.

docs.title: The Stages and Their Commands
docs.text:
Stage Command(s) What it does SGE conversion sge_convert, reformat_cosmx Converts raw platform output into the unified transcript format. SGE stitching and orientation sge_stitch, sge_orientate Combines tiles or sections into one SGE; rotates or flips coordinates. Spatial factors (FICTURE) run_ficture2, run_ficture2_multi Trains or projects FICTURE models and decodes pixels; _multi trains one model across samples. Cell analyses run_ficture2_multi_cells, import_cell, import_square Analyzes segmented cells, or imports platform cell and bin analyses (Xenium Ranger, Space Ranger). Background images import_image Converts DAPI, H&E, and other images into aligned PMTiles. Packaging run_cartload2, run_cartload2_multi Packages the SGE, factors, and cell layers into PMTiles with a catalog.yaml. Publishing upload_aws, upload_zenodo Uploads a packaged directory to S3 or Zenodo. AI annotation anno_cartload_folder, annotate_factors_with_llm Labels factors and cell clusters with an LLM.

run_together uses the multi-sample commands (run_ficture2_multi, run_ficture2_multi_cells) even for a single sample, so its outputs follow their layout. The single-sample run_ficture2 and run_cartload2 remain available for step-by-step use.

docs.title: Walkthroughs
docs.text:
• Per platform: each platform tutorial has a "step by step" part that runs sge_convert → run_ficture2 → run_cartload2 → upload on a small dataset, after the equivalent run_together command.
  • Multiple samples: the Human Cortex Multi-sample Tutorial runs run_ficture2_multi and run_cartload2_multi on five human cortex MERFISH samples.

Question

  • Which interface should I use?
  • How do I resume or restart a run?

docs.title: Single Sample with run_together
docs.text:
run_together runs a complete CartoScope pipeline with a single command: SGE conversion → FICTURE → cell analyses → background images → asset packaging → (optional) publishing. It builds one Makefile and runs it, so the pipeline is resumable and parallel out of the box.

This guide processes a public 10x Xenium human lung cancer dataset (a full section, larger than the quick start examples).

The recommended entry point

run_together is the recommended way to run CartLoader on any supported platform, for one sample or many. The individual commands remain available for step-by-step use; the older run_xenium / run_visiumhd orchestrators are legacy. See Which interface should I use?.

docs.title: Prepare Input
docs.text:
Download the Xenium Ranger output from the 10x Genomics Dataset portal and unzip it:

work_dir=/path/to/work/directory
mkdir -p ${work_dir}/raw && cd ${work_dir}/raw

wget https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/xenium/2.0.0/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs.zip
# or: curl -O https://cf.10xgenomics.com/samples/xenium/2.0.0/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE/Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs.zip
unzip Xenium_V1_humanLung_Cancer_FFPE_outs.zip

${work_dir}/raw is now the Xenium Ranger output directory. The 10x_xenium profile reads its standard layout automatically, so you do not list these files yourself:

${work_dir}/raw/
├── transcripts.parquet                 # or transcripts.csv.gz
├── cell_boundaries.csv.gz              # cell boundaries for the cell analyses
├── cells.csv.gz                        # cell centroids (x_centroid, y_centroid)
├── analysis/clustering/gene_expression_graphclust/clusters.csv   # Xenium Ranger clusters
└── morphology_focus/morphology_focus_000{0,1,2,3}.ome.tif        # dapi/boundary/rna/protein images

See the Xenium platform page for every path the profile looks for.

docs.title: Define ID and Parameters
docs.text:
DATA_ID="xenium-v1-humanlung-cancer-ffpe"   # dataset name; names the output folder and the packaged assets
train_width=18                              # FICTURE hexagon width (µm)
n_factor=24                                 # number of factors (comma-separated for several)
n_jobs=10

docs.title: Run the Pipeline
docs.text:
LocallyVia Docker

Requires a local installation, including the tools built by submodules/build.sh; run_together finds them there, so it takes no tool-path options.

cartloader run_together \
    --platform 10x_xenium \
    --in-dir  ${work_dir}/raw \
    --out-dir ${work_dir}/output/${DATA_ID} \
    --id ${DATA_ID} \
    --width ${train_width} \
    --n-factor ${n_factor} \
    -j ${n_jobs} --threads ${n_jobs}

Uses the prebuilt image, which includes every tool (see Quick Start with Docker).

docker run --rm \
    -v ${work_dir}:/data \
    hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
    run_together \
    --platform 10x_xenium \
    --in-dir  /data/raw \
    --out-dir /data/output/${DATA_ID} \
    --id ${DATA_ID} \
    --width ${train_width} \
    --n-factor ${n_factor} \
    -j ${n_jobs} --threads ${n_jobs}

With this profile, one run produces: the converted SGE; one FICTURE model per --width × --n-factor combination with pixel-level decoding; two cell analyses (cartloader, a FICTURE analysis of the segmented cells, and xeniumranger, an import of the Xenium Ranger clusters); the four morphology images; and the packaged PMTiles.

Preview before running

Add --dry-run to write the Makefile and print every command (make -n) without executing. Inspect ${work_dir}/output/${DATA_ID}/run_together.mk and run_together.resolved.json to see exactly what will run.

docs.title: Projection-only Mode
docs.text:
To reuse models from a previous FICTURE run instead of training new ones, point --project-models at that run's FICTURE directory. run_together reads its ficture.params.json and re-projects every model it lists; no LDA training runs.

cartloader run_together --platform 10x_xenium \
    --in-dir ${work_dir}/raw --out-dir ${work_dir}/output/${DATA_ID} --id ${DATA_ID} \
    --project-models /path/to/previous/fic --width 12 -j ${n_jobs}

docs.title: Output
docs.text:
${work_dir}/output/${DATA_ID}/
├── run_together.mk               # the generated pipeline (Makefile)
├── run_together.resolved.json    # fully resolved settings (provenance)
├── mk/                           # per-stage flag files that drive make
├── tsv/<id>/                     # converted SGE (transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz, features, coordinate ranges)
├── fic/                          # FICTURE results (per sample under fic/samples/<id>/)
└── cartl/<id>/                   # packaged PMTiles + catalog.yaml  ← deploy this

The packaged directory is named <out-dir name>-<id>, shortened to <id> when the two are equal, as in the command above. Without --id, the sample ID is rep1, so the directory would be cartl/xenium-v1-humanlung-cancer-ffpe-rep1/.

The catalog.yaml plus its PMTiles is the deployable CartoScope asset. A joint multi-sample run produces one such directory per sample plus a cartl/multi-catalog.yaml; see Multiple Samples with run_together. For per-stage output details, see sge_convert, run_ficture2_multi, and run_cartload2.

docs.title: Resume, Re-run, and Publish
docs.text:
• Resume after a failure: re-run the same command (or make -f .../run_together.mk -j N). Completed stages are skipped via their flag files.
  • Run part of the pipeline: --only ingest,ficture or --skip images. Excluded upstream stages are assumed already done.
  • Force a clean rebuild: --restart (make -B).
  • Publish (opt-in): AI annotation and S3 upload are separate flags: --anno or --anno-deep (with --tissue/--organism) and --s3-upload. See Publishing.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Process several sections under one joint FICTURE model: Multiple Samples with run_together.
  • Every option and configuration key: run_together reference.
  • The exact inputs each platform expects: Platforms.

docs.title: Multiple Samples with run_together
docs.text:
When you have several sections that should share one FICTURE model, list them in a sample sheet and run_together will:

  1. ingest every sample,
  2. train a single joint model on all of them together,
  3. package each sample independently against that shared model.

The dependency graph fans in on the joint model, then fans back out per sample — so make -j ingests all samples in parallel, blocks once on the shared model, then packages each sample in parallel:

ingest (sample 1) ─┐
                   ├─► ficture (joint model) ─┬─► cartload 1 ─► images 1 ─► publish 1
ingest (sample 2) ─┘                          └─► cartload 2 ─► images 2 ─► publish 2

When to use a joint model

Sharing one model across sections makes factors directly comparable between samples and is the recommended setup for replicates or a cohort. For unrelated samples, run them independently (see batches). Background: Why multi-sample?

docs.title: 1. List the samples in a TSV sheet
docs.text:
A multi-sample run is just a single-sample run with --samples samples.tsv in place of --in-dir. The sheet is a wide table of input roles; for the common case you only need id + in_dir:

id      in_dir
rep1    /data/kidney/rep1/outs
rep2    /data/kidney/rep2/outs
rep3    /data/kidney/rep3/outs

docs.title: 2. Run
docs.text:
cartloader run_together --platform 10x_xenium \
    --samples samples.tsv --out-dir /path/to/output/kidney-cohort \
    --width 18 --n-factor 24 -j 10

All rows share one --out-dir, so they train one joint model. Everything else (FICTURE mode, images, cell analyses) is assembled exactly as in the single-sample run and applied to every sample. Add --dry-run to inspect run_together.mk and run_together.resolved.json first.

With Docker, mount the directories that hold the sheet, the inputs, and the output, and use the container paths both on the command line and inside the sheet:

docker run --rm -v /data:/data hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
    run_together --platform 10x_xenium \
    --samples /data/kidney/samples.tsv --out-dir /data/output/kidney-cohort \
    --width 18 --n-factor 24 -j 10

Output layout

Packaging is delegated to run_cartload2_multi: each sample is written to a self-contained cartl/<multi_id>-<sample_id>/ directory (with <multi_id> defaulting to the --out-dir basename), plus a cartl/multi-catalog.yaml that links every per-sample catalog.yaml and copies the shared factor files (post/rgb/de/info/umap) into the cartl/ root as a unified factors: map. Upload the whole cartl/ directory to S3 as one unit.

Extra role columns

The sheet can also carry per-sample inputs — raw_transcript (a raw CSV to ingest), transcript (pre-converted TSV, skips ingest), xy, boundaries, clusters, mex, cellxgene (a cell×gene matrix CSV, e.g. MERSCOPE cell_by_gene.csv): 

id    in_dir       transcript                     boundaries               cellxgene
rep1  /data/rep1
rep2               /data/rep2/transcripts.tsv.gz  /data/rep2/bounds.csv.gz
rep3  /data/rep3                                                            /data/rep3/cell_by_gene.csv
See the reference → sample sheet for the full column list, aliases, and the three transcript sources.

docs.title: When to use JSON instead
docs.text:
Escalate to a --config JSON when samples need different inputs, or to change run-wide settings beyond the CLI flags. JSON augments the CLI: per-sample inputs go in samples entries, and run-wide blocks such as cartload sit at the top level (a joint run packages all samples with one run_cartload2_multi call, so packaging settings apply to every sample):

{
  "cartload": { "bin_count": 300 },
  "samples": [
    { "id": "rep3", "in_dir": "/data/kidney/rep3/outs",
      "hne": "/data/kidney/rep3/he.tif" }
  ]
}

Samples from the config and the sheet are combined

samples entries in the JSON are added to the rows of --samples; a sample listed in both appears twice. List each sample in only one place.

Unknown keys abort the run, so a typo is caught instead of silently ignored. See the configuration reference for every key.

docs.title: Visium HD example
docs.text:
The same shape works for Visium HD; the 10x_visium_hd profile adds the square/cell imports and (with a per-sample hne column) the H&E layer automatically. Add hne as a sheet column:

id      in_dir             hne
38088   /data/SI_38088/outs  /data/HE_38088.tif
39685   /data/SI_39685/outs  /data/HE_39685.tif

cartloader run_together --platform 10x_visium_hd \
    --samples samples.tsv --out-dir /path/to/output/prostate-cohort -j 10

docs.title: Publishing (opt-in)
docs.text:
Publishing is CLI-driven, with no config block. Enable AI annotation (--anno, or --anno-deep for one joint LLM call over all factors; both need --tissue/--organism) and/or S3 upload (--s3-upload) for every sample:

cartloader run_together --platform 10x_xenium \
    --samples samples.tsv --out-dir OUT --width 18 --n-factor 24 -j 10 \
    --anno --tissue "Kidney" --organism human \
    --s3-upload --collection kidney-cohort

Each sample uploads to s3://cartostore/data/batch=<YYYY_MM>/<collection>/<multi_id>-<sample_id>/, where <YYYY_MM> defaults to the current date (override --batch) and <collection> defaults to the out-dir basename (override --collection). See the reference → Publish for all flags (--s3-prefix, --aws-profile, annotation model/threads, …).

docs.title: Batches of independent samples
docs.text:
For many unrelated samples (each its own model), use --out-root instead of --out-dir:

cartloader run_together --platform 10x_xenium \
    --samples samples.tsv --out-root /path/to/output/2026_07 -j 6

Each row becomes its own <out_root>/<id>/ with an independent model. See Specifying Inputs → Multi-sample.

docs.title: Visium HD End-to-End Pipeline
docs.text:
This tutorial walks through end‑to‑end processing of 10x Visium HD data with CartLoader: converting inputs, running FICTURE, importing cell results and histology, packaging assets, and uploading for sharing.

Legacy

This tutorial uses run_visiumhd, a legacy orchestrator superseded by run_together, which runs the same stages for the standard Space Ranger layout (and multiple samples with a joint model) and is the recommended workflow. The page is kept for existing users; see Legacy Orchestrators.

Known issue: combining --run-ficture2 with --run-cartload2 in one run_visiumhd call, as in the examples below, currently fails at the packaging step. Workaround: once FICTURE has finished, run run_cartload2 directly with --fic-dir <out-dir>/ficture2, then upload; see Legacy Orchestrators.

docs.text:
See Space Ranger output details in the official documentation: Space Ranger Outputs

RAW Data StructureSGE FormatCell Analysis Result Format

│   ├── square_002um
│   │   ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix

│   │   │   │       └── ...
│   │   │   └── umap
│   │   │       └── gene_expression_2_components
│   │   │           └── projection.csv
│   │   ├── filtered_feature_bc_matrix
│   │   │   └── ...     # Mirrors binned_outputs/square_002um/filtered_feature_bc_matrix
│   │   ├── ...
│   │   └── spatial
│   │       └── ...     # Mirrors binned_outputs/square_002um/spatial
│   └── square_016um
│       └── ...         # Mirrors square_008um (analysis, spatial, filtered_feature_bc_matrix)
├── segmented_outputs
│   ├── cell_segmentations.geojson
│   └── ...             # Mirrors binned_outputs/square_008um (analysis, spatial, filtered_feature_bc_matrix)
└── ...

Visium HD slides use a 2×2 µm grid of barcoded squares (square_002um) for high-resolution spatial gene mapping. Use filtered_feature_bc_matrix to only process tissue-associated signals.

ATTENTION

The file‑format examples below use a sample Visium HD dataset. Paths, IDs, and values are illustrative and may not match the dataset used in this tutorial.

SGE comprises several key files as follows:

filtered_feature_bc_matrix/barcodes.tsv.gz – spatial barcode for tissue locations 
s_002um_00639_00600-1
s_002um_00923_01639-1
s_002um_01050_01530-1
  • Column 1: Spatial barcodes corresponding to specific locations on the tissue section.
filtered_feature_bc_matrix/features.tsv.gz – feature metadata 
ENSMUSG00000051951  Xkr4    Gene Expression
ENSMUSG00000025900  Rp1     Gene Expression
ENSMUSG00000025902  Sox17   Gene Expression
  • Column 1: Feature ID
  • Column 2: Feature symbol
  • Column 3: Feature type
filtered_feature_bc_matrix/matrix.mtx.gz – expression count matrix 
%%MatrixMarket matrix coordinate integer general
%
19059 869411 11376563
3606 1 1
8957 1 1
9733 1 1
  • Header: Initial lines form the header, declaring the matrix's adherence to the Market Matrix (MTX) format, outlining its traits. This may include comments (lines beginning with %) for extra metadata, all marked by a “%”.
  • Dimensions: Following the header, the first line details the matrix dimensions: the count of rows (features), columns (barcodes), and non-zero entries.
  • Data Entries: After the dimensions, each subsequent line provides three fields: row index (feature index), column index (barcode index), and the expression-count value.
tissue_positions.parquet – spatial barcode metadata 
barcode                 in_tissue   array_row   array_col   pxl_row_in_fullres  pxl_col_in_fullres
s_002um_00434_01637-1   1           434         1637        3396.371014         9125.919898
  • barcode: Unique spatial barcode associated with each capture spot.
  • in_tissue: Binary flag (1 = in tissue, 0 = background) indicating whether the spot falls within the tissue boundary.
  • array_row, array_col: Integer indices representing the position of the spot on the capture array grid.
  • pxl_row_in_fullres, pxl_col_in_fullres: Floating point coordinates locating the spot in full-resolution tissue image pixels.
scalefactors_json.json – pixel-to-micrometer scaling factors 
{
    "spot_diameter_fullres": 7.303953797779634,
    "bin_size_um": 2.0,
    "microns_per_pixel": 0.2738242950835738,
    "regist_target_img_scalef": 0.2505533,
    "tissue_lowres_scalef": 0.02505533,
    "fiducial_diameter_fullres": 1205.1523766336395,
    "tissue_hires_scalef": 0.2505533
}
  • spot_diameter_fullres: Estimated diameter of a barcoded spot in full-resolution pixels.
  • bin_size_um: Physical size (in micrometers) of the smallest bin, typically 2.0 µm for Visium HD.
  • microns_per_pixel: Resolution of the full-res image, used to convert pixel distances to micrometers.
  • regist_target_img_scalef: Scaling factor applied during image registration to the target image.
  • tissue_lowres_scalef: Downscaling factor from full-res to low-resolution tissue image.
  • fiducial_diameter_fullres: Diameter of fiducial markers in full-resolution pixels, useful for alignment.
  • tissue_hires_scalef: Downscaling factor from full-res to high-resolution tissue image.

Cell Segmentation Mask

Location: segmented_outputs/cell_segmentations.geojson 

{"type": "FeatureCollection", "features": [
  {"type": "Feature",
   "geometry": {"type": "Polygon", "coordinates": [[[x1, y1], [x2, y2], ...]]},
   "properties": {"cell_id": 1}},
  ...
]}

  • One polygon per segmented cell, with vertices in full-resolution image pixels (converted to µm with microns_per_pixel from scalefactors_json.json).
  • cell_id: integer cell ID; cell N is barcode cellid_00000000N-1 (zero-padded to 9 digits) in the cell feature matrix.

Cell Feature Matrix

Location: segmented_outputs/filtered_feature_cell_matrix

This contains barcodes.tsv.gz,features.tsv.gz, matrix.mtx.gz, providing cell id, feature information, and expression count matrix, respectively.

Clusters

docs.title: Define ID and Parameters
docs.text:
# Unique identifier for your dataset
DATA_ID="visiumhd_3prime_mouse_brain"    # change this to reflect your dataset name

# LDA parameters
train_width=18                           # define LDA training hexagon width (comma-separated if multiple widths are applied)
n_factor=48                              # define number of factors in LDA training (comma-separated if multiple n-factor values are provided)

# Path to AWS S3 directory
S3_DIR=s3://your-bucket/path/to/dir      # recommended: end with DATA_ID, e.g. s3://your-bucket/visiumhd-3prime-mouse-brain

How to define scaling for Visium HD?

10x Visium HD provides scalefactors_json.json (pixel‑to‑µm). CartLoader accepts it via --scale-json and computes the scaling automatically, so you don’t need to manually specify --units-per-um.

Alternatively, provide the scale directly with --units-per-um.

docs.title: Example Runs
docs.text: Choose one of the following options to run the run_visiumhd pipeline, either locally or with Docker. Add --import-squares to either command to also import the Space Ranger 8 µm and 16 µm square-bin results.

docs.title: Run Pipeline Locally
docs.text:
Set Up Environment 

# ====
# Replace the placeholders with values for your system.

docs.title: Xenium End-to-End Pipeline
docs.text:
This tutorial walks through end‑to‑end processing of 10x Xenium data with CartLoader: converting inputs, running FICTURE, importing cell results and histology, packaging assets, and uploading to AWS for sharing.

Legacy

This tutorial uses run_xenium, a legacy orchestrator superseded by run_together, which runs the same stages for the standard Xenium layout and is the recommended workflow. The page is kept for existing users; see Legacy Orchestrators.

Known issue: combining --run-ficture2 with --run-cartload2 in one run_xenium call, as in the examples below, currently fails at the packaging step. Workaround: once FICTURE has finished, run run_cartload2 directly with --fic-dir <out-dir>/ficture2, then upload; see Legacy Orchestrators.

docs.title: Data Access
docs.text:
Download the ST data from the 10x Genomics Dataset portal.

Use wgetUse curl

If you have wget installed, use the following commands to download the output from 10X.

# Define the work directory
work_dir=/path/to/work/directory

docs.title: Define ID and Parameters
docs.text:
# Unique identifier for your dataset
DATA_ID="xenium-v1-humanlung-cancer-ffpe"   # change this to reflect your dataset name
SCALE=1                                     # coordinate to micrometer scaling factor

# LDA parameters
train_width=18                            # define LDA training hexagon width (comma-separated if multiple widths are applied)
n_factor=24                               # define number of factors in LDA training (comma-separated if multiple n-factor values are provided)

# Path to AWS S3 directory
S3_DIR=s3://your-bucket/path/to/dir       # recommended: end with DATA_ID, e.g. s3://your-bucket/xenium-v1-humanlung-cancer-ffpe

How to define Scaling Factors for Xenium?

--units-per-um means "coordinate units per micrometer" in your raw transcript coordinates. For the Xenium example dataset in this tutorial, coordinates are already in µm, so use --units-per-um 1.

Check this value for your own dataset

Do not assume --units-per-um 1 is always correct. Always verify the coordinate unit in your input data.

If your coordinates are in pixels (or any unit other than µm), set --units-per-um to the correct value.

docs.title: Get Started
docs.text:
The recommended way to run CartLoader is run_together: a single command that takes a sample from raw platform output to deployable CartoScope assets: SGE conversion, FICTURE spatial factors, cell analyses, background images, and PMTiles packaging. It plans every step as one resumable Makefile, so rerunning the same command after an interruption picks up where it stopped.

Both quick starts below run two examples:

  1. A small mouse hippocampus dataset (Seq-Scope), finishes in minutes. In Docker it needs no download at all.
  2. A Xenium human kidney section (GSE264334), which exercises the whole pipeline, including cell segmentation imports and the DAPI image.

docs.text:

      • 🔧 Run Locally

        Install cartloader and its tools on your system.

      Not sure which to choose?

      See Docker or local?. In short: use Docker to try CartLoader or to run a released version reproducibly; install locally to follow the latest code or modify it.

docs.title: After the quick start
docs.text:
• Your own data: the platform tutorials show the run_together command for each supported platform, and Specifying Inputs covers every way to describe a sample.
  • Several samples together: Multiple Samples with run_together trains one shared model across samples.
  • Publishing and annotation: run_together --s3-upload and --anno / --anno-deep (see Publishing).
  • Individual commands: the Step-by-step section runs each stage (sge_convert, run_ficture2, run_cartload2, ...) separately for full control.

docs.title: Quick Start: Run with Docker
docs.text:
This quick start runs run_together inside the prebuilt Docker image, which contains CartLoader, every tool it calls, and a small starter dataset.

Use Cases

The fastest way to try CartLoader: nothing to install except Docker, and the first example needs no download.

Requirements

  • Docker on your system (see Install Docker).
  • For the second example: about 10 GB of free disk (a 1.5 GB download plus about 8 GB of outputs); it took about 11 minutes on a 12-core laptop with --threads 4 -j 4.

Question

  • I am not sure whether to run with Docker or run locally. Which one should I choose?

docs.title: Install Docker
docs.text:
If you are new to Docker, see the Docker documentation for installation and basic usage. Then check that it works:

docker --version         # Docker is installed
docker run hello-world   # Docker can run containers

If these commands fail, install Docker first.

docs.title: Get the Image
docs.text:
docker pull hyunminkang/cartloader:latest

latest always points to the most recent release. For reproducible results, use a dated tag instead (for example hyunminkang/cartloader:20261007-1432); every release is listed on Docker Hub.

How the image is used: its entry point is the cartloader command, so whatever follows the image name is a cartloader subcommand and its options:

docker run --rm -v <host-dir>:<container-dir> hyunminkang/cartloader:latest <command> [options]
  • -v mounts a directory from your machine into the container. Paths in the options must be the container paths.
  • --rm removes the container when the command finishes; outputs written to a mounted directory stay on your machine.
  • To look around inside the image (the repository is at /app/cartloader, the starter data at /app/data): 
    docker run --rm -it --entrypoint bash hyunminkang/cartloader:latest

File ownership on Linux

The container runs as root, so on Linux the files it writes are owned by root. Change ownership afterwards if needed, e.g. sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) out.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
The image contains a mouse hippocampus SGE from Seq-Scope under /app/data/sge/, already converted to the FICTURE-compatible transcript format by sge_convert:

transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz: transcript-indexed SGE in TSV 
X        Y        gene     count
295.29   1422.35  Myo3a    0
1745.54  1110.72  Med14    1
1745.54  1110.72  Ntpcr    1
  • X: X coordinates in um
  • Y: Y coordinates in um
  • gene: gene symbols
  • count: expression count per pixel per gene
feature.clean.tsv.gz: UMI counts on a per-gene basis in TSV 

gene           gene_id             count
Gm29155        ENSMUSG00000100764  1
Pcmtd1         ENSMUSG00000051285  431
Gm26901        ENSMUSG00000097797  1
* gene: gene symbols * gene_id: gene IDs * count: expression count per gene

coordinate_minmax.tsv: X Y min/max coordinates 
xmin    0.14
xmax    2359.90
ymin    0.23
ymax    1439.95
  • xmin xmax: min and max X coordinates in um
  • ymin ymax: min and max Y coordinates in um

The same data is on Zenodo: seqscope_starter.std.tar.gz.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
mkdir -p out
docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/out:/out hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
  run_together \
    --platform seqscope \
    --in-transcript /app/data/sge/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz \
    --out-dir /out/seqscope_hippo \
    --id seqscope_hippo \
    --width 18 \
    --n-factor 6,12 \
    --threads 4 -j 4
Option Meaning --platform seqscope Use the Seq-Scope platform profile for defaults. --in-transcript An already-converted transcript TSV, so the SGE conversion step is skipped. --out-dir, --id Output directory and the sample ID used to name the packaged assets. --width, --n-factor FICTURE hexagon width (µm) and the number(s) of factors; one model per combination. --threads, -j Threads per job and number of parallel jobs.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: The deployable result is out/seqscope_hippo/cartl/seqscope_hippo/: a catalog.yaml plus the PMTiles it references (the SGE and one set of factor layers per model). See Outputs for the full layout.

docs.text:

docs.title: Example 2: Xenium Human Kidney (full pipeline)
docs.text: This example starts from raw Xenium output, so every stage runs: SGE conversion, FICTURE, two cell analyses (CartLoader's own, from the Xenium cell boundaries, and an import of the Xenium Ranger clusters), the DAPI image, and packaging.

docs.title: Input
docs.text:
A human kidney section from GSE264334, repackaged in the standard Xenium output layout and hosted on the AWS Open Data Registry (no AWS account needed):

# with the AWS CLI
aws s3 cp --no-sign-request \
  "s3://cartostore/data/batch=2026_05/xenium-geo-public-dataset-collection/xenium-human-kidney-igan-bull2024-20260516/gse264334-reformatted.tar.gz" .
# or with curl
curl -O "https://cartostore.s3.amazonaws.com/data/batch=2026_05/xenium-geo-public-dataset-collection/xenium-human-kidney-igan-bull2024-20260516/gse264334-reformatted.tar.gz"

tar -xzf gse264334-reformatted.tar.gz    # creates gse264334-reformatted/

run_together finds the inputs inside the folder by their standard Xenium names: transcripts.csv.gz, cells.csv.gz, cell_boundaries.csv.gz, analysis/clustering/gene_expression_graphclust/clusters.csv, and morphology.ome.tif (see the Xenium platform page).

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
docker run --rm -v $(pwd):/work hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
  run_together \
    --platform 10x_xenium \
    --in-dir /work/gse264334-reformatted \
    --out-dir /work/out/gse264334 \
    --id gse264334 \
    --bin-count 50 \
    --threads 4 -j 4

Without --width/--n-factor, the Xenium profile's defaults apply (12 µm hexagons; 12, 24, and 48 factors). --bin-count 50 groups genes into 50 bins for the point layers instead of the default 500, which makes packaging faster for a quick test.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text:
run_together writes everything under --out-dir:

<out-dir>/
├── run_together.mk            # the generated Makefile (rerun the command to resume)
├── run_together.resolved.json # the fully resolved configuration of the run
├── mk/                        # per-stage done flags
├── tsv/                       # converted SGE (transcripts, features, coordinate ranges)
├── fic/                       # FICTURE models, factor maps, cell analyses
└── cartl/<id>/                # catalog.yaml + PMTiles  ← the deployable result

Upload cartl/<id>/ to any web-accessible storage to view it in CartoScope, or let run_together do it with --s3-upload (see Publishing).

Interrupted or failed run?

Rerun the same command: finished steps are skipped. Add --restart to rebuild everything. See Resume or Restart.

docs.title: Quick Start: Run Locally
docs.text:
This quick start runs run_together with a local installation of CartLoader, on the same two examples as the Docker quick start.

Use Cases

Use a local installation to follow the latest code on GitHub, to modify CartLoader, or when Docker is not available.

Requirements

  • CartLoader and its tools installed and built as described in the Installation Guide, including bash build.sh in submodules/.
  • For the second example: about 10 GB of free disk (a 1.5 GB download plus about 8 GB of outputs); it took about 11 minutes on a 12-core laptop with --threads 4 -j 4.

Question

  • I am not sure whether to run with Docker or run locally. Which one should I choose?

docs.title: Check the Installation
docs.text:
Activate the environment you installed CartLoader into, then check that every dependency is found:

python installation/check_dependencies.py    # run from the cartloader repository

run_together uses the tools built under submodules/ (punkst, spatula, pmpoint, tippecanoe, pmtiles, geotiff2pmtiles), so you never pass tool paths to it.

After updating CartLoader, reinstall and rebuild

The pipeline expects the Python packages and tool versions pinned by the repository. After git pull, reinstall the Python dependencies and rebuild the submodules; otherwise a step may fail with a missing-package error (for example requires the 'imagecodecs' package), an "unknown option" error, or a usage message: 

uv pip install -e ".[ai]"                 # or: python -m pip install -e ".[ai]"
git submodule update --init --recursive
cd submodules && bash build.sh

docs.title: CosMx SMI Starter Tutorial
docs.text:
This tutorial walks through a starter end-to-end workflow for CosMx SMI data using an adult mouse hippocampus subset extracted from a coronal brain section.

It first runs the whole analysis with a single run_together command, then walks through the same analysis step by step: input preparation, SGE format conversion, FICTURE analysis, asset packaging, and data upload.

docs.title: Run with run_together
docs.text:
Download the example data, hosted on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.17953582), into a work directory:

work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # replace with your work directory
mkdir -p ${work_dir} && cd ${work_dir}
wget https://zenodo.org/records/17953582/files/cosmxsmi_starter.raw.tar.gz
tar --strip-components=1 -zxvf cosmxsmi_starter.raw.tar.gz   # extracts input.tsv.gz

The CosMx SMI profile expects a full AtoMx flat-file export (transcript, cell-metadata, and polygon files). The starter data is a single transcript table, so it goes through the generic profile with the cosmx_smi input preset of sge_convert (comma-separated; columns x_global_px, y_global_px, target). Write a small config file that selects the preset:

cat > cosmxsmi_starter.json <<'EOF'
{ "ingest": { "sge_platform": "cosmx_smi" } }
EOF

Then run the pipeline, either with a local installation or with the Docker image:

LocallyDocker 
cartloader run_together \
  --platform generic \
  --raw-transcript ./input.tsv.gz \
  --config cosmxsmi_starter.json \
  --units-per-um 8.333333 \
  --out-dir ./out/cosmxsmi_hippo \
  --id cosmxsmi_hippo \
  --width 12 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

docker run --rm -v ${work_dir}:/data hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
  run_together \
  --platform generic \
  --raw-transcript /data/input.tsv.gz \
  --config /data/cosmxsmi_starter.json \
  --units-per-um 8.333333 \
  --out-dir /data/out/cosmxsmi_hippo \
  --id cosmxsmi_hippo \
  --width 12 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

--units-per-um 8.333333 (1000 / 120) converts the 120 nm pixels to µm. The result to deploy is out/cosmxsmi_hippo/cartl/cosmxsmi_hippo/ (a catalog.yaml and the PMTiles it lists). Add --dry-run to print the commands without running them.

How run_together differs from the step-by-step path

  • FICTURE runs through run_ficture2_multi (a joint model over a single sample) with single-molecule pixel decoding, instead of run_ficture2.
  • Feature filters are the run_together defaults: control features (Unassigned, Neg, BLANK/Blank, Intergenic, Deprecated, System, NCS-, NCP-) are dropped at ingest; predicted (Gm<digit>), mitochondrial (mt-/MT-), and ribosomal (Rps/Rpl) genes stay in the data but are left out of the factor models. Change them with --ingest-exclude-feature-regex and --exclude-feature-regex.
  • Point layers are packaged with pmpoint (--use-pmpoint, 500 gene bins) instead of tippecanoe.
  • Outputs go under --out-dir: tsv/<id>/ (converted SGE), fic/ (FICTURE), and cartl/<id>/ (PMTiles and catalog.yaml; deploy this), instead of sge/, ficture2/, and cartload2/.
  • Publishing is built in: --s3-upload uploads cartl/<id>/ to S3 (see Publishing). For Zenodo, run upload_zenodo on cartl/<id>/ as in the step-by-step path.

docs.title: Step by Step (Individual Commands)
docs.text: The same analysis, one command at a time. Use it to understand each stage or to customize it.

docs.title: Set Up the Environment
docs.text:
# ====
# Replace the placeholders with values for your system.
# ====
work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # directory holding the input data; outputs are written here too
cd $work_dir

n_jobs=10                               # number of parallel jobs (also used as threads per job below)

# Activate the Python environment in which CartLoader is installed
conda activate ENV_NAME                 # replace ENV_NAME (or: source /path/to/venv/bin/activate)

No tool paths needed

Once submodules/build.sh has run (see Installation), every CartLoader command finds spatula, punkst, tippecanoe, pmtiles, and pmpoint in the submodules/ directory of the repository, and the default color map at assets/default_color_map.tsv. Pass --spatula, --ficture2 (the punkst repository directory, which contains bin/punkst), --tippecanoe, --pmtiles, or --cmap-file only to use a different build or file. upload_aws runs the aws CLI from your PATH (--aws to override).

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text:
Use the data downloaded above.

NanoString CosMx SMI produces single‑molecule spatial transcriptomics data as a comma‑separated values (CSV) table (input.tsv.gz in the starter data).

CSV File Format

"fov","cell_ID","x_global_px","y_global_px","x_local_px","y_local_px","z","target","CellComp"
64,0,-473043,7954.533,4015.3,4246.2,1,"Gfap","None"
64,0,-473022.9,7902.723,4035.48,4194.39,1,"Fth1","None"
64,0,-473132,7836.476,3926.34,4128.143,1,"Ptn","None"
  • fov: The field of view (FOV) number.
  • cell_ID: Unique identifier for a single cell within a given FOV; 0 if background or unassigned molecules.
  • x_global_px, y_global_px: Global pixel coordinates relative to the tissue.
  • x_local_px, y_local_px: The x or y position (in pixels) relative to the given FOV.
  • z: Z-plane index representing the depth (optical section) where the transcript was detected.
  • target: Target name.
  • CellComp: Subcellular location of the target.

docs.title: Define ID and Parameters
docs.text:
# Unique identifier for your dataset
DATA_ID="cosmxsmi_hippo"                # change this to reflect your dataset name
PLATFORM="cosmx_smi"                    # platform information
SCALE=$(echo 1000/120|bc -l)            # coordinate units per micrometer

# LDA parameters
train_width=12                           # define LDA training hexagon width (comma-separated if multiple widths are applied)
n_factor=6,12                            # define number of factors in LDA training (comma-separated if multiple n-factor values are provided)

How to define Scaling Factors for CosMx SMI?

According to the README.html provided with the example CosMx dataset, each pixel has an edge length of 120 nm. To calculate the number of pixels per micrometer, use the formula: scale = 1000 / 120.

docs.title: SGE Format Conversion
docs.text:
Convert the raw input to the unified SGE format. See more details in its Reference page.

cartloader sge_convert \
  --makefn sge_convert.mk \
  --platform ${PLATFORM} \
  --in-csv ./input.tsv.gz \
  --units-per-um ${SCALE} \
  --out-dir ./sge \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(BLANK|Neg|Intergenic|Deprecated|Unassigned)' \
  --sge-visual \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --platform required string Input platform, which sets the default input columns and delimiter (options: 10x_visium_hd, seqscope, illumina, 10x_xenium, bgi_stereoseq, cosmx_smi, vizgen_merscope, pixel_seq, nova_st, generic) --in-csv required string Path to the input transcript CSV/TSV file --out-dir required string Output directory for the converted SGE files --units-per-um float Coordinate units per µm in the input (default: 1, i.e. already in µm; 1000 for the Seq-Scope raw TSV; detected from the barcodes for illumina) --csv-colname-feature-name string Gene-name column in the input (default: set by --platform) --csv-colname-count string Count column in the input (default: set by --platform; without one, each row counts 1) --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: sge_convert.mk) --exclude-feature-regex regex Pattern of feature names to drop (e.g. control probes) --sge-visual flag Draw the converted SGE as an image (xy.png) for a visual check --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1)

docs.title: FICTURE Analysis
docs.text:
Compute spatial factors using punkst (FICTURE2). See more details on the Reference page.

cartloader run_ficture2 \
  --makefn run_ficture2.mk \
  --main \
  --in-transcript ./sge/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz \
  --in-feature ./sge/feature.clean.tsv.gz \
  --in-minmax ./sge/coordinate_minmax.tsv \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(mt-.*$|Gm\d+$)' \
  --out-dir ./ficture2 \
  --width ${train_width} \
  --n-factor ${n_factor} \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs} \
  --threads ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --main required 1 flag Run all five main steps --in-transcript required string Path to the transcript-indexed SGE file from sge_convert --out-dir required string Output directory --width required int or comma-separated list Hexagon width(s) in µm for LDA training --n-factor required int or comma-separated list Number(s) of LDA factors; one model per width × factor combination --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: run_ficture2.mk) --in-feature string Path to the per-gene count file from sge_convert (default: the feature list made during tiling) --in-minmax string Path to the coordinate min/max file from sge_convert (default: the range computed during tiling) --exclude-feature-regex regex Feature names to leave out of the factor analysis. punkst matches the whole name, so end each alternative with .* or $ as needed (the example drops mitochondrial mt-* and predicted Gm<digits> genes) --cmap-file string Color map TSV (default: assets/default_color_map.tsv in the CartLoader repository) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1) --threads int Number of threads per job (default: 4)

1: CartLoader requires at least one action: --tile (tiling), --segment (hexagon segmentation), --init-lda (LDA training), --decode (pixel-level decoding), --umap (UMAP of the factors), or --main for all five.

docs.title: CartLoader Asset Packaging
docs.text:
Package the SGE and the FICTURE results into PMTiles and a catalog.yaml for CartoScope. See more details in its Reference page.

cartloader run_cartload2 \
  --makefn run_cartload2.mk \
  --fic-dir ./ficture2 \
  --out-dir ./cartload2 \
  --id ${DATA_ID} \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs} \
  --threads ${n_jobs}

Packaging without factor analysis

To host only the SGE (no factors), use cartloader run_together ... --no-ficture, which tiles the transcripts and packages them without training any model.

Parameter Required Type Description --fic-dir required string FICTURE output directory from run_ficture2; must contain ficture.params.json (the SGE paths are read from it) --out-dir required string Output directory for the PMTiles, assets, and catalog.yaml --id required string Dataset ID used in the catalog and output metadata (no whitespace) --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: run_cartload2.mk) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1) --threads int Number of threads per job (default: 4) --spatula, --tippecanoe, --pmtiles string Tool paths (default: the copies built under submodules/)

docs.title: Upload to Data Repository
docs.text:
Choose a data repository to host/share your output

CartLoader supports two upload options (AWS and Zenodo) for storing PMTiles of SGE and spatial factors in a data repository.

Choose the one that best suits your needs.

AWS UploadsZenodo Uploads

Upload the generated CartLoader outputs to your designated AWS S3 directory. The aws CLI must be configured with credentials that can write there (see AWS Upload Failures).

# AWS S3 target location
S3_DIR=s3://your-bucket/path/to/dir     # recommended: end with DATA_ID, e.g. s3://your-bucket/test-data/${DATA_ID}

cartloader upload_aws \
  --in-dir ./cartload2 \
  --s3-dir "${S3_DIR}" \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --in-dir required string Directory with the CartLoader packaging output (containing catalog.yaml) --s3-dir required string Target S3 directory --profile string AWS CLI profile to use --aws string Path to the AWS CLI (default: aws) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 2)

Upload the generated CartLoader outputs to a new Zenodo deposition or an existing one (see Zenodo Setup for the access token).

zenodo_token=/path/to/zenodo/token/file    # file holding your Zenodo access token

cartloader upload_zenodo \
  --in-dir ./cartload2 \
  --upload-method catalog \
  --zenodo-token ${zenodo_token} \
  --title "Your Title" \
  --creators "Lastname, Firstname" \
  --description "This is an example description"

docs.title: Generic Platform Tutorial
docs.text:
Use the generic profile (--platform generic) for any platform without a dedicated profile, or whenever your data is a plain transcript table: one row per molecule (or per spatial bin and gene) with X, Y, gene, and optionally a count and a cell ID.

To show the workflow on real data, this tutorial treats the Xenium starter table, a small region of the adult mouse brain, as if it came from an unknown platform. It has the typical quirks of a table from another tool: comma-separated, its own column names, no count column, and a cell-ID column. (For actual Xenium data, use the Xenium profile instead.)

It first runs the whole analysis with a single run_together command, then walks through the same analysis step by step.

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text:
Download the example data, hosted on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.17953582), into a work directory:

work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # replace with your work directory
mkdir -p ${work_dir} && cd ${work_dir}
wget https://zenodo.org/records/17953582/files/xenium_starter.raw.tar.gz
tar --strip-components=1 -zxvf xenium_starter.raw.tar.gz   # extracts input.tsv.gz

input.tsv.gz is comma-separated despite its name. Its first lines:

"transcript_id","cell_id","overlaps_nucleus","feature_name","x_location","y_location","z_location","qv"
281827164036151,133793,1,"Sox10",2350.0232,4153.6846,16.592316,40.0

docs.title: Describe the Table
docs.text:
Tell run_together how to read the table:

What run_together needs In this file Option X and Y coordinates x_location, y_location --colname-transcript-x, --colname-transcript-y Gene name feature_name --colname-transcript-feature Count none: each row is one molecule --colname-transcript-count (omitted here) Coordinate unit micrometers --units-per-um 1 (input units per µm) Cell ID (optional) cell_id --colname-transcript-cell cell_id and --colname-cell cell_id Delimiter comma ingest.extra_flags in a config file (below); tab is the default

The delimiter has no command-line option, so set it in a small config file:

cat > generic_starter.json <<'EOF'
{ "ingest": { "extra_flags": ["--csv-delim ,"] } }
EOF

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Run the pipeline, either with a local installation or with the Docker image:

LocallyDocker 
cartloader run_together \
  --platform generic \
  --raw-transcript ./input.tsv.gz \
  --config generic_starter.json \
  --colname-transcript-x x_location \
  --colname-transcript-y y_location \
  --colname-transcript-feature feature_name \
  --colname-transcript-cell cell_id \
  --colname-cell cell_id \
  --units-per-um 1 \
  --out-dir ./out/generic_hippo \
  --id generic_hippo \
  --width 12 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

docker run --rm -v ${work_dir}:/data hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
  run_together \
  --platform generic \
  --raw-transcript /data/input.tsv.gz \
  --config /data/generic_starter.json \
  --colname-transcript-x x_location \
  --colname-transcript-y y_location \
  --colname-transcript-feature feature_name \
  --colname-transcript-cell cell_id \
  --colname-cell cell_id \
  --units-per-um 1 \
  --out-dir /data/out/generic_hippo \
  --id generic_hippo \
  --width 12 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

What happens:

  • SGE conversion reads the table with the column mapping above and writes the unified format. The generic profile drops negative-control and unassigned probes by default (^(Unassigned|Neg|BLANK|Blank|Intergenic|Deprecated|System|NCS-|NCP-)); set --ingest-exclude-feature-regex to change that.
  • FICTURE trains one model per --width × --n-factor combination and decodes every pixel.
  • Cell analysis runs because --colname-cell is given: transcripts are grouped by cell_id into cells, which are clustered with the largest model. Transcripts outside any cell (cell_id of -1 here) are ignored. Without the two cell options, the run stays pixel-level.
  • Packaging writes the deployable result to out/generic_hippo/cartl/generic_hippo/: a catalog.yaml and the PMTiles it lists.

Add --dry-run to print the commands without running them.

docs.title: Adapting It to Your Data
docs.text:
• A tab-separated table needs no config file: tab is the default delimiter.
  • A count column (e.g. UMIs per spatial bin): name it with --colname-transcript-count.
  • Other units: set --units-per-um to the number of coordinate units per micrometer, e.g. 1000 for nanometers (see How do I define scaling?).
  • No cell IDs: omit --colname-transcript-cell and --colname-cell.
  • Cell centroids or polygons from your segmentation can be added with --in-cell-xy and --in-cell-boundary; see the generic platform page for their formats, for several samples at once, and for a full config.

How run_together differs from the step-by-step path

  • FICTURE runs through run_ficture2_multi (a joint model over a single sample) with single-molecule pixel decoding, instead of run_ficture2.
  • Feature filters are the run_together defaults: control features (Unassigned, Neg, BLANK/Blank, Intergenic, Deprecated, System, NCS-, NCP-) are dropped at ingest; predicted (Gm<digit>), mitochondrial (mt-/MT-), and ribosomal (Rps/Rpl) genes stay in the data but are left out of the factor models. Change them with --ingest-exclude-feature-regex and --exclude-feature-regex.
  • Point layers are packaged with pmpoint (--use-pmpoint, 500 gene bins) instead of tippecanoe.
  • Outputs go under --out-dir: tsv/<id>/ (converted SGE), fic/ (FICTURE), and cartl/<id>/ (PMTiles and catalog.yaml; deploy this), instead of sge/, ficture2/, and cartload2/.
  • Publishing is built in: --s3-upload uploads cartl/<id>/ to S3 (see Publishing). For Zenodo, run upload_zenodo on cartl/<id>/ as in the step-by-step path.

docs.title: Step by Step (Individual Commands)
docs.text: The same pixel-level analysis, one command at a time. (The cell analysis that run_together adds is run by run_ficture2_multi_cells; it is easiest to get through run_together.)

docs.title: Set Up the Environment
docs.text:
# ====
# Replace the placeholders with values for your system.
# ====
work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # directory holding the input data; outputs are written here too
cd $work_dir

n_jobs=10                               # number of parallel jobs (also used as threads per job below)

# Activate the Python environment in which CartLoader is installed
conda activate ENV_NAME                 # replace ENV_NAME (or: source /path/to/venv/bin/activate)

No tool paths needed

Once submodules/build.sh has run (see Installation), every CartLoader command finds spatula, punkst, tippecanoe, pmtiles, and pmpoint in the submodules/ directory of the repository, and the default color map at assets/default_color_map.tsv. Pass --spatula, --ficture2 (the punkst repository directory, which contains bin/punkst), --tippecanoe, --pmtiles, or --cmap-file only to use a different build or file. upload_aws runs the aws CLI from your PATH (--aws to override).

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text: Use the data downloaded above.

docs.title: Define ID and Parameters
docs.text:
# Unique identifier for your dataset
DATA_ID="generic_hippo"                  # change this to reflect your dataset name

# LDA parameters
train_width=12                           # define LDA training hexagon width (comma-separated if multiple widths are applied)
n_factor=6,12                            # define number of factors in LDA training (comma-separated if multiple n-factor values are provided)

docs.title: SGE Format Conversion
docs.text:
Convert the table to the unified SGE format with sge_convert in generic mode. The --csv-* options play the role of run_together's --colname-transcript-* options:

cartloader sge_convert \
  --makefn sge_convert.mk \
  --platform generic \
  --in-csv ./input.tsv.gz \
  --csv-delim , \
  --csv-colname-x x_location \
  --csv-colname-y y_location \
  --csv-colname-feature-name feature_name \
  --units-per-um 1 \
  --out-dir ./sge \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(Unassigned|Neg|BLANK|Blank|Intergenic|Deprecated|System|NCS-|NCP-)' \
  --sge-visual \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs}

Without --csv-colname-count, each row counts as one molecule.

docs.title: FICTURE Analysis
docs.text:
Compute spatial factors using punkst (FICTURE2). See more details on the Reference page.

cartloader run_ficture2 \
  --makefn run_ficture2.mk \
  --main \
  --in-transcript ./sge/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz \
  --in-feature ./sge/feature.clean.tsv.gz \
  --in-minmax ./sge/coordinate_minmax.tsv \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(mt-.*$|Gm\d+$)' \
  --out-dir ./ficture2 \
  --width ${train_width} \
  --n-factor ${n_factor} \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs} \
  --threads ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --main required 1 flag Run all five main steps --in-transcript required string Path to the transcript-indexed SGE file from sge_convert --out-dir required string Output directory --width required int or comma-separated list Hexagon width(s) in µm for LDA training --n-factor required int or comma-separated list Number(s) of LDA factors; one model per width × factor combination --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: run_ficture2.mk) --in-feature string Path to the per-gene count file from sge_convert (default: the feature list made during tiling) --in-minmax string Path to the coordinate min/max file from sge_convert (default: the range computed during tiling) --exclude-feature-regex regex Feature names to leave out of the factor analysis. punkst matches the whole name, so end each alternative with .* or $ as needed (the example drops mitochondrial mt-* and predicted Gm<digits> genes) --cmap-file string Color map TSV (default: assets/default_color_map.tsv in the CartLoader repository) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1) --threads int Number of threads per job (default: 4)

1: CartLoader requires at least one action: --tile (tiling), --segment (hexagon segmentation), --init-lda (LDA training), --decode (pixel-level decoding), --umap (UMAP of the factors), or --main for all five.

docs.title: CartLoader Asset Packaging
docs.text:
Package the SGE and the FICTURE results into PMTiles and a catalog.yaml for CartoScope. See more details in its Reference page.

cartloader run_cartload2 \
  --makefn run_cartload2.mk \
  --fic-dir ./ficture2 \
  --out-dir ./cartload2 \
  --id ${DATA_ID} \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs} \
  --threads ${n_jobs}

Packaging without factor analysis

To host only the SGE (no factors), use cartloader run_together ... --no-ficture, which tiles the transcripts and packages them without training any model.

Parameter Required Type Description --fic-dir required string FICTURE output directory from run_ficture2; must contain ficture.params.json (the SGE paths are read from it) --out-dir required string Output directory for the PMTiles, assets, and catalog.yaml --id required string Dataset ID used in the catalog and output metadata (no whitespace) --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: run_cartload2.mk) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1) --threads int Number of threads per job (default: 4) --spatula, --tippecanoe, --pmtiles string Tool paths (default: the copies built under submodules/)

docs.title: Upload to Data Repository
docs.text:
Choose a data repository to host/share your output

CartLoader supports two upload options (AWS and Zenodo) for storing PMTiles of SGE and spatial factors in a data repository.

Choose the one that best suits your needs.

AWS UploadsZenodo Uploads

Upload the generated CartLoader outputs to your designated AWS S3 directory. The aws CLI must be configured with credentials that can write there (see AWS Upload Failures).

# AWS S3 target location
S3_DIR=s3://your-bucket/path/to/dir     # recommended: end with DATA_ID, e.g. s3://your-bucket/test-data/${DATA_ID}

cartloader upload_aws \
  --in-dir ./cartload2 \
  --s3-dir "${S3_DIR}" \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --in-dir required string Directory with the CartLoader packaging output (containing catalog.yaml) --s3-dir required string Target S3 directory --profile string AWS CLI profile to use --aws string Path to the AWS CLI (default: aws) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 2)

Upload the generated CartLoader outputs to a new Zenodo deposition or an existing one (see Zenodo Setup for the access token).

zenodo_token=/path/to/zenodo/token/file    # file holding your Zenodo access token

cartloader upload_zenodo \
  --in-dir ./cartload2 \
  --upload-method catalog \
  --zenodo-token ${zenodo_token} \
  --title "Your Title" \
  --creators "Lastname, Firstname" \
  --description "This is an example description"

docs.title: Vizgen MERSCOPE Starter Tutorial
docs.text:
The input is an SGE dataset from the adult mouse hippocampus, extracted by masking a coronal brain section (Slice Number: 2; Replicate Number: 1; file: detected_transcripts.csv) from Vizgen MERSCOPE Neuroscience Showcase.

It first runs the whole analysis with a single run_together command, then walks through the same analysis step by step: input preparation, SGE format conversion, FICTURE analysis, asset packaging, and data upload.

docs.title: Run with run_together
docs.text:
Download the example data, hosted on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.17953582), into a work directory:

work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # replace with your work directory
mkdir -p ${work_dir} && cd ${work_dir}
wget https://zenodo.org/records/17953582/files/merscope_starter.raw.tar.gz
tar --strip-components=1 -zxvf merscope_starter.raw.tar.gz   # extracts input.tsv.gz

Then run the pipeline, either with a local installation or with the Docker image:

LocallyDocker 
cartloader run_together \
  --platform merfish \
  --raw-transcript ./input.tsv.gz \
  --out-dir ./out/merscope_hippo \
  --id merscope_hippo \
  --width 12 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

docker run --rm -v ${work_dir}:/data hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
  run_together \
  --platform merfish \
  --raw-transcript /data/input.tsv.gz \
  --out-dir /data/out/merscope_hippo \
  --id merscope_hippo \
  --width 12 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

The MERSCOPE profile (--platform merfish) reads the transcript file named by --raw-transcript. The result to deploy is out/merscope_hippo/cartl/merscope_hippo/ (a catalog.yaml and the PMTiles it lists). Add --dry-run to print the commands without running them.

How run_together differs from the step-by-step path

  • FICTURE runs through run_ficture2_multi (a joint model over a single sample) with single-molecule pixel decoding, instead of run_ficture2.
  • Feature filters are the run_together defaults: control features (Unassigned, Neg, BLANK/Blank, Intergenic, Deprecated, System, NCS-, NCP-) are dropped at ingest; predicted (Gm<digit>), mitochondrial (mt-/MT-), and ribosomal (Rps/Rpl) genes stay in the data but are left out of the factor models. Change them with --ingest-exclude-feature-regex and --exclude-feature-regex.
  • Point layers are packaged with pmpoint (--use-pmpoint, 500 gene bins) instead of tippecanoe.
  • Outputs go under --out-dir: tsv/<id>/ (converted SGE), fic/ (FICTURE), and cartl/<id>/ (PMTiles and catalog.yaml; deploy this), instead of sge/, ficture2/, and cartload2/.
  • Publishing is built in: --s3-upload uploads cartl/<id>/ to S3 (see Publishing). For Zenodo, run upload_zenodo on cartl/<id>/ as in the step-by-step path.

docs.text: The same analysis, one command at a time. Use it to understand each stage or to customize it.

docs.title: Set Up the Environment
docs.text:

Pass --spatula, --ficture2 (the punkst repository directory, which contains bin/punkst), --tippecanoe, --pmtiles, or --cmap-file only to use a different build or file. upload_aws runs the aws CLI from your PATH (--aws to override).

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text:
Use the data downloaded above.

The MERSCOPE input SGE includes one comma‑delimited text file (detected_transcripts.csv; input.tsv.gz in the starter data) in the following format:

CSV File Format

,barcode_id,global_x,global_y,global_z,x,y,fov,gene
0,22,56.930107,3851.851,5.0,147.80061,1711.9067,0,Adgre1
1,22,183.60107,3874.0085,5.0,1320.6799,1917.0692,0,Adgre1
2,22,59.750736,3666.5576,5.0,132.66754,1844.2372,1,Adgre1
  • Column 1: Unique numeric index for each transcript within a field of view (non-consecutive, ascending).
  • barcode_id: Zero-based index of the transcript barcode in the codebook; forms a composite key with fov.
  • global_x: Transcript x coordinates (µm) in the experimental region; may be negative due to alignment.
  • global_y: Transcript y coordinates (µm) in the experimental region; may be negative due to alignment.
  • global_z: Zero‑based z‑position index.
  • x: The x-coordinate of the transcript (µm), within the coordinate space of the field of view.
  • y: The y-coordinate of the transcript (µm), within the coordinate space of the field of view.
  • fov: Zero-based field of view index; forms a composite key with barcode_id.
  • gene: Gene name associated with the transcript.

docs.text:
# Unique identifier for your dataset
DATA_ID="merscope_hippo"                # change this to reflect your dataset name
PLATFORM="vizgen_merscope"              # platform information

How to define Scaling Factors for MERSCOPE?

The MERSCOPE example data currently used here provides SGE in µm. Define the scaling factor from coordinate units to micrometers as 1.
