docs.title: Pixel-Seq Starter Tutorial
docs.text:
Since the Pixel-Seq publication provides SGE data only from the mouse olfactory bulb and parabrachial nucleus — neither of which includes the hippocampus — we extract a subregion from the olfactory bulb as the input for this tutorial.

It first runs the whole analysis with a single run_together command, then walks through the same analysis step by step: input preparation, SGE format conversion, FICTURE analysis, asset packaging, and data upload.

docs.title: Run with run_together
docs.text:
Download the example data, hosted on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.17953582), into a work directory:

work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # replace with your work directory
mkdir -p ${work_dir} && cd ${work_dir}
wget https://zenodo.org/records/17953582/files/pixelseq_starter.raw.tar.gz
tar --strip-components=1 -zxvf pixelseq_starter.raw.tar.gz   # extracts input.tsv.gz

Then run the pipeline, either with a local installation or with the Docker image:

LocallyDocker 
cartloader run_together \
  --platform generic \
  --raw-transcript ./input.tsv.gz \
  --colname-transcript-x xcoord \
  --colname-transcript-y ycoord \
  --colname-transcript-feature geneName \
  --units-per-um 3.076923 \
  --out-dir ./out/pixelseq_hippo \
  --id pixelseq_hippo \
  --width 18 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

docker run --rm -v ${work_dir}:/data hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
  run_together \
  --platform generic \
  --raw-transcript /data/input.tsv.gz \
  --colname-transcript-x xcoord \
  --colname-transcript-y ycoord \
  --colname-transcript-feature geneName \
  --units-per-um 3.076923 \
  --out-dir /data/out/pixelseq_hippo \
  --id pixelseq_hippo \
  --width 18 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

Pixel-seq has no dedicated run_together profile, so the tab-separated file goes through the generic profile: the --colname-transcript-* options name its coordinate and gene columns (each row counts as one molecule, as in the step-by-step path), and --units-per-um sets the pixel size. The result to deploy is out/pixelseq_hippo/cartl/pixelseq_hippo/ (a catalog.yaml and the PMTiles it lists). Add --dry-run to print the commands without running them.

How run_together differs from the step-by-step path

  • FICTURE runs through run_ficture2_multi (a joint model over a single sample) with single-molecule pixel decoding, instead of run_ficture2.
  • Feature filters are the run_together defaults: control features (Unassigned, Neg, BLANK/Blank, Intergenic, Deprecated, System, NCS-, NCP-) are dropped at ingest; predicted (Gm<digit>), mitochondrial (mt-/MT-), and ribosomal (Rps/Rpl) genes stay in the data but are left out of the factor models. Change them with --ingest-exclude-feature-regex and --exclude-feature-regex.
  • Point layers are packaged with pmpoint (--use-pmpoint, 500 gene bins) instead of tippecanoe.
  • Outputs go under --out-dir: tsv/<id>/ (converted SGE), fic/ (FICTURE), and cartl/<id>/ (PMTiles and catalog.yaml; deploy this), instead of sge/, ficture2/, and cartload2/.
  • Publishing is built in: --s3-upload uploads cartl/<id>/ to S3 (see Publishing). For Zenodo, run upload_zenodo on cartl/<id>/ as in the step-by-step path.

docs.title: Step by Step (Individual Commands)
docs.text: The same analysis, one command at a time. Use it to understand each stage or to customize it.

docs.title: Set Up the Environment
docs.text:
# ====
# Replace the placeholders with values for your system.
# ====
work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # directory holding the input data; outputs are written here too
cd $work_dir

n_jobs=10                               # number of parallel jobs (also used as threads per job below)

# Activate the Python environment in which CartLoader is installed
conda activate ENV_NAME                 # replace ENV_NAME (or: source /path/to/venv/bin/activate)

No tool paths needed

Once submodules/build.sh has run (see Installation), every CartLoader command finds spatula, punkst, tippecanoe, pmtiles, and pmpoint in the submodules/ directory of the repository, and the default color map at assets/default_color_map.tsv. Pass --spatula, --ficture2 (the punkst repository directory, which contains bin/punkst), --tippecanoe, --pmtiles, or --cmap-file only to use a different build or file. upload_aws runs the aws CLI from your PATH (--aws to override).

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text:
Use the data downloaded above.

The Pixel-Seq SGE includes one tab-delimited text file (input.tsv.gz in the starter data), where each row represents a unique RNA molecule detected within a defined field of view (FOV), with associated genomic and spatial metadata.

TSV file format

FOVx  FOVy  xcoord     ycoord     UMIs     SpatialBarcode            MapStrand  Chrom  Start      STARmapping        Counts  geneID              geneName  bioType                 intronRatio
017   005   26691.5    5786.5     TAACGAA  AAGGTTCATACCTACGACTGTTAA  16         1      24613729   150M               1       ENSMUSG00000101111  Gm28437   unprocessed_pseudogene  0.00
016   007   27590.25   4639.0815  TAATATA  AATGGCGCATTTTGCTGTTTAGGC  16         2      39001628   138M2341N12M       1       ENSMUSG00000062997  Rpl35     protein_coding          0.00
018   006   25099.945  5621.8335  AGTTGTA  CTGCATATGTGTCACCTAGGTAGC  16         1      24615767   150M               1       ENSMUSG00000101249  Gm29216   unprocessed_pseudogene  0.00
  • FOVx, FOVy: Field-of-view indices indicating the imaging tile coordinates in the x and y directions.
  • xcoord, ycoord: Spatial coordinates (in microns or pixels).
  • UMIs: Unique molecular identifier (UMI) sequence.
  • SpatialBarcode: Spatial barcode capturing the location and identity.
  • MapStrand: Indicates the strand orientation of the mapped read.
  • Chrom, Start: Chromosome number and start position of the mapped read on the genome.
  • STARmapping: Alignment pattern (CIGAR string) from the STAR aligner indicating how the transcript maps to the genome.
  • Counts: Number of times the UMI/gene combination was observed.
  • geneID, geneName: Ensembl gene ID and gene symbol.
  • bioType: Gene biotype.
  • intronRatio: Fraction of UMI counts assigned to intronic regions.

docs.title: Define ID and Parameters
docs.text:
# Unique identifier for your dataset
DATA_ID="pixelseq_hippo"                # change this to reflect your dataset name
PLATFORM="pixel_seq"                    # platform information
SCALE=3.076923                          # coordinate units per micrometer

# LDA parameters
train_width=18                           # define LDA training hexagon width (comma-separated if multiple widths are applied)
n_factor=6,12                            # define number of factors in LDA training (comma-separated if multiple n-factor values are provided)

How to define Scaling Factors for Pixel-Seq?

In Pixel-Seq publication:

"Because polonies have varied sizes and shapes, to maximize the feature resolution we developed a base-calling pipeline to determine the major barcode species in each pixel (0.325 × 0.325 µm²) of gel images to construct a spatial barcode map".

Accordingly, we defined scale as 1/0.325 = 3.076923

docs.title: SGE Format Conversion
docs.text:
Convert the raw input to the unified SGE format. See more details in its Reference page.

cartloader sge_convert \
  --makefn sge_convert.mk \
  --platform ${PLATFORM} \
  --in-csv ./input.tsv.gz \
  --units-per-um ${SCALE} \
  --out-dir ./sge \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(BLANK|Neg|Intergenic|Deprecated|Unassigned)' \
  --sge-visual \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --platform required string Input platform, which sets the default input columns and delimiter (options: 10x_visium_hd, seqscope, illumina, 10x_xenium, bgi_stereoseq, cosmx_smi, vizgen_merscope, pixel_seq, nova_st, generic) --in-csv required string Path to the input transcript CSV/TSV file --out-dir required string Output directory for the converted SGE files --units-per-um float Coordinate units per µm in the input (default: 1, i.e. already in µm; 1000 for the Seq-Scope raw TSV; detected from the barcodes for illumina) --csv-colname-feature-name string Gene-name column in the input (default: set by --platform) --csv-colname-count string Count column in the input (default: set by --platform; without one, each row counts 1) --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: sge_convert.mk) --exclude-feature-regex regex Pattern of feature names to drop (e.g. control probes) --sge-visual flag Draw the converted SGE as an image (xy.png) for a visual check --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1)

docs.title: FICTURE Analysis
docs.text:
Compute spatial factors using punkst (FICTURE2). See more details on the Reference page.

cartloader run_ficture2 \
  --makefn run_ficture2.mk \
  --main \
  --in-transcript ./sge/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz \
  --in-feature ./sge/feature.clean.tsv.gz \
  --in-minmax ./sge/coordinate_minmax.tsv \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(mt-.*$|Gm\d+$)' \
  --out-dir ./ficture2 \
  --width ${train_width} \
  --n-factor ${n_factor} \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs} \
  --threads ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --main required 1 flag Run all five main steps --in-transcript required string Path to the transcript-indexed SGE file from sge_convert --out-dir required string Output directory --width required int or comma-separated list Hexagon width(s) in µm for LDA training --n-factor required int or comma-separated list Number(s) of LDA factors; one model per width × factor combination --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: run_ficture2.mk) --in-feature string Path to the per-gene count file from sge_convert (default: the feature list made during tiling) --in-minmax string Path to the coordinate min/max file from sge_convert (default: the range computed during tiling) --exclude-feature-regex regex Feature names to leave out of the factor analysis. punkst matches the whole name, so end each alternative with .* or $ as needed (the example drops mitochondrial mt-* and predicted Gm<digits> genes) --cmap-file string Color map TSV (default: assets/default_color_map.tsv in the CartLoader repository) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1) --threads int Number of threads per job (default: 4)

1: CartLoader requires at least one action: --tile (tiling), --segment (hexagon segmentation), --init-lda (LDA training), --decode (pixel-level decoding), --umap (UMAP of the factors), or --main for all five.

docs.title: CartLoader Asset Packaging
docs.text:
Package the SGE and the FICTURE results into PMTiles and a catalog.yaml for CartoScope. See more details in its Reference page.

cartloader run_cartload2 \
  --makefn run_cartload2.mk \
  --fic-dir ./ficture2 \
  --out-dir ./cartload2 \
  --id ${DATA_ID} \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs} \
  --threads ${n_jobs}

Packaging without factor analysis

To host only the SGE (no factors), use cartloader run_together ... --no-ficture, which tiles the transcripts and packages them without training any model.

Choose a data repository to host/share your output

  --n-jobs ${n_jobs}

  • FICTURE runs through run_ficture2_multi (a joint model over a single sample) with single-molecule pixel decoding, instead of run_ficture2.
  • Feature filters are the run_together defaults: control features (Unassigned, Neg, BLANK/Blank, Intergenic, Deprecated, System, NCS-, NCP-) are dropped at ingest; predicted (Gm<digit>), mitochondrial (mt-/MT-), and ribosomal (Rps/Rpl) genes stay in the data but are left out of the factor models.   • Point layers are packaged with pmpoint (--use-pmpoint, 500 gene bins) instead of tippecanoe.
  • Outputs go under --out-dir: tsv/<id>/ (converted SGE), fic/ (FICTURE), and cartl/<id>/ (PMTiles and catalog.yaml; deploy this), instead of sge/, ficture2/, and cartload2/.

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text:
Use the data downloaded above. Actual input formats are platform-dependent; see the other platform tutorials for theirs.

SeqScope provides SGE with three files:

barcodes.tsv.gz – spatial barcode metadata 
AAAACAAAAACCTTCTTCGGACACTGGTCT  1   20  1   1   295288  1422349 0,1,0,0,0
AAAACAAAAATCCTGTTATACATGCCATGG  2   45  1   1   1745544 1110720 2,2,1,0,1
AAAACAAAACACGGGAAAAAACTATAGGTG  3   58  1   1   887244  250820  7,7,5,0,1
  • Column 1: Sorted spatial barcodes
  • Column 2: 1-based integer index of spatial barcodes, used in matrix.mtx.gz
  • Column 3: 1-based integer index from the full barcode that is in the STARsolo output
  • Column 4: Lane ID (fixed as 1)
  • Column 5: Tile ID (fixed as 1)
  • Column 6: X-coordinates
  • Column 7: Y-coordinates
  • Column 8: Five comma-separated numbers denote the count per spatial barcode for "Gene", "GeneFull", "Spliced", "Unspliced", and "Ambiguous".
features.tsv.gz – feature metadata 
ENSMUSG00000100764  Gm29155 1   1,1,1,0,0
ENSMUSG00000100635  Gm29157 2   0,0,0,0,0
ENSMUSG00000100480  Gm29156 3   0,0,0,0,0
  • Column 1: Feature ID
  • Column 2: Feature symbol
  • Column 3: 1-based integer index of genes, used in matrix.mtx.gz
  • Column 4: Five comma-separated numbers denote the count per gene "Gene", "GeneFull", "Spliced", "Unspliced", and "Ambiguous".
matrix.mtx.gz – expression count matrix 
%%MatrixMarket matrix coordinate integer general
%
33989 2928173 5404336
2487 1 0 1 0 0 0
5104 2 1 1 0 0 1
  • Header: Initial lines form the header, declaring the matrix's adherence to the Market Matrix (MTX) format, outlining its traits. This may include comments (lines beginning with %) for extra metadata, all marked by a “%”.
  • Dimensions: Following the header, the first line details the matrix dimensions: the count of rows (features), columns (barcodes), and non-zero entries.
  • Data Entries: After the dimensions, subsequent lines enumerate non‑zero entries in seven columns: row index (feature index), column index (barcode index), and five values (expression levels) corresponding to "Gene", "GeneFull", "Spliced", "Unspliced", and "Ambiguous".
    • "Gene": represents unique, confidently mapped transcript count ("gene name"-based);
    • "GeneFull": denotes total transcript count assigned to gene (includes ambiguities).

S3_DIR=s3://your-bucket/path/to/dir     # recommended: end with DATA_ID, e.g. s3://your-bucket/test-data/${DATA_ID}

cartloader upload_aws \
  --in-dir ./cartload2 \
  --s3-dir "${S3_DIR}" \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --in-dir required string Directory with the CartLoader packaging output (containing catalog.yaml) --s3-dir required string Target S3 directory --profile string AWS CLI profile to use --aws string Path to the AWS CLI (default: aws) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 2)

Upload the generated CartLoader outputs to a new Zenodo deposition or an existing one (see Zenodo Setup for the access token).

zenodo_token=/path/to/zenodo/token/file    # file holding your Zenodo access token

cartloader upload_zenodo \
  --in-dir ./cartload2 \
  --upload-method catalog \
  --zenodo-token ${zenodo_token} \
  --title "Your Title" \
  --creators "Lastname, Firstname" \
  --description "This is an example description"
Parameter Required Type Description --in-dir required string Directory with the CartLoader packaging output --zenodo-token required string Path to the file holding your Zenodo access token --upload-method string Which files to upload: all (every file in --in-dir; default), catalog (the files listed in catalog.yaml), or files (the names given with --files) --catalog-yaml string Catalog to read with --upload-method catalog (default: <in-dir>/catalog.yaml) --zenodo-deposition-id string Existing deposition to upload into (default: create a new one) --title required 1 string Title of the deposition --creators required 1 list of str Creators in "Lastname, Firstname" format, each quoted --description string Description of the deposition

1: Required when creating a new deposition, or when the existing one lacks it.

docs.title: Stereo-seq Starter Tutorial
docs.text:
The input data represents the mouse hippocampus. For demonstration purposes, we selected an adult mouse brain coronal section from the official release and extracted only the hippocampus region. The full-section data is sourced from the Stereo-seq platform as part of the MOSTA project.

It first runs the whole analysis with a single run_together command, then walks through the same analysis step by step: input preparation, SGE format conversion, FICTURE analysis, asset packaging, and data upload.

docs.title: Run with run_together
docs.text:
Download the example data, hosted on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.17953582), into a work directory:

work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # replace with your work directory
mkdir -p ${work_dir} && cd ${work_dir}
wget https://zenodo.org/records/17953582/files/stereoseq_starter.raw.tar.gz
tar --strip-components=1 -zxvf stereoseq_starter.raw.tar.gz   # extracts input.tsv.gz

Then run the pipeline, either with a local installation or with the Docker image:

LocallyDocker 
cartloader run_together \
  --platform generic \
  --raw-transcript ./input.tsv.gz \
  --colname-transcript-x x \
  --colname-transcript-y y \
  --colname-transcript-feature geneID \
  --colname-transcript-count MIDCounts \
  --units-per-um 2 \
  --out-dir ./out/stereoseq_hippo \
  --id stereoseq_hippo \
  --width 18 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

docker run --rm -v ${work_dir}:/data hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
  run_together \
  --platform generic \
  --raw-transcript /data/input.tsv.gz \
  --colname-transcript-x x \
  --colname-transcript-y y \
  --colname-transcript-feature geneID \
  --colname-transcript-count MIDCounts \
  --units-per-um 2 \
  --out-dir /data/out/stereoseq_hippo \
  --id stereoseq_hippo \
  --width 18 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

The Stereo-seq profile ingests SAW .gef files (and needs the SAW binary), so a text GEM file like this one goes through the generic profile instead: the --colname-transcript-* options name its columns, and --units-per-um 2 converts its 0.5 µm grid to µm. The result to deploy is out/stereoseq_hippo/cartl/stereoseq_hippo/ (a catalog.yaml and the PMTiles it lists). Add --dry-run to print the commands without running them.

How run_together differs from the step-by-step path

  • FICTURE runs through run_ficture2_multi (a joint model over a single sample) with single-molecule pixel decoding, instead of run_ficture2.
  • Feature filters are the run_together defaults: control features (Unassigned, Neg, BLANK/Blank, Intergenic, Deprecated, System, NCS-, NCP-) are dropped at ingest; predicted (Gm<digit>), mitochondrial (mt-/MT-), and ribosomal (Rps/Rpl) genes stay in the data but are left out of the factor models. Change them with --ingest-exclude-feature-regex and --exclude-feature-regex.
  • Point layers are packaged with pmpoint (--use-pmpoint, 500 gene bins) instead of tippecanoe.
  • Outputs go under --out-dir: tsv/<id>/ (converted SGE), fic/ (FICTURE), and cartl/<id>/ (PMTiles and catalog.yaml; deploy this), instead of sge/, ficture2/, and cartload2/.
  • Publishing is built in: --s3-upload uploads cartl/<id>/ to S3 (see Publishing). For Zenodo, run upload_zenodo on cartl/<id>/ as in the step-by-step path.

docs.title: Step by Step (Individual Commands)
docs.text: The same analysis, one command at a time. Use it to understand each stage or to customize it.

docs.title: Set Up the Environment
docs.text:
# ====
# Replace the placeholders with values for your system.
# ====
work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # directory holding the input data; outputs are written here too
cd $work_dir

n_jobs=10                               # number of parallel jobs (also used as threads per job below)

# Activate the Python environment in which CartLoader is installed
conda activate ENV_NAME                 # replace ENV_NAME (or: source /path/to/venv/bin/activate)

No tool paths needed

Once submodules/build.sh has run (see Installation), every CartLoader command finds spatula, punkst, tippecanoe, pmtiles, and pmpoint in the submodules/ directory of the repository, and the default color map at assets/default_color_map.tsv. Pass --spatula, --ficture2 (the punkst repository directory, which contains bin/punkst), --tippecanoe, --pmtiles, or --cmap-file only to use a different build or file. upload_aws runs the aws CLI from your PATH (--aws to override).

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text:
Use the data downloaded above.

Stereo‑seq SGE includes one tab‑delimited “Bin1” gene expression matrix (GEM) file, input.tsv.gz in the starter data:

TSV File Format

geneID          x       y       MIDCounts
0610005C13Rik   6632    9074    1
0610005C13Rik   8651    8935    1
0610005C13Rik   7228    12814   2
  • geneID: Gene symbol.
  • x: X coordinate of each DNB on the capture chip.
  • y: Y coordinate of each DNB on the capture chip.
  • MIDCounts: UMI count for each gene at each DNB.

Column names differ between SAW versions

This MOSTA file names its columns geneID (gene symbol) and MIDCounts. GEM files from current SAW versions use geneName and ExonCount instead, which are the defaults of the bgi_stereoseq preset, so this tutorial names the starter file's columns explicitly.

docs.title: Define ID and Parameters
docs.text:
# Unique identifier for your dataset
DATA_ID="stereoseq_hippo"                # change this to reflect your dataset name
PLATFORM="bgi_stereoseq"                 # platform information
SCALE=2                                  # coordinate units per micrometer

# LDA parameters
train_width=18                           # define LDA training hexagon width (comma-separated if multiple widths are applied)
n_factor=6,12                            # define number of factors in LDA training (comma-separated if multiple n-factor values are provided)

How to define Scaling Factors for Stereo-seq?

According to the Stereo-seq paper, the technology features spot sizes of approximately 220 nanometers in diameter with center-to-center distances of about 500 nanometers. Thus, each pixel corresponds to approximately 0.5 micrometers. The scaling factor from coordinate to µm is defined as 2.

docs.title: SGE Format Conversion
docs.text:
Convert the raw input to the unified SGE format. See more details in its Reference page. The --csv-colname-* options name the starter file's gene and count columns (see the note above).

cartloader sge_convert \
  --makefn sge_convert.mk \
  --platform ${PLATFORM} \
  --in-csv ./input.tsv.gz \
  --csv-colname-feature-name geneID \
  --csv-colname-count MIDCounts \
  --units-per-um ${SCALE} \
  --out-dir ./sge \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(BLANK|Neg|Intergenic|Deprecated|Unassigned)' \
  --sge-visual \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --platform required string Input platform, which sets the default input columns and delimiter (options: 10x_visium_hd, seqscope, illumina, 10x_xenium, bgi_stereoseq, cosmx_smi, vizgen_merscope, pixel_seq, nova_st, generic) --in-csv required string Path to the input transcript CSV/TSV file --out-dir required string Output directory for the converted SGE files --units-per-um float Coordinate units per µm in the input (default: 1, i.e. already in µm; 1000 for the Seq-Scope raw TSV; detected from the barcodes for illumina) --csv-colname-feature-name string Gene-name column in the input (default: set by --platform) --csv-colname-count string Count column in the input (default: set by --platform; without one, each row counts 1) --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: sge_convert.mk) --exclude-feature-regex regex Pattern of feature names to drop (e.g. control probes) --sge-visual flag Draw the converted SGE as an image (xy.png) for a visual check --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1)

docs.title: FICTURE Analysis
docs.text:
Compute spatial factors using punkst (FICTURE2). See more details on the Reference page.

cartloader run_ficture2 \
  --makefn run_ficture2.mk \
  --main \
  --in-transcript ./sge/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz \
  --in-feature ./sge/feature.clean.tsv.gz \
  --in-minmax ./sge/coordinate_minmax.tsv \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(mt-.*$|Gm\d+$)' \
  --out-dir ./ficture2 \
  --width ${train_width} \
  --n-factor ${n_factor} \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs} \
  --threads ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --main required 1 flag Run all five main steps --in-transcript required string Path to the transcript-indexed SGE file from sge_convert --out-dir required string Output directory --width required int or comma-separated list Hexagon width(s) in µm for LDA training --n-factor required int or comma-separated list Number(s) of LDA factors; one model per width × factor combination --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: run_ficture2.mk) --in-feature string Path to the per-gene count file from sge_convert (default: the feature list made during tiling) --in-minmax string Path to the coordinate min/max file from sge_convert (default: the range computed during tiling) --exclude-feature-regex regex Feature names to leave out of the factor analysis. punkst matches the whole name, so end each alternative with .* or $ as needed (the example drops mitochondrial mt-* and predicted Gm<digits> genes) --cmap-file string Color map TSV (default: assets/default_color_map.tsv in the CartLoader repository) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1) --threads int Number of threads per job (default: 4)

1: CartLoader requires at least one action: --tile (tiling), --segment (hexagon segmentation), --init-lda (LDA training), --decode (pixel-level decoding), --umap (UMAP of the factors), or --main for all five.

docs.title: CartLoader Asset Packaging
docs.text:
Package the SGE and the FICTURE results into PMTiles and a catalog.yaml for CartoScope. See more details in its Reference page.

cartloader run_cartload2 \
  --makefn run_cartload2.mk \
  --fic-dir ./ficture2 \
  --out-dir ./cartload2 \
  --id ${DATA_ID} \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs} \
  --threads ${n_jobs}

Packaging without factor analysis

To host only the SGE (no factors), use cartloader run_together ... --no-ficture, which tiles the transcripts and packages them without training any model.

Parameter Required Type Description --fic-dir required string FICTURE output directory from run_ficture2; must contain ficture.params.json (the SGE paths are read from it) --out-dir required string Output directory for the PMTiles, assets, and catalog.yaml --id required string Dataset ID used in the catalog and output metadata (no whitespace) --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: run_cartload2.mk) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1) --threads int Number of threads per job (default: 4) --spatula, --tippecanoe, --pmtiles string Tool paths (default: the copies built under submodules/)

docs.title: 10x Visium HD Starter Tutorial
docs.text:
The input data originates from the mouse hippocampus and is extracted from an official release of mouse brain SGE data.

It first runs the whole analysis with a single run_together command, then walks through the same analysis step by step: input preparation, SGE format conversion, FICTURE analysis, asset packaging, and data upload.

docs.title: Run with run_together
docs.text:
Download the example data, hosted on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.17953582), into a work directory:

work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # replace with your work directory
mkdir -p ${work_dir} && cd ${work_dir}
wget https://zenodo.org/records/17953582/files/visiumhd_starter.raw.tar.gz
tar -zxvf visiumhd_starter.raw.tar.gz   # creates raw/ with the 2 µm MEX files, tissue_positions.parquet, scalefactors_json.json

The 10x Visium HD profile expects a Space Ranger outs/ directory, where these files sit under binned_outputs/square_002um/. The starter data keeps them flat in raw/, so write a small config file that points the profile at them (paths are relative to --in-dir):

cat > visiumhd_starter.json <<'EOF'
{
  "ingest": {
    "inputs": {
      "--in-mex": ".",
      "--pos-parquet": "tissue_positions.parquet",
      "--scale-json": "scalefactors_json.json"
    }
  }
}
EOF

Then run the pipeline, either with a local installation or with the Docker image:

LocallyDocker 
cartloader run_together \
  --platform 10x_visium_hd \
  --in-dir ./raw \
  --config visiumhd_starter.json \
  --out-dir ./out/visiumhd_hippo \
  --id visiumhd_hippo \
  --width 18 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

docker run --rm -v ${work_dir}:/data hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
  run_together \
  --platform 10x_visium_hd \
  --in-dir /data/raw \
  --config /data/visiumhd_starter.json \
  --out-dir /data/out/visiumhd_hippo \
  --id visiumhd_hippo \
  --width 18 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

The result to deploy is out/visiumhd_hippo/cartl/visiumhd_hippo/ (a catalog.yaml and the PMTiles it lists). Add --dry-run to print the commands without running them. With a full Space Ranger outs/ directory, drop --config: the profile then also imports the segmented cells, the 8 µm and 16 µm bins, and the H&E image when present.

How run_together differs from the step-by-step path

  • FICTURE runs through run_ficture2_multi (a joint model over a single sample) with single-molecule pixel decoding, instead of run_ficture2.
  • Feature filters are the run_together defaults: control features (Unassigned, Neg, BLANK/Blank, Intergenic, Deprecated, System, NCS-, NCP-) are dropped at ingest; predicted (Gm<digit>), mitochondrial (mt-/MT-), and ribosomal (Rps/Rpl) genes stay in the data but are left out of the factor models. Change them with --ingest-exclude-feature-regex and --exclude-feature-regex.
  • Point layers are packaged with pmpoint (--use-pmpoint, 500 gene bins) instead of tippecanoe.
  • Outputs go under --out-dir: tsv/<id>/ (converted SGE), fic/ (FICTURE), and cartl/<id>/ (PMTiles and catalog.yaml; deploy this), instead of sge/, ficture2/, and cartload2/.
  • Publishing is built in: --s3-upload uploads cartl/<id>/ to S3 (see Publishing). For Zenodo, run upload_zenodo on cartl/<id>/ as in the step-by-step path.

docs.title: Step by Step (Individual Commands)
docs.text: The same analysis, one command at a time. Use it to understand each stage or to customize it.

docs.title: Set Up the Environment
docs.text:
# ====
# Replace the placeholders with values for your system.
# ====
work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # directory holding the input data; outputs are written here too
cd $work_dir

n_jobs=10                               # number of parallel jobs (also used as threads per job below)

# Activate the Python environment in which CartLoader is installed
conda activate ENV_NAME                 # replace ENV_NAME (or: source /path/to/venv/bin/activate)

No tool paths needed

Once submodules/build.sh has run (see Installation), every CartLoader command finds spatula, punkst, tippecanoe, pmtiles, and pmpoint in the submodules/ directory of the repository, and the default color map at assets/default_color_map.tsv. Pass --spatula, --ficture2 (the punkst repository directory, which contains bin/punkst), --tippecanoe, --pmtiles, or --cmap-file only to use a different build or file. upload_aws runs the aws CLI from your PATH (--aws to override).

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text:
Use the data downloaded above.

Visium HD slides use a 2×2 µm grid of barcoded squares (square_002um) for high-resolution spatial gene mapping. Use filtered_feature_bc_matrix to only process tissue-associated signals.

ATTENTION

The file‑format examples below use a sample Visium HD dataset. Paths, IDs, and values are illustrative and may not match the dataset used in this tutorial.

SGE comprises several key files as follows:

filtered_feature_bc_matrix/barcodes.tsv.gz – spatial barcode for tissue locations 
s_002um_00639_00600-1
s_002um_00923_01639-1
s_002um_01050_01530-1
  • Column 1: Spatial barcodes corresponding to specific locations on the tissue section.
filtered_feature_bc_matrix/features.tsv.gz – feature metadata 
ENSMUSG00000051951  Xkr4    Gene Expression
ENSMUSG00000025900  Rp1     Gene Expression
ENSMUSG00000025902  Sox17   Gene Expression
  • Column 1: Feature ID
  • Column 2: Feature symbol
  • Column 3: Feature type
filtered_feature_bc_matrix/matrix.mtx.gz – expression count matrix 
%%MatrixMarket matrix coordinate integer general
%
19059 869411 11376563
3606 1 1
8957 1 1
9733 1 1
  • Header: Initial lines form the header, declaring the matrix's adherence to the Market Matrix (MTX) format, outlining its traits. This may include comments (lines beginning with %) for extra metadata, all marked by a “%”.
  • Dimensions: Following the header, the first line details the matrix dimensions: the count of rows (features), columns (barcodes), and non-zero entries.
  • Data Entries: After the dimensions, each subsequent line provides three fields: row index (feature index), column index (barcode index), and the expression-count value.
tissue_positions.parquet – spatial barcode metadata 
barcode                 in_tissue   array_row   array_col   pxl_row_in_fullres  pxl_col_in_fullres
s_002um_00434_01637-1   1           434         1637        3396.371014         9125.919898
  • barcode: Unique spatial barcode associated with each capture spot.
  • in_tissue: Binary flag (1 = in tissue, 0 = background) indicating whether the spot falls within the tissue boundary.
  • array_row, array_col: Integer indices representing the position of the spot on the capture array grid.
  • pxl_row_in_fullres, pxl_col_in_fullres: Floating point coordinates locating the spot in full-resolution tissue image pixels.
scalefactors_json.json – pixel-to-micrometer scaling factors 
{
    "spot_diameter_fullres": 7.303953797779634,
    "bin_size_um": 2.0,
    "microns_per_pixel": 0.2738242950835738,
    "regist_target_img_scalef": 0.2505533,
    "tissue_lowres_scalef": 0.02505533,
    "fiducial_diameter_fullres": 1205.1523766336395,
    "tissue_hires_scalef": 0.2505533
}
  • spot_diameter_fullres: Estimated diameter of a barcoded spot in full-resolution pixels.
  • bin_size_um: Physical size (in micrometers) of the smallest bin, typically 2.0 µm for Visium HD.
  • microns_per_pixel: Resolution of the full-res image, used to convert pixel distances to micrometers.
  • regist_target_img_scalef: Scaling factor applied during image registration to the target image.
  • tissue_lowres_scalef: Downscaling factor from full-res to low-resolution tissue image.
  • fiducial_diameter_fullres: Diameter of fiducial markers in full-resolution pixels, useful for alignment.
  • tissue_hires_scalef: Downscaling factor from full-res to high-resolution tissue image.

docs.title: Define ID and Parameters
docs.text:
# Unique identifier for your dataset
DATA_ID="visiumhd_hippo"                 # change this to reflect your dataset name
PLATFORM="10x_visium_hd"                 # platform information

# LDA parameters
train_width=18                           # define LDA training hexagon width (comma-separated if multiple widths are applied)
n_factor=6,12                            # define number of factors in LDA training (comma-separated if multiple n-factor values are provided)

How to define Scaling Factors for Visium HD?

10x Visium HD includes a scalefactors_json.json file that provides pixel-to-micrometer scaling information. CartLoader can directly accept this file via the --scale-json option and automatically compute the appropriate scaling factor, so you do not need to manually calculate and specify --units-per-um.

Alternatively, users may bypass the JSON file by directly providing a value through the --units-per-um option.

docs.title: SGE Format Conversion
docs.text:
Convert the raw input to the unified SGE format. See more details in its Reference page.

cartloader sge_convert \
  --makefn sge_convert.mk \
  --platform ${PLATFORM} \
  --in-mex ./raw \
  --pos-parquet ./raw/tissue_positions.parquet \
  --scale-json ./raw/scalefactors_json.json \
  --out-dir ./sge \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(BLANK|NegCon|NegPrb)' \
  --sge-visual \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --platform required string Input platform (options: 10x_visium_hd, seqscope, illumina, 10x_xenium, bgi_stereoseq, cosmx_smi, vizgen_merscope, pixel_seq, nova_st, generic) --in-mex required string Input MEX directory holding barcodes.tsv.gz, features.tsv.gz, and matrix.mtx.gz --pos-parquet required string Path to tissue_positions.parquet, which gives each barcode's position --scale-json required 1 string Path to scalefactors_json.json, used to convert pixel positions to µm --out-dir required string Output directory for the converted SGE files --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: sge_convert.mk) --exclude-feature-regex regex Pattern of feature names to drop (e.g. control probes) --sge-visual flag Draw the converted SGE as an image (xy.png) for a visual check --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1)

1: CartLoader needs the scale either from a JSON file (--scale-json, which must contain microns_per_pixel) or as a number (--units-per-um, pixels per µm).

docs.title: FICTURE Analysis
docs.text:
Compute spatial factors using punkst (FICTURE2). See more details on the Reference page. For Visium HD, --decode-scale 2 draws the factor image at 2 µm per pixel, the bin size.

cartloader run_ficture2 \
  --makefn run_ficture2.mk \
  --main \
  --in-transcript ./sge/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz \
  --in-feature ./sge/feature.clean.tsv.gz \
  --in-minmax ./sge/coordinate_minmax.tsv \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(mt-.*$|Gm\d+$)' \
  --decode-scale 2 \
  --out-dir ./ficture2 \
  --width ${train_width} \
  --n-factor ${n_factor} \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs} \
  --threads ${n_jobs}

docs.title: 10x Xenium Starter Tutorial
docs.text:
This tutorial uses SGE data generated with the 10x Genomics Xenium platform, and it has been cropped to a small region of the adult mouse brain for demonstration purposes.

It first runs the whole analysis with a single run_together command, then walks through the same analysis step by step: input preparation, SGE format conversion, FICTURE analysis, asset packaging, and data upload.

docs.title: Run with run_together
docs.text:
Download the example data, hosted on Zenodo (10.5281/zenodo.17953582), into a work directory:

work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # replace with your work directory
mkdir -p ${work_dir} && cd ${work_dir}
wget https://zenodo.org/records/17953582/files/xenium_starter.raw.tar.gz
tar --strip-components=1 -zxvf xenium_starter.raw.tar.gz   # extracts input.tsv.gz

The 10x Xenium profile carries the cell_id, z_location, overlaps_nucleus, and nucleus_distance columns through ingest. This starter file predates nucleus_distance, so write a small config file that leaves it out:

cat > xenium_starter.json <<'EOF'
{ "ingest": { "csv_colnames_others": ["cell_id", "z_location", "overlaps_nucleus"] } }
EOF

Then run the pipeline, either with a local installation or with the Docker image:

LocallyDocker 
cartloader run_together \
  --platform 10x_xenium \
  --raw-transcript ./input.tsv.gz \
  --config xenium_starter.json \
  --out-dir ./out/xenium_hippo \
  --id xenium_hippo \
  --width 12 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

docker run --rm -v ${work_dir}:/data hyunminkang/cartloader:latest \
  run_together \
  --platform 10x_xenium \
  --raw-transcript /data/input.tsv.gz \
  --config /data/xenium_starter.json \
  --out-dir /data/out/xenium_hippo \
  --id xenium_hippo \
  --width 12 \
  --n-factor 6,12 \
  --threads 4 -j 4

--raw-transcript names the transcript file directly, since the starter data is a single file rather than a Xenium Ranger output directory (--in-dir). The result to deploy is out/xenium_hippo/cartl/xenium_hippo/ (a catalog.yaml and the PMTiles it lists). Add --dry-run to print the commands without running them.

How run_together differs from the step-by-step path

  • FICTURE runs through run_ficture2_multi (a joint model over a single sample) with single-molecule pixel decoding, instead of run_ficture2.
  • Feature filters are the run_together defaults: control features (Unassigned, Neg, BLANK/Blank, Intergenic, Deprecated, System, NCS-, NCP-) are dropped at ingest; predicted (Gm<digit>), mitochondrial (mt-/MT-), and ribosomal (Rps/Rpl) genes stay in the data but are left out of the factor models. Change them with --ingest-exclude-feature-regex and --exclude-feature-regex.
  • Point layers are packaged with pmpoint (--use-pmpoint, 500 gene bins) instead of tippecanoe.
  • Outputs go under --out-dir: tsv/<id>/ (converted SGE), fic/ (FICTURE), and cartl/<id>/ (PMTiles and catalog.yaml; deploy this), instead of sge/, ficture2/, and cartload2/.
  • Publishing is built in: --s3-upload uploads cartl/<id>/ to S3 (see Publishing). For Zenodo, run upload_zenodo on cartl/<id>/ as in the step-by-step path.

docs.title: Step by Step (Individual Commands)
docs.text: The same analysis, one command at a time. Use it to understand each stage or to customize it.

docs.title: Set Up the Environment
docs.text:
# ====
# Replace the placeholders with values for your system.
# ====
work_dir=/path/to/work/directory        # directory holding the input data; outputs are written here too
cd $work_dir

n_jobs=10                               # number of parallel jobs (also used as threads per job below)

# Activate the Python environment in which CartLoader is installed
conda activate ENV_NAME                 # replace ENV_NAME (or: source /path/to/venv/bin/activate)

No tool paths needed

Once submodules/build.sh has run (see Installation), every CartLoader command finds spatula, punkst, tippecanoe, pmtiles, and pmpoint in the submodules/ directory of the repository, and the default color map at assets/default_color_map.tsv. Pass --spatula, --ficture2 (the punkst repository directory, which contains bin/punkst), --tippecanoe, --pmtiles, or --cmap-file only to use a different build or file. upload_aws runs the aws CLI from your PATH (--aws to override).

docs.title: Input Data
docs.text:
Use the data downloaded above.

The 10x Genomics Xenium platform outputs Spatial Gene Expression (SGE) data in a comma‑separated values (CSV) format.

CSV File Format

"transcript_id","cell_id","overlaps_nucleus","feature_name","x_location","y_location","z_location","qv"
281827164036151,133793,1,"Sox10",2350.0232,4153.6846,16.592316,40.0
281827164036152,133793,1,"Sox10",2350.2585,4154.5225,17.237207,10.514394
281827164036164,151216,0,"Sox10",2350.5874,4277.699,14.285685,40.0
  • "transcript_id": Unique identifier for each detected transcript molecule.
  • "cell_id": ID of the segmented cell associated with the transcript.
  • "overlaps_nucleus": 1 if the transcript overlaps the nucleus mask, 0 otherwise.
  • "feature_name": Feature name corresponding to the transcript (typically a gene).
  • "x_location": X coordinate of the transcript.
  • "y_location": Y coordinate of the transcript.
  • "z_location": Z coordinate (depth) of the transcript.
  • "qv": Quality value indicating confidence in transcript detection.

In the starter data this file is input.tsv.gz (comma-separated despite its name). It has no nucleus_distance column, which newer Xenium Ranger versions add.

docs.title: Define ID and Parameters
docs.text:
# Unique identifier for your dataset
DATA_ID="xenium_hippo"                  # change this to reflect your dataset name
PLATFORM="10x_xenium"                   # platform information
SCALE=1                                 # coordinate units per micrometer

# LDA parameters
train_width=12                           # define LDA training hexagon width (comma-separated if multiple widths are applied)
n_factor=6,12                            # define number of factors in LDA training (comma-separated if multiple n-factor values are provided)

How to define Scaling Factors for Xenium?

The Xenium example data currently used here provides SGE in micrometer units. Define the scaling factor from coordinate units to micrometers as 1.

docs.title: SGE Format Conversion
docs.text:
Convert the raw input to the unified SGE format. See more details in its Reference page.

cartloader sge_convert \
  --makefn sge_convert.mk \
  --platform ${PLATFORM} \
  --in-csv ./input.tsv.gz \
  --units-per-um ${SCALE} \
  --out-dir ./sge \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(BLANK|Neg|Intergenic|Deprecated|Unassigned)' \
  --sge-visual \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --platform required string Input platform, which sets the default input columns and delimiter (options: 10x_visium_hd, seqscope, illumina, 10x_xenium, bgi_stereoseq, cosmx_smi, vizgen_merscope, pixel_seq, nova_st, generic) --in-csv required string Path to the input transcript CSV/TSV file --out-dir required string Output directory for the converted SGE files --units-per-um float Coordinate units per µm in the input (default: 1, i.e. already in µm; 1000 for the Seq-Scope raw TSV; detected from the barcodes for illumina) --csv-colname-feature-name string Gene-name column in the input (default: set by --platform) --csv-colname-count string Count column in the input (default: set by --platform; without one, each row counts 1) --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: sge_convert.mk) --exclude-feature-regex regex Pattern of feature names to drop (e.g. control probes) --sge-visual flag Draw the converted SGE as an image (xy.png) for a visual check --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1)

docs.title: FICTURE Analysis
docs.text:
Compute spatial factors using punkst (FICTURE2). See more details on the Reference page.

cartloader run_ficture2 \
  --makefn run_ficture2.mk \
  --main \
  --in-transcript ./sge/transcripts.unsorted.tsv.gz \
  --in-feature ./sge/feature.clean.tsv.gz \
  --in-minmax ./sge/coordinate_minmax.tsv \
  --exclude-feature-regex '^(mt-.*$|Gm\d+$)' \
  --out-dir ./ficture2 \
  --width ${train_width} \
  --n-factor ${n_factor} \
  --n-jobs ${n_jobs} \
  --threads ${n_jobs}
Parameter Required Type Description --main required 1 flag Run all five main steps --in-transcript required string Path to the transcript-indexed SGE file from sge_convert --out-dir required string Output directory --width required int or comma-separated list Hexagon width(s) in µm for LDA training --n-factor required int or comma-separated list Number(s) of LDA factors; one model per width × factor combination --makefn string File name for the generated Makefile (default: run_ficture2.mk) --in-feature string Path to the per-gene count file from sge_convert (default: the feature list made during tiling) --in-minmax string Path to the coordinate min/max file from sge_convert (default: the range computed during tiling) --exclude-feature-regex regex Feature names to leave out of the factor analysis. punkst matches the whole name, so end each alternative with .* or $ as needed (the example drops mitochondrial mt-* and predicted Gm<digits> genes) --cmap-file string Color map TSV (default: assets/default_color_map.tsv in the CartLoader repository) --n-jobs int Number of parallel jobs (default: 1) --threads int Number of threads per job (default: 4)

1: CartLoader requires at least one action: --tile (tiling), --segment (hexagon segmentation), --init-lda (LDA training), --decode (pixel-level decoding), --umap (UMAP of the factors), or --main for all five.
